title: Pin today's token and session authentication for shipped clients
body:
Tests only: no behavior change, no migrations.

These pin how shipped clients authenticate today — the CLI and scripts holding a personal access token, and the native apps sending the `session_token` cookie — so the pending OAuth stack (#2296 → … → #3169) has to keep them green when it rebases onto this, or change one deliberately and say so.

## Pins

`test/controllers/shipped_client_authentication_test.rb` (OSS and SaaS):

| Pin | Guards |
|---|---|
| A PAT sent as Bearer on JSON reaches every account its identity has a user in (37s, initech, and `/my/identity.json` lists both) | [`Authentication#authenticate_by_bearer_token`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/48f58c2ffedd6d261cf4f8a1d22955fc253969d3/app/controllers/concerns/authentication.rb#L58-L70): `Current.identity = identity` — the token resolves to an Identity, not a User |
| A PAT is 403 in an account its identity has no user in | [`Authorization#ensure_can_access_account`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/48f58c2ffedd6d261cf4f8a1d22955fc253969d3/app/controllers/concerns/authorization.rb) |
| A read PAT may GET/HEAD, gets 401 on POST/PATCH/DELETE; a write PAT may POST | [`Identity::AccessToken#allows?`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/48f58c2ffedd6d261cf4f8a1d22955fc253969d3/app/models/identity/access_token.rb#L7-L9): `method.in?(%w[ GET HEAD ]) \|\| write?` |
| A PAT never expires (10-year-old token, 10 years on, still 200) | [`Identity.find_by_permissable_access_token`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/48f58c2ffedd6d261cf4f8a1d22955fc253969d3/app/models/identity.rb#L19-L21): `AccessToken.find_by(token: token)` |
| Bearer on a non-JSON (HTML) request is 401, not authenticated | [`Authentication#bearer_token_authenticatable_request?`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/48f58c2ffedd6d261cf4f8a1d22955fc253969d3/app/controllers/concerns/authentication.rb#L72-L74): `request.format.json?` |
| The `session_token` from JSON magic-link sign-in, sent back as a raw `Cookie` header (as [fizzy-android's FizzySdk.kt](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy-android/blob/main/library/sdk/src/main/kotlin/com/basecamp/fizzy/library/sdk/generated/FizzySdk.kt#L50) does), authenticates JSON requests: 200 | [`Authentication#resume_session`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/48f58c2ffedd6d261cf4f8a1d22955fc253969d3/app/controllers/concerns/authentication.rb#L48-L56) |
| A JSON request with no or a bad session cookie is 302 to `/session/new`, not 401 | [`Authentication#request_authentication`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/48f58c2ffedd6d261cf4f8a1d22955fc253969d3/app/controllers/concerns/authentication.rb#L76-L82) → `redirect_to_login_url` |

`saas/test/controllers/admin/audits_controller_test.rb` (SaaS), alongside the existing auditor-token tests:

| Pin | Guards |
|---|---|
| An auditor bearer token is 401 on ordinary JSON endpoints (`/boards.json`, `/my/identity.json`) | [`Admin::AuditsController#require_authentication`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/48f58c2ffedd6d261cf4f8a1d22955fc253969d3/saas/app/controllers/admin/audits_controller.rb#L3-L13) is the only caller of `auditor_from_bearer_token` |
| A PAT is 401 on the audits console | same, falling through to `super` and the JSON-only bearer path |

## Mutation checks

Each guard was broken locally, the pin watched fail, then reverted: per-account tokens, skipping `ensure_can_access_account`, `allows?` → `true`, `allows?` → reads only, a one-year `created_at` window on token lookup, `bearer_token_authenticatable_request?` → `true`, skipping `resume_session` on JSON, and 401 instead of redirect for unauthenticated JSON. Every one failed only the pin it targets (the per-account mutation also trips the 403 pin, which turns 401). Each pin above failed only under the mutation aimed at it (the per-account mutation also turns the 403 pin into a 401). The `ensure_can_access_account` mutation shows up as an error rather than an assertion failure, since the action then renders without a user.

SaaS auditor pins, under SaaS mode: letting `Identity.find_by_permissable_access_token` also accept an auditor token fails the "outside the console" pin. Letting `Admin::AuditsController` also accept a PAT fails the "PAT on the console" pin. Dropping the auditor path from `Admin::AuditsController#require_authentication` fails the existing "valid bearer token is allowed" tests, which already pin that the console keeps working.

## CI

Full `bin/ci` in SaaS mode passed on 48f58c2: SaaS 1925 runs, OSS 1755 runs, and both system suites, all with 0 failures. GitHub Actions is green in both OSS and SaaS, on SQLite and MySQL.

title: Store tokens and client secrets as digests (D1 of 3: read by digest, plaintext fallback)
body:
> **Reviewing note (2026-10-24):** `main` was merged into this branch (`da3f593f6`, then Ruby 4 test fixes `52d49bc5a` and two redaction commits `0fb6c23a0`, `0cfe38111`), so until the PRs below it land, the diff against `oauth-delegate-resources` also shows `main`'s changes. To review this PR's own work, read the first-parent commits after `6fd18cd05` (`git log --first-parent 6fd18cd05..oauth-token-digests`).

> [!WARNING]
> **This PR contains migrations. Don't merge it directly.** It has to go through the beta integration branch ([`oauth-integration-2026-10-15`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/oauth-integration-2026-10-15/docs/oauth/integration-migrations.md)) and be **migrated by hand on beta before it lands**. beta1 runs against `fizzy_production` (`saas/config/database.yml` ends `beta: *production`), so migrating on beta1 *is* migrating production. The rows to add to that branch's migration inventory are [below](#migration-inventory-rows-for-the-integration-branch); this PR doesn't push to the integration branch.
>
> **Before beta boots this code, `OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER` must exist** in 1Password (account `23QPQDKZC5BKBIIG7UGT5GR5RM`, vault **Deploy**, item **Fizzy**) as two fields: `Production/OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER` (beta's secrets read this one too) and `Staging/OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER`. A SaaS deploy without it fails `kamal secrets fetch`, and the app refuses to boot. See [Deploy prerequisites](#deploy-prerequisites).

Stacked on #3169 (train: #2296 → #3080 → #3081 → #3082 → #3160 → #3161 → #3159 → #3163 → #3169 → this).

Implements **step D1** of hashing tokens at rest. The plan has three deploys, so no token stops working at any point:

| Step | What it does | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **D1** (this PR) | Add digest columns with unique indexes, then backfill. Read by digest, falling back to plaintext for personal access tokens and digesting them as it finds them. Personal access tokens are still written in plaintext too, for production `main`. OAuth credentials are digest-only. | this PR |
| D2 | Rerun the backfill. Stop writing plaintext and stop the fallback. Add `token` to `ignored_columns`. | after D1 is deployed to production |
| D3 | Drop `identity_access_tokens.token`. | after D2 is deployed everywhere |

## What D1 does

### `TokenDigester` ([`app/models/token_digester.rb`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/09523ade5f33a3a6e2f933b061fbb18822d98524/app/models/token_digester.rb))

- Stores `OpenSSL::HMAC.hexdigest("SHA256", pepper, raw)`: lowercase hex, byte-for-byte what [bc3's `Oauth::TokenDigester#digest`](https://github.com/basecamp/bc3/blob/master/app/models/oauth/token_digester.rb) computes. A test pins it to the published HMAC-SHA256 vector.
- **Version prefix for rotating the pepper later.** A digest can be stored as `"<n>$<hex>"`, and a bare digest is version 1. Lookups go through `TokenDigester.digests(raw)`, one digest per pepper version in service, so a future v2 can be added without a flag day. Only v1 exists today.
- **Pepper:**
  - SaaS reads `OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER`, named to mirror bc3's `credentials.oauth.token_pepper` (personal access tokens are digested under it too; in Fizzy they're OAuth grants of a first-party client after #3205). Fizzy keeps no encrypted credentials file, so every SaaS secret, `SECRET_KEY_BASE` included, comes from the environment through `.kamal/secrets`; reading credentials first would add a second source for one value, and self-hosted installs need the variable either way. Outside development and test it's required, and must be at least 32 characters. The [initializer](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/09523ade5f33a3a6e2f933b061fbb18822d98524/config/initializers/token_digester.rb) checks at boot, so a deploy missing it fails before it serves anything. There's no fallback to a derived key, which would digest with a different key than every stored token, as bc3's [`verify_pepper!`](https://github.com/basecamp/bc3/blob/master/config/initializers/oauth_token_pepper.rb) also refuses to. Asset precompilation (`SECRET_KEY_BASE_DUMMY`) skips the check.
  - OSS uses `OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER` when it's set. Otherwise it uses `Rails.application.key_generator.generate_key("token_digest_pepper", 32)`, a key derived from `SECRET_KEY_BASE`. [`docs/docker-deployment.md`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/09523ade5f33a3a6e2f933b061fbb18822d98524/docs/docker-deployment.md#secret-key-base) now says so: on a self-hosted install, **rotating `SECRET_KEY_BASE` invalidates every personal access token and connected app** unless `OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER` is set separately.

### `identity_access_tokens`

- **Schema.** New columns `token_digest` and `refresh_token_digest` (`string`, limit 80), each with a **unique index**. The indexes are created in the schema migration, before any digest is written, so a duplicate fails loudly and no lookup ever scans the table. Before this, `token` had no index, and every Bearer request scanned all ~3,500 rows.
- **Backfill** ([`BackfillTokenDigests`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/09523ade5f33a3a6e2f933b061fbb18822d98524/db/migrate/20261015120100_backfill_token_digests.rb)).
  - It runs in Ruby, because MySQL and SQLite have no HMAC: batches of 500, with `disable_ddl_transaction!`.
  - Each row is written with `update_all`, so `updated_at`, the grant idle clock from #3161, doesn't move.
  - **Duplicate plaintext tokens are refused before anything is written.** The error names the row ids and never the tokens.
  - It's rerunnable: it touches only rows without a digest, skips columns that are already gone, and its `down` does nothing. `db:migrate:redo:primary VERSION=20261015120100` runs it again.
- **Writes.**
  - Personal access tokens get both `token` and `token_digest`, because production `main` still reads `token` while beta runs this.
  - OAuth access tokens get the digest only, and `token` stays NULL.
  - A refresh writes new digests and clears any plaintext.
  - Raw values exist only in memory, as virtual attributes (`raw_token`, `raw_refresh_token`), on the record that issued or rotated them.
- **Reads.** [`find_by_raw_token`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/09523ade5f33a3a6e2f933b061fbb18822d98524/app/models/identity/access_token.rb) looks up the digest first. If that misses, it falls back to `personal.where(token_digest: nil).find_by(token: raw)` and heals the row it finds: the digest goes to the **primary**, even when the lookup ran on the replica as GET requests do, via `update_columns`, so `updated_at` doesn't move.
  - Review caught the replica case. A test that runs the lookup under `with_reading_role` failed on MySQL with `ActiveRecord::ReadOnlyError` before the fix.
  - Prefixed tokens fall back too: #3163 issues `fizzy_pat_` tokens without digests on beta today. A plaintext match is confirmed byte for byte, since MySQL compares `token` case-insensitively, so a differently cased token neither authenticates nor installs a wrong digest.
  - The fallback stays inside the caller's scope, so `oauth.find_by_raw_token` never matches a personal token.

### OAuth-only plaintext columns: replaced now

These have never held production data, since the OAuth tables and columns have never served production traffic, and OAuth has never shipped on `main`, so no self-hosted install has them either. So they're replaced in this step rather than kept for two more deploys. **That holds only while this PR ships in the same release as the rest of the OAuth stack (#2296 onward).**

- `identity_access_tokens.refresh_token` → `refresh_token_digest`. The plaintext column itself stays until #3203 (D3) drops it beside `token`: `Identity::AccessToken` ignores it, and the backfill empties it. Production `main` caches that table's columns and names every one on INSERT, so dropping it under `main` would fail its personal access token inserts until a restart (see the runbook notes).
- `oauth_retired_refresh_tokens` is rebuilt keyed by digest: `refresh_token_digest`, `successor_refresh_token_digest`, and an encrypted `successor_payload`. Retired tokens exist only to recognize a replay, so they're dropped rather than converted. A replay of a token rotated before the migration is answered as an unknown token.
- `oauth_clients.client_secret` → `client_secret_digest`.

**Refresh replay grace with digests** ([`Oauth::RetiredRefreshToken`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/09523ade5f33a3a6e2f933b061fbb18822d98524/app/models/oauth/retired_refresh_token.rb)). A retry within 60s used to answer from the grant's plaintext tokens. Now each rotation stores its successor pair in the retired row, the way [bc3's `rotate_to!`](https://github.com/basecamp/bc3/blob/master/app/models/oauth/refresh_token/rotation.rb) stores `successor_raw_token`:

- The pair is encrypted with a `MessageEncryptor` key derived from `secret_key_base` (salt `oauth_refresh_token_successor`, as in bc3).
- It's sealed with `expires_in: GRACE`, so it can't be decrypted after the window even if nothing blanks it.
- It's blanked by `Oauth::RetiredRefreshToken.forget_successors` every 5 minutes (`config/recurring.yml`). The sweep looks back one day, so it stays an index range over recent rows rather than a scan of 90 days of retired tokens.
- `superseded?` compares `refresh_token_digest` with `successor_refresh_token_digest`.
- A retry whose pair is gone (blanked or undecryptable) inside the window is refused with `invalid_grant` "Refresh token no longer retryable", without revoking. That matches bc3's "Grace window token not available".

**Client secrets.**
- The raw secret is returned only in the DCR creation response, as before, and it's now held only in memory (`raw_client_secret`).
- It's verified by `TokenDigester.verify`, a constant-time compare of HMACs.
- **This deviates from bc3**, which uses bcrypt (`has_secure_password :secret`). Fizzy only issues generated secrets, 257 bits of randomness since #3163 (about 140 before it), so a deliberately slow hash adds no guessing resistance that the entropy doesn't already give, and one keyed digest covers every credential. The deviation is recorded in [`docs/oauth/spec_conformance.md`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/09523ade5f33a3a6e2f933b061fbb18822d98524/docs/oauth/spec_conformance.md#rfc-6749-231-client-authentication). That doc's "Secrets stored in plaintext … **Deliberate**" line is now **Fixed**, and a Token format row records the digests.

### Personal access token: shown once

Creating a token used to redirect to `/my/access_tokens/<signed id>`, which showed the raw token to anyone who loaded it within 10 seconds. Now:

- The token appears only in the create response itself: a `turbo_stream` that replaces the form, or an HTML 201 without Turbo.
- That response, and the JSON one fizzy-cli uses, carries `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- The `show` route and action are gone.
- The JSON response shape is unchanged (`id`, `token`, `description`, `permission`, `created_at`).

**Issuer without a trailing slash** ([`Oauth::BaseController#oauth_issuer`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/09523ade5f33a3a6e2f933b061fbb18822d98524/app/controllers/oauth/base_controller.rb)). The metadata `issuer`, the `iss` authorization response parameter, the Basic challenge's realm and the protected resource's `authorization_servers` were `root_url`, `https://app.fizzy.do/`. Clients compare issuers as exact strings (RFC 8414 §3.3), bc3's `canonical_issuer_url` is the bare origin, and fizzy-mcp-server trims the slash from the issuer it's configured with, so its startup check would have refused this metadata. They're now `https://app.fizzy.do`, still from the one method; the protected resource's own `resource` identifier is unchanged. A test checks `authorization_servers` is exactly the advertised issuer.

## Deploy prerequisites

1. **Create `OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER`** before anything running this code boots on beta, staging or production. Use at least 32 characters, e.g. `bin/rails secret`.
   - **`Production/OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER`** (the Production section of the Fizzy item in the Deploy vault): read by production and by every beta (`saas/.kamal/secrets.beta`, which `secrets.beta1`–`4` link to, fetches `Production/OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER`). **Beta and production must share it**, because beta writes digests into production's database. Reading the one field from both, rather than copying it into the Beta section, makes sharing structural. Beta deployers already read this vault.
   - **`Staging/OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER`**: staging has its own database, so it gets its own pepper.
   - It **must never change** afterwards. Rotating it means adding a v2 pepper (see `TokenDigester`), not editing this one.
2. Without it, `kamal secrets fetch` fails for that destination, and a container started without it refuses to boot (`TokenDigester::MissingPepper`).
3. `SECRET_KEY_BASE` differs between beta and production (the Beta and Production sections). It only keys the 60-second successor payload, so a retry answered by the other deployment would get "no longer retryable" rather than revocation. They're different hosts, so in practice this never happens.

## Migration inventory rows for the integration branch

For [`docs/oauth/integration-migrations.md`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/oauth-integration-2026-10-15/docs/oauth/integration-migrations.md) on `oauth-integration-2026-10-15`. This PR doesn't change that branch. These rows extend its table, and its `migrate:up`/`down` lists, after #7:

| # | Version / file | PR | What it does | Production table | MySQL 8.4 DDL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | `20261015120000_add_token_digests.rb` | this | `change_table :identity_access_tokens, bulk: true`: `token_digest`, `refresh_token_digest` (string 80), a unique index on each. `add_column :oauth_clients, :client_secret_digest` (string 80) | `identity_access_tokens`: ~3,500 rows | One ALTER, INPLACE LOCK=NONE. Every row starts NULL, so neither unique index can fail |
| 9 | `20261015120100_backfill_token_digests.rb` | this | **Data only, no DDL.** Refuses duplicate `token`s first. Then one `UPDATE … WHERE id = ?` per row: `token_digest` for every token (OAuth rows also get `token` NULLed), `refresh_token_digest` (and `refresh_token` NULLed) and `client_secret_digest` where those columns still exist. `updated_at` doesn't move. `disable_ddl_transaction!`, batches of 500. `down` is a no-op | `identity_access_tokens` | Row locks only, ~3,500 single-row updates on the primary key, a few seconds |
| 10 | `20261015120200_drop_plaintext_oauth_credentials.rb` | this | Drop `oauth_clients.client_secret`. Drop and recreate `oauth_retired_refresh_tokens` keyed by digest, with `successor_payload` text. Leaves `identity_access_tokens` alone | the empty `oauth_*` tables only, which `main` doesn't model | DROP COLUMN is INSTANT. The `oauth_*` tables are empty in production |

Notes for the runbook:

- **Undo** by version, newest first: `20261015120200`, `20261015120100` (no-op), `20261015120000`. Undoing #10 restores an empty `client_secret` column and an empty retired-token table, not the old values. Undoing #8 drops the digests, and the personal access tokens still hold their plaintext.
- **No migration here drops a column of a table `main` uses, so production needs no restart.** Production `main` runs with `partial_inserts` off (`load_defaults 8.1`) and no schema cache dump, so a process names every column it has cached on INSERT. Dropping `identity_access_tokens.refresh_token` in #10, as this PR first did, failed personal access token inserts from any `main` process that cached the table between #3 and #10, until it restarted (reproduced on thelio). That column now goes in D3. [`test/migrations/drop_plaintext_oauth_credentials_test.rb`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/617edb87b/test/migrations/drop_plaintext_oauth_credentials_test.rb) caches the table's columns the way `main` does, runs #10 and creates a token with them; against the old #10 it fails with `Unknown column 'refresh_token'`.
- **Run #8 to #10 in the same session as #1 to #7.**
- **Prefixed personal access tokens.** A `fizzy_pat_` token written without a digest is never found. Only pre-D1 stack code writes those: the integration branch without this PR, deployed to beta. So **merge this PR into the integration branch before its migrations run on beta1**. If anything else wrote such tokens after the backfill, rerun it with `bin/rails db:migrate:redo:primary VERSION=20261015120100`.
- Production `main` keeps writing personal access tokens without digests until D1 reaches production. Each is digested the first time it's used, from beta or, after D1 lands, from production. D2 starts by rerunning the backfill for any never used.
- Beta's `recurring.yml` runs only Solid Queue maintenance, so `forget_successors` doesn't run from beta. OAuth is dark there, and the payload expires cryptographically anyway.

Verified on thelio against a dedicated MySQL 8.4 container (SaaS):

- Loaded #3169's schema and created a personal access token, an OAuth grant and a confidential client with the parent's code. Then migrated with this branch.
- Every value was digested and verified. The personal access token kept its plaintext, the grant's plaintext was cleared, and both `updated_at`s were unchanged.
- Then down newest-first and up again, then `redo` of the backfill. Each dump differs from the committed `db/schema.rb` (or, after down, from #3169's) in column order only, physical rather than sorted, the same as the integration doc found for #1–#7.

## Tests

New:

- [`test/models/token_digester_test.rb`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/09523ade5f33a3a6e2f933b061fbb18822d98524/test/models/token_digester_test.rb):
  - bc3 byte-compatibility against the HMAC-SHA256 vector.
  - Version prefix and multi-version lookup.
  - `verify` refuses an unknown version, a malformed prefix, blanks, nil and non-strings.
  - The pepper is read from `OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER` (the name the deploy configs and docs give; any other would quietly fall back to the derived key).
  - The pepper is required in SaaS beta, staging and production, and not in development, test or OSS. A short pepper is refused. The derived fallback is the key generator's.
- [`test/models/identity/access_token_test.rb`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/09523ade5f33a3a6e2f933b061fbb18822d98524/test/models/identity/access_token_test.rb):
  - Personal tokens are stored digested plus plaintext. Grants and rotations store digests only.
  - Lookup is by digest, and an ordinary lookup issues no plaintext query.
  - **Fallback and heal:** an undigested personal token authenticates, gets its digest, keeps its `updated_at`, and the next lookup is digest-only.
  - The heal works from the replica.
  - Prefixed tokens skip the fallback, OAuth rows never fall back, and the fallback stays in scope.
  - **Uniqueness** of `token_digest` and `refresh_token_digest`.
- [`test/migrations/backfill_token_digests_test.rb`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/09523ade5f33a3a6e2f933b061fbb18822d98524/test/migrations/backfill_token_digests_test.rb):
  - Personal tokens keep their plaintext, and grants' plaintext is cleared.
  - **`updated_at` is untouched.**
  - It's idempotent.
  - The backfilled token authenticates.
  - **Duplicates are refused before any write**, naming ids, not tokens.
- [`test/models/oauth/retired_refresh_token_test.rb`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/09523ade5f33a3a6e2f933b061fbb18822d98524/test/models/oauth/retired_refresh_token_test.rb):
  - The retired row holds digests, and the successor pair only encrypted: no raw token appears in the payload.
  - The pair is readable at 59s and unreadable at 61s.
  - `forget_successors` blanks only past the window.
  - `superseded?` compares by digest.
  - A tampered payload reads as none.
- `OauthRefreshReplayTest`: **a retry inside the window whose pair is gone is refused without revoking.** The existing #3160 tests (same pair at 59s, revoke at exactly 60s, superseded, lost race, and so on) pass unchanged in substance.
- `OauthFlowTest`: **a DCR-registered secret is stored only as its digest and authenticates with Basic.** `Oauth::ClientTest` checks the digest on create and none for public clients.
- `My::AccessTokensControllerTest`:
  - **Reveal once:** the HTML and turbo stream create responses carry the token and `no-store`.
  - The old show URL is 404, and the index doesn't contain the token.
  - JSON create carries `no-store`, and its token matches the stored digest.
- Fixtures compute digests in ERB (`TokenDigester.digest(...)`).

Existing tests now use `raw_token` and `raw_refresh_token` for values held in memory, and compare digests where they used to reread plaintext. An `assert_not exists?(token: …)` would now pass vacuously, so each became `exists?(token_digest: TokenDigester.digest(…))`.

**#3191 pins.** Merged `test/pin-shipped-client-auth` into this branch locally (not pushed) and ran `ShippedClientAuthenticationTest` and the SaaS `Admin::AuditsControllerTest`: all pass, in OSS (8 tests) and SaaS (17 tests, auditor pins included). (The two pins the integration doc lists as failing are against #3158, which isn't below this PR.)

Suites (thelio, gated on exit status):

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| SaaS (MySQL 8.4) | 2210 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors |
| OSS (SQLite) | 2043 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors |
| OSS (MySQL 8.4, `DATABASE_ADAPTER=mysql`) | 2043 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors |

These ran at `239292edd`. The head adds only the PR number to the conformance doc. System tests weren't run locally; CI runs them.

RuboCop, Brakeman and gitleaks are clean.

## Not done here, on purpose

- **Client secrets have no `fizzy_cs_` prefix yet.** That's out of scope and still the follow-up #3163 names.
- **No data in the plaintext OAuth columns is carried over** beyond the backfill: they have none in production.
- **Personal access token plaintext stays until D3.** Production `main` reads only `token` until D1 is deployed there.
- **No new third party or personal-data flow.** The pepper is a server-side secret in our existing 1Password vault.

title: Keep sign-in codes, API tokens and join codes out of logged SQL
body:
Card step 12 on [Ops card 10373658070](https://app.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/27/card_tables/cards/10373658070): SQL-log filtering for Fizzy.

## The problem

Trilogy runs without prepared statements, so every value reaches the SQL text as a quoted literal. `Rails.event.debug_mode = true` ([config/application.rb](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/27d0d2e6be80623d492b723126f16ef3018d6981/config/application.rb#L24-L28)) sends each statement to the log at debug level. In SaaS mode, rails_structured_logging's recorder attaches to `Rails.logger` at debug level, so those lines go into the `original` field of every request's and job's structured line, and from there into Loki. Today that includes:

- **Magic-link sign-in codes:** the `Exists?`/`Pluck` uniqueness check and the `INSERT INTO magic_links` when one is sent, and the `SELECT` when one is redeemed.
- **API access tokens:** the `identity_access_tokens` lookup on every bearer-authenticated request, and the insert when one is created.
- **Account join codes:** the lookup, the insert, and the `UPDATE` on reset.

Sentry breadcrumbs carry the same SQL, read straight from the `sql.active_record` notification. A database error on one of these statements can quote the value in its message, which reaches the structured line's `error` field and Sentry.

Two other paths logged the same magic-link code into the same structured lines:

- **The request parameter.** `code` wasn't in `filter_parameters`, so `Parameters: {"code" => "…"}` showed up on `Sessions::MagicLinksController#create`.
- **The mail itself.** Debug mode logs every delivered mail's encoded source, including the subject "Your Fizzy code is …" and the body, in the `ActionMailer::MailDeliveryJob` line.

## The change

Adapted from HEY's `ActiveRecordSqlRedaction` (basecamp/haystack#8950, #8953, #8955). The SQL sent to the database never changes. Only what is logged, reported or raised about it does.

- **Which statements:** any statement that names a redacted table, in any case: `` `t` `` on MySQL, `"t"` on SQLite, or bare in hand-written SQL. In those statements every literal and every bind is filtered. Going by table rather than column covers `INSERT … VALUES`, multi-row inserts, upserts and `IN` lists without parsing column positions.
- **What is filtered:** everything from the statement's first quote to its end. This holds however the adapter escapes quotes. SQLite doesn't treat a backslash as an escape, so with HEY's literal-by-literal regex, a bulk-inserted value ending in `\` (account imports do this) pushed the next value out of the match. A malformed statement whose last literal never closed loses that literal too. What's left is the statement's shape up to its first value, for example ``SELECT `identity_access_tokens`.* FROM `identity_access_tokens` WHERE `identity_access_tokens`.`token` = '[FILTERED]'``.
- **Where** (`lib/rails_ext/active_record_sql_redaction.rb`), per Lewis's review:
  - **The `sql.active_record` notification itself.** A `subscribe("sql.active_record", prepend: true)` block replaces the payload's SQL with the redacted text and clears `:binds` and `:type_casted_binds` once, after the statement runs and before any other consumer reads it: Rails' structured event (and through it the text and structured logs), Sentry's breadcrumbs and spans, and anything subscribed later. The adapter's own SQL and bind objects are untouched. Statements run while `Relation#explain` collects keep their SQL, because explain re-runs them from this payload. Nothing in the app calls explain.
  - **Database errors, at translation.** A MySQL server error loses its whole message (only the code stays), as in HEY. Any other error on a redacted statement is filtered the same way as a statement, from its first quote on. Examples are SQLite's syntax errors and the read-only error (`ActiveRecord::ReadOnlyError`, which quotes the statement). The wording the adapters classify errors by quotes nothing, so it survives. The cause is filtered in place, so the translated error and its `cause` both show the filtered message.
- **Sentry** (`saas/lib/fizzy/saas/sentry_sql_redaction.rb`, installed in the engine's `Sentry.init`): breadcrumbs and spans get redacted SQL from the notification. `before_send` stays as the backstop for exception values that name a redacted table. `before_breadcrumb` and `before_send_transaction` also stay, as a backstop against a consumer that reads SQL outside the notification payload, or a Rails or Sentry upgrade that changes subscriber order. Fizzy doesn't sample transactions today. On this Rails revision, executed statements are instrumented through a handle that skips Sentry's span timestamp, so only query-cache hits become DB spans.
- **Parameters** (`config/application.rb`): `code` joins `filter_parameters`, covering the magic-link code and the join code's route parameter. So does `/(?:\A|\.)url\z/`, for a webhook's URL. It's anchored so other params ending in "url" keep their values. It also matches the dotted path, because once any dotted filter is present (`encrypts` adds `audit.notes` and others at eager load), Rails matches every filter against the full path, `webhook.url`. A plain `\Aurl\z` passed in a lazy-loaded test and failed in an eager-loaded one.
- **Delivered mail** (`lib/rails_ext/action_mailer_delivered_event_without_mail.rb`): a `subscribe("deliver.action_mailer", prepend: true)` block sets `payload[:mail]` to `[FILTERED]`. It runs when the notification finishes, after delivery, and delivery works from the mail object. The log keeps "Delivered mail <id>" without the content. This also takes every other mail's recipients and content out of Loki.

### Covered columns

| table.column | secret | how found |
|---|---|---|
| `magic_links.code` | sign-in code | named in the card; `MagicLink` |
| `identity_access_tokens.token` | API bearer token | named in the card; `has_secure_token` in `Identity::AccessToken` |
| `account_join_codes.code` | join code | named in the card; `Account::JoinCode` |
| `identity_transfers.token` | session transfer token: signs its holder in for 4 hours | `has_secure_token` in `Identity::Transfer` |
| `webhooks.signing_secret`, `webhooks.url` | HMAC secret; a Slack or Campfire incoming-webhook URL is a bearer credential | `has_secure_token :signing_secret` in `Webhook` |

How I found them:

- `rg has_secure_token|generates_token_for|SecureRandom|encrypts` across `app/`, `saas/app`, `lib/` and `saas/lib`.
- A scan of every column in `db/schema.rb`, `db/schema_sqlite.rb` and `saas/db/saas_schema.rb` for `token|code|secret|key|digest|pass|otp|nonce|challenge|cred|endpoint|auth|salt|signature|url|cookie|hash`.
- An eager-loaded enumeration of every model's columns in both modes.

### Guard

A test (`every column that looks secret is redacted or declared not secret`) eager loads, scans every model's columns for names like `token|code|secret|passw|digest|key|salt|otp|nonce|credential`, and fails unless each one is on a redacted table or listed in `NOT_SECRET` with a reason.

- **What it catches:** an accident. Someone adds `has_secure_token` or a code column without registering its table.
- **What it can't see:** a credential in a column named otherwise (webhooks' `url` is the example, listed by hand), or a table without a model. Those have to be listed by hand.

### Candidates left out

| column | why it's not redacted |
|---|---|
| `board_publications.key` | the public link to a published board; it's in that page's URL path, so every request for the page logs it anyway |
| `push_subscriptions.endpoint`, `.auth_key`, `.p256dh_key` | Web Push accepts a message only if it's signed with our VAPID key |
| `action_push_native_devices.token` | APNs/FCM device address; pushing to it takes our push credentials |
| `active_storage_blobs.key` | object name; reading the object takes a signed URL |
| `audits1984_auditor_tokens.token_digest`, `filters.params_digest`, `active_storage_variant_records.variation_digest` | digests |
| `action_pack_passkeys.credential_id`, `.public_key` | public by design |
| `sessions.id` | the cookie is a signed id; the bare id can't be replayed |

## Not covered here, and why

These are real, but outside SQL logging. Each needs its own change, and some need a decision.

1. **Request URL paths carry two of these secrets.**
   - **Join codes:** `GET/POST /join/:code` logs the code in `url.full`, `url.path` and the `Started GET "/join/…"` line, and in Sentry's `request.url` and breadcrumb `path`.
   - **Transfer tokens:** `/session/transfers/:id` logs the token the same way. Its parameter is `id`, which `filter_parameters` can't single out.

   Filtering paths means changing rails_structured_logging's request serializer and the Rails request-start log line, or moving these credentials out of the URL. **Step 13's join-code check will still find the code in URL fields until that ships.**
2. **Email-change confirmation tokens** (`User::EmailAddressChangeable#send_email_address_change_confirmation`) are passed to `deliver_later` as an argument. Active Job logs its arguments, and Solid Queue's `INSERT INTO solid_queue_jobs` carries them too. The token is a 30-minute signed GlobalID that completes a change the user asked for. The fix is to have the mailer generate it.
3. **Sentry `net.http` breadcrumbs** record a webhook delivery's full URL. It is attached to an event only if that job then reports an error. Fixing it means keeping only scheme and host for every outgoing request's breadcrumb, which is a debugging trade-off to decide on.
4. **Hex (`0x…`) and double-quoted string literals:** Active Record writes neither, and I found no call site that does.
5. **A webhook URL sent in the query string** (`?webhook[url]=…`) stays in `filtered_path`. Rails filters query-string keys as written, `webhook[url]`, which the filter doesn't match. The form and the API both send it in the body, so this only happens if a client puts its own URL in the query string.

## How it was tested

- **`test/lib/rails_ext/active_record_sql_redaction_test.rb`** runs in both modes (MySQL in SaaS, SQLite in OSS) and uses made-up values throughout. For each covered table it runs a real insert, lookup and update (plus delete or reset where the app does one). It asserts three things:
  - the statement shape is in the log, so the test can't pass on an empty log;
  - the value is absent;
  - the value still reached the database, in the SQL text on MySQL or as a bind on SQLite, and the lookup found the row.

  The file also covers:
  - the structured event payload;
  - a duplicate-entry error, an invalid statement's error and a read-only refusal, checking message, `to_s`, `detailed_message`, `full_message` and `inspect` on both the error and its cause;
  - a bulk insert with a value ending in a backslash;
  - hand-written SQL that names a table bare;
  - a control showing other tables keep their literals.
- **`saas/test/integration/structured_log_redaction_test.rb`** is the SaaS logging path. It captures the exact lines the boot-time rails_structured_logging subscribers write, by stubbing `info` on the configured structured logger, while running:
  - a full magic-link sign-in, including the mail delivery job;
  - a bearer-token API request;
  - a join-code reset;
  - creating a webhook;
  - a job that hits a duplicate entry.

  It checks every line for the made-up value, including `original`, `http.request.parameters` and `error.message`/`error.cause.message`. It also runs the Sentry hooks against a real `Sentry::Configuration`, `Breadcrumb` and `ErrorEvent`.
- **Mutations**, each caught in at least one mode, and `bin/ci` runs both. The first six were measured on the first commit:

  | removed or reverted | failures |
  |---|---|
  | event prepend | 10 |
  | error translation prepend | 2 |
  | mail filter | 1 |
  | `code` filter | 1 |
  | Sentry breadcrumb filter | 1 |
  | `webhooks` from the list | 3, including the guard |
  | bind filtering | 1 (SQLite) |
  | read-only prepend | 1 (MySQL) |
  | literal filtering of non-server errors | 1 (SQLite) |
  | HEY's literal regex | 3 (SQLite) |
  | first-to-last quote match | 3, including the Sentry breadcrumb |
  | quoted-only table matching | 1 MySQL, 2 SQLite |
- **Review:** an adversarial second review attacked missed columns, statement shapes, bypassing log paths and tests passing for the wrong reason. Its findings were:
  - **Fixed in the second commit:** the SQLite backslash leak, errors without a server code (read-only and SQLite), bare table names, the webhook URL parameter, and the SQLite error test gap.
  - **Above, under "Not covered here":** the URL paths, the email-change token and the Sentry HTTP breadcrumbs.

  A second pass on those fixes found three more:
  - **Fixed in the third commit:** an unclosed literal in an error, table names in other cases, and a read-only test that couldn't fail on SQLite. Removing the read-only prepend or the unclosed-literal handling now fails a SQLite test.
  - **Declined:** the query-string webhook URL (item 5 above), and `ReadOnlyError.new(message: …)`. No caller does that, and the one-argument constructor is kept.

  On review here, Copilot found the same unclosed-literal gap in statements, outside errors. The fifth commit filters statements from the first quote on, like errors. CodeQL flagged a test that bulk-inserted a made-up signing secret; that regression now uses an access token instead.

## Notification-based redaction (after review)

Following @lewispb's review, the SQL and delivered-mail redaction moved from prepends on Rails' structured-event subscribers to prepended `sql.active_record` and `deliver.action_mailer` subscriptions. The table policy and the redactor didn't change.

How it was tested, in both database modes (MySQL/Trilogy in SaaS, SQLite in OSS):
- **Order at boot:** both subscriptions are first among their event's listeners, the SQL one in the first group to finish. It's still first after Sentry's breadcrumb logger and tracing are activated.
- **Later consumers:** consumers subscribed afterwards with a one-argument block, a five-argument block and a regex all see redacted SQL and empty binds.
- **The database still gets the real values:** a subscriber prepended ahead of the redaction records the payload as the adapter built it, and every lookup still finds its row.
- **Sentry:** Sentry is started as the engine starts it, with a dummy transport and the real breadcrumb logger and tracing subscribers. With no Sentry filters installed, the recorded `sql.active_record` breadcrumbs and a DB span (a query-cache hit) carry no value. With the production configuration, breadcrumbs, spans and error events carry none either.
- **Mail:** the delivered mail still contains the code (subject and body), while the log and the `action_mailer.delivered` event don't.
- **End to end:** the SaaS structured-log tests are kept.
- **Mutations:**
  - emptying the SQL subscriber fails 17 tests in SaaS and 6 in OSS;
  - subscribing it without `prepend:` fails the boot-order and both Sentry tests;
  - removing the mail filter fails 2.

A further adversarial review of this change:
- **Fixed:** EXPLAIN on a redacted table had broken, because explain re-runs collected statements from the payload. Also fixed: test teardown left Sentry's non-SQL tracing subscriptions behind.
- **Recorded, not changed:** start-phase consumers, unsubscribe-by-name, and DB spans existing only for query-cache hits (see Risk).

## CI

The fourth commit makes `bin/ci` runnable in SaaS mode with Bundler 4. Booting `bin/ci` exports `BUNDLE_LOCKFILE`, which outranks the `BUNDLE_GEMFILE` each step sets. So the SaaS steps resolved `Gemfile.saas` against `Gemfile.lock`. They then either failed ("git source … is not yet checked out") or, with `auto_install`, rewrote `Gemfile.lock`. `config/ci.rb` now drops the variable so each step derives its own. It's a separate commit so it can be split out if preferred.

## Risk and rollback

- **What changes:** logging and reporting only. Statements on five low-volume tables lose their literal values in logs, Sentry and errors, but keep their shape, table and timing. Delivered mail is no longer logged, and `code` and `url` parameters show as `[FILTERED]`.
- **Cost:** one regex per logged statement.
- **Rails internals:** two notification subscriptions, plus two prepends, on `AbstractAdapter#translate_exception_class` and `ActiveRecord::ReadOnlyError#initialize`. A Rails bump that renames either prepended method fails its tests rather than silently leaking. Tests also assert that both subscriptions run first at boot, before Rails' and Sentry's.
- **Known boundaries of the notification approach:**
  - An evented subscriber's `start` callback runs before any `finish`, so it sees the raw payload. Nothing installed reads SQL at start.
  - Unsubscribing `sql.active_record` by name removes the redaction along with everything else. Sentry's `Tracing.unsubscribe_tracing_events` does this, but nothing in the app or in Sentry's normal lifecycle calls it, and the Sentry backstop filters still apply.
- **Rollback:** revert. No migration.
- **Personal data:** no new flow to a third party; this removes data from logs and Sentry.

## Existing Loki lines are a separate step

This stops new lines only. Lines already in Loki keep these values until they're deleted. The coordinator will post delete selectors after deploy, as a separate step on the card.

title: Store personal access tokens only as digests (D2 of 3: rerun the backfill, stop the plaintext)
body:
> [!CAUTION]
> **Explicitly gated. Don't merge this until production is running D1 (#3192)**, on every production container, **and the backfill rerun in this PR (`20261017120000`) has run against `fizzy_production`**, digesting every personal access token production `main` wrote in plaintext meanwhile. This code stops falling back to plaintext: a token production `main` wrote without a digest, and never used since, stops authenticating the moment this code serves it, unless the rerun has digested it first.

> [!WARNING]
> **This PR contains migrations. Don't merge it directly.** It has to go through the beta integration branch ([`oauth-integration-2026-10-15`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/oauth-integration-2026-10-15/docs/oauth/integration-migrations.md)) and be **migrated by hand on beta before it lands**. beta1 runs against `fizzy_production` (`saas/config/database.yml` ends `beta: *production`), so migrating on beta1 *is* migrating production. The rows to add to that branch's migration inventory are [below](#migration-inventory-rows-for-the-integration-branch); this PR doesn't push to the integration branch.

Stacked on #3192 (train: #2296 → #3080 → #3081 → #3082 → #3160 → #3161 → #3159 → #3163 → #3169 → #3192 → this → #3203).

Implements **step D2** of hashing tokens at rest (rubric TK-2, bearer artifacts stored only as digests):

| Step | What it does | Status |
|---|---|---|
| D1 (#3192) | Add digest columns, backfill, read by digest with a plaintext fallback for personal access tokens, keep writing their plaintext for production `main` | after the OAuth stack |
| **D2** (this PR) | Rerun the backfill. Stop writing plaintext and stop the fallback. Ignore `token` | after D1 is deployed to production |
| D3 (#3203) | Drop `identity_access_tokens.token` | after D2 is deployed everywhere |

## What D2 does

- **Rerun of the backfill** ([`BackfillRemainingTokenDigests`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/3ac03cc45d6f78bf551fa797d3cc360698c569d8/db/migrate/20261017120000_backfill_remaining_token_digests.rb)). The same digesting as D1's `BackfillTokenDigests`, for the one column left: every row with a `token` and no `token_digest` gets its digest, and an OAuth row's plaintext is cleared (none should exist). It's self-contained, with its own model, rather than requiring D1's migration file, so loading both in one `db:migrate` doesn't redefine a class.
  - `update_all`, one `UPDATE … WHERE id = ? AND token_digest IS NULL` per row, so `updated_at`, the grant idle clock, doesn't move.
  - Batches of 500, `disable_ddl_transaction!`.
  - **Duplicate plaintext tokens are refused before anything is written**, naming row ids, never tokens. That includes a new token duplicating one D1 already digested, since D1 kept personal tokens' plaintext.
  - Rerunnable: it touches only rows without a digest, does nothing once the column is gone (after D3), and its `down` is a no-op, so `bin/rails db:migrate:redo:primary VERSION=20261017120000` runs it again.
  - Personal access tokens **keep their plaintext** until D3 drops the column, so rolling production back to code that reads only plaintext still finds them. Clearing it here would buy one deploy's worth of plaintext-at-rest and cost that rollback.
- **Compatible with #3205 (personal access tokens as grants of a personal access client).** #3205 changes #3192's backfill so a rerun keeps the plaintext of a token issued by that client (`client_id` `fizzy-personal-access`), not only of one with no client. This rerun does the same: it looks the client up by that `client_id` and treats its tokens as personal, so whichever order the two land in, no personal token loses its plaintext before D3. Before #3205 the lookup finds nothing and only client-less tokens count as personal, as in D1. A test stands a fixture client in for it. Versions don't collide either: #3205 takes `20261016120000` and `20261016120100`, so this is `20261017120000` (and D3's `20261017130000`). In the model, #3205 rewrites `set_token` to branch on `personal?`; this PR removes the lines it rewrites, so whichever rebases second keeps #3205's `personal?` branch and drops `token.presence` and the plaintext write. A trial merge of the two (local, not pushed) conflicts only there, in both schema version lines and in the conformance doc; with that resolved, this PR's tests pass, and #3205's tests that pin D1's plaintext write and fallback (in `personal_access_token_forms_test.rb` and `personal_access_client_test.rb`) fail as they should once D2 is below them, and need the same `.token` → `.raw_token` / digest-only rewrite this PR gives D1's tests.
- **No plaintext writes.** `set_token` writes only `token_digest`. A rotation no longer names `token` either.
- **No plaintext fallback.** `find_by_raw_token` is `find_by(token_digest: TokenDigester.digests(raw))` and nothing else; `find_and_digest_undigested` is gone, and with it #3192's rule that a datacenter outside the primary authenticates an undigested token without healing it. Those tokens are left to D2-1 as well. `find_honored`, which bearer authentication uses, goes through it, so it finds by digest alone.
- **`self.ignored_columns += %w[ token ]`** on `Identity::AccessToken`. With `partial_inserts` off (`load_defaults 8.1`), a model names every column it knows on INSERT; ignoring `token` takes it out of every INSERT and, since Rails enumerates columns when any are ignored, every SELECT. That is what lets D3 drop it under running D2 processes.

Unchanged: the token format (`fizzy_pat_` + base58 body), the create JSON fizzy-cli reads (`id`, `token`, `description`, `permission`, `created_at`), the revocation endpoint (it already goes through `find_by_raw_token`), and every OAuth path, which D1 already made digest-only.

### Tests

- `ApiTest`: the two scheme pins (`bearer` matched case-insensitively, `Basic Bearer …` not bearer) present the fixture's `raw_token`. (#3192 now sends grants' raw tokens in its three challenge pins itself.)
- Fixtures store only digests; their raw values live in `AccessTokenTestHelper::RAW_FIXTURE_TOKENS`, and `identity_access_tokens(...)` hands back records carrying `raw_token`, as an issued token does. Call sites moved from `.token` to `.raw_token`.
- `Identity::AccessTokenTest`: personal tokens store only their digest (the column is NULL), a token stored only in plaintext **doesn't** authenticate and issues no plaintext query, and the model ignores the column. D1's fallback tests are gone with the fallback.
- `BackfillRemainingTokenDigestsTest`: digests the leftovers, keeps personal plaintext and clears a grant's, leaves `updated_at` alone, is idempotent, the result authenticates, refuses duplicates (including one already digested) before any write without naming the token, keeps the plaintext of the personal access client's tokens, and is a no-op once the column is gone. D1's `BackfillTokenDigestsTest` now writes and reads plaintext through the migration's own model.

## Migration inventory rows for the integration branch

For [`docs/oauth/integration-migrations.md`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/oauth-integration-2026-10-15/docs/oauth/integration-migrations.md) on `oauth-integration-2026-10-15`. This PR doesn't change that branch. Labeled D2-1 rather than numbered, so a sibling PR claiming the rows after #3192's 8–10 doesn't collide:

| # | Version / file | PR | What it does | Production table | MySQL 8.4 DDL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D2-1 | `20261017120000_backfill_remaining_token_digests.rb` | this | **Data only, no DDL.** Refuses duplicate `token`s first. Then one `UPDATE … WHERE id = ? AND token_digest IS NULL` per row with a `token` and no digest: `token_digest`, and `token` NULLed for OAuth rows (a personal access client's rows, once #3205 adds it, keep it). `updated_at` doesn't move. `disable_ddl_transaction!`, batches of 500. `down` is a no-op | `identity_access_tokens`: ~3,500 rows | No ALTER, so no exclusive metadata lock: only the shared MDL every read takes, and row locks on the primary key. `token` has no index, so the duplicate check and the batch selection each scan ~3,500 rows, milliseconds. Expect a handful of updates: only tokens production `main` wrote before D1 reached it and nobody has used since |

Notes for the runbook:

- **Order.** (1) D1 deployed to every production container; no `main` process older than D1 left running. (2) Run D2-1 on beta1. (3) Only then let D2 code serve, on beta or anywhere: beta's web role doesn't migrate on boot (see the integration doc), so either migrate with the new image first (its option B) or accept that until D2-1 runs, beta refuses the leftover plaintext-only tokens (production, still on D1, keeps accepting and healing them).
- **If anything wrote a plaintext-only token after D2-1 ran** (a pre-D1 process that outlived the deploy), rerun it: `bin/rails db:migrate:redo:primary VERSION=20261017120000`. A quick check before landing: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM identity_access_tokens WHERE token_digest IS NULL` should be 0.
- **Undo** by version: `bin/rails db:migrate:down:primary VERSION=20261017120000` is a no-op (the digests stay, and D1 reads them). Undoing the code is a plain revert: D1 still reads digests first and falls back to the plaintext that's still there. Never `db:rollback` (see the integration doc).
- **Self-hosted installs** migrate on boot before serving (`db:prepare`), so one that upgrades straight past D1 runs D1's backfill and D2-1 before this code answers a request. With Kamal, the old container keeps serving until the new one passes its health check, so a personal access token created on a pre-D1 container in those seconds, after D2-1 has scanned, has no digest and never authenticates. Its holder sees a 401 on first use and creates another. Closing that would mean keeping the plaintext fallback D2 exists to remove, so it isn't done; D1 and D2 reach `main` separately, so an install that follows `main` passes through D1 first.

## Verified

On thelio at the `dcb914ceb` head, whose diff differs from this head's only in three `api_test.rb` lines that #3192 now carries itself, gated on exit status (CI's commands: `bin/rails db:setup` then `bin/rails test`, against a dedicated `mysql:8.4` container):

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| SaaS (MySQL 8.4) | 2298 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors |
| OSS (SQLite) | 2130 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors |
| OSS (MySQL 8.4, `DATABASE_ADAPTER=mysql`) | 2130 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors |

Migration round trip, SQLite and a dedicated MySQL 8.4 container: loaded #3192's schema and seeded a personal access token written by pre-D1 code (plaintext only, never used), one written by D1 (plaintext and digest) and an OAuth grant (digest only), all with `updated_at` five days back. Then up to `20261017120000`: the pre-D1 token got its digest, everything kept its digest, personal plaintext stayed, no `updated_at` moved, and the dump matches this branch's `db/schema.rb` / `db/schema_sqlite.rb` exactly. `redo` of the rerun: same. (D3 continues the round trip.)

**#3191 shipped-client pins**, at 8340a8db4 (this head before a rebase that touched only files this PR doesn't) merged with `test/pin-shipped-client-auth` at 98572aaaf, locally, not pushed. Unchanged, `ShippedClientAuthenticationTest` errors (OSS: 8 tests, 6 errors), because its `bearer` helper reads the fixture's plaintext as `.token`, which no longer exists, and so does one SaaS audits test. With those two lines reading `.raw_token`, they pass: OSS (SQLite) 8 tests, SaaS (MySQL 8.4) 17 with the auditor pins, 0 failures. **Whichever of #3191 and this lands second carries that two-line change.** The token string and the create JSON shape are unchanged.

## Not done here, on purpose

- **The plaintext column stays** until D3, for the rollback above.
- **No change to `oauth_*`**: D1 already made OAuth credentials digest-only.
- **No new third party or personal-data flow.**

title: Drop the plaintext personal access token column (D3 of 3: drop identity_access_tokens.token)
body:
> [!CAUTION]
> **Explicitly gated. Don't merge this until D2 (#3202) is deployed to production and to beta** (every beta destination: they share `fizzy_production`), and to staging, **and every process that might name `token` on INSERT has been replaced.** Production runs with `partial_inserts` off (`load_defaults 8.1`), so a process running D1 or anything older names every column it knows on every INSERT. Once `token` is gone, such a process fails to create personal access tokens (`Unknown column 'token'`), fails OAuth refreshes (D1's rotation writes `token: nil`), and answers an unknown Bearer token with a 500 instead of a 401 (D1's plaintext fallback queries `token`). D2 ignores the column, so only D2 or later may be running when this migrates.

> [!WARNING]
> **This PR contains migrations. Don't merge it directly.** It has to go through the beta integration branch ([`oauth-integration-2026-10-15`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/oauth-integration-2026-10-15/docs/oauth/integration-migrations.md)) and be **migrated by hand on beta before it lands**. beta1 runs against `fizzy_production` (`saas/config/database.yml` ends `beta: *production`), so migrating on beta1 *is* migrating production. The rows to add to that branch's migration inventory are [below](#migration-inventory-rows-for-the-integration-branch); this PR doesn't push to the integration branch.

Stacked on #3202 (train: … → #3169 → #3192 → #3202 → this).

Implements **step D3**, the last, of hashing tokens at rest (rubric TK-2, bearer artifacts stored only as digests):

| Step | What it does | Status |
|---|---|---|
| D1 (#3192) | Add digest columns, backfill, read by digest with a plaintext fallback, keep writing personal plaintext | after the OAuth stack |
| D2 (#3202) | Rerun the backfill, stop writing and reading plaintext, ignore `token` | after D1 is deployed to production |
| **D3** (this PR) | Drop `identity_access_tokens.token` | after D2 is deployed everywhere |

## What D3 does

- [`DropIdentityAccessTokenPlaintext`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/5c0461094696a0e398533c2b55c06af3a4171464/db/migrate/20261017130000_drop_identity_access_token_plaintext.rb): on MySQL, `ALTER TABLE identity_access_tokens DROP INDEX index_identity_access_tokens_on_refresh_token, DROP COLUMN refresh_token, DROP COLUMN token, ALGORITHM=INPLACE, LOCK=NONE`, a table rebuild; elsewhere `remove_index` and `remove_column`. The plaintext `refresh_token` column was kept out of #3192's `DropPlaintextOauthCredentials`, so that no migration dropped a column production `main` had cached; #3192 ignores it and empties it, so it goes here. MySQL 8.4 would otherwise drop it INSTANT, from the data dictionary alone, leaving each row's plaintext in the table's pages until the row is next rewritten, which for a personal access token is usually never (`updated_at` doesn't move on use). With it go the plaintext personal access tokens D1 and D2 left beside their digests. **No token is stored in plaintext any more.**
- **`down` restores both columns empty**: nullable `string`s, `refresh_token` with its unique index, as they were before any token was written. **The values are unrecoverable**: only digests remain, so code that reads only plaintext (production `main` before D1) can't authenticate any token again. D1 and D2 read digests and keep working.
- `Identity::AccessToken` no longer needs `ignored_columns`, so it's removed. `db/schema.rb` and `db/schema_sqlite.rb` drop both columns and the index, and move to `2026_10_17_130000`.
- Tests: D1's and D2's backfill tests are deleted, since both write plaintext into a column that no longer exists. Both migrations stay, and run in order on a fresh `db:migrate` before this one. `Identity::AccessTokenTest` asserts both columns are gone. [`test/migrations/drop_identity_access_token_plaintext_test.rb`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/a420fae04/test/migrations/drop_identity_access_token_plaintext_test.rb) caches the table's columns as D2's code does (ignoring both), runs the migration, and creates a token with them.
- Docs: the conformance record's token row says step 3 is done, and [`docs/docker-deployment.md`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/5c0461094696a0e398533c2b55c06af3a4171464/docs/docker-deployment.md#secret-key-base) now says tokens are *stored* only as digests, not just looked up by them.

## Migration inventory rows for the integration branch

For [`docs/oauth/integration-migrations.md`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/oauth-integration-2026-10-15/docs/oauth/integration-migrations.md) on `oauth-integration-2026-10-15`. This PR doesn't change that branch. Labeled D3-1 so a sibling PR's rows after #3192's 8–10 don't collide:

| # | Version / file | PR | What it does | Production table | MySQL 8.4 DDL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D3-1 | `20261017130000_drop_identity_access_token_plaintext.rb` | this | MySQL: `ALTER TABLE identity_access_tokens DROP INDEX index_identity_access_tokens_on_refresh_token, DROP COLUMN refresh_token, DROP COLUMN token, ALGORITHM=INPLACE, LOCK=NONE`. `down` adds both back, nullable and empty, with the index | `identity_access_tokens`: ~3,500 rows | **INPLACE, LOCK=NONE: a table rebuild that allows concurrent reads and writes**, forced rather than MySQL's default INSTANT so the plaintext leaves the pages (see above). Sub-second at ~3,500 rows and 0.65 MB; on 8.4.11 the rebuild was confirmed by the table's InnoDB `TABLE_ID` changing and `TOTAL_ROW_VERSIONS` resetting to 0. `token` has no index of its own; `refresh_token`'s goes in the same statement |

Notes for the runbook:

- **The lock that matters.** Like every online ALTER, the rebuild takes an exclusive metadata lock on `identity_access_tokens`, which every Bearer request reads, briefly at its start and again at its end. Each time it waits for every open transaction that has touched the table, and while it waits, every new query on the table queues behind it: API traffic stalls. The `MIGRATE=1` connection has no `max_execution_time`, and on `main` nothing sets `lock_wait_timeout` (the integration branch sets 5 s). Check `information_schema.innodb_trx` just before, and if the step sits for more than a few seconds, cancel it rather than let the queue build; it's one statement, so it's safe to rerun.
- **Before running it**, confirm nothing older than D2 is running: production, every beta destination and staging on D2's image, no lingering old containers or console sessions (`bin/kamal app details -d <dest>`). A D1 process left running is the failure in the caution above.
- **Undo** by version: `bin/rails db:migrate:down:primary VERSION=20261017130000`. It restores empty columns, not the tokens. Never `db:rollback` (see the integration doc). Undoing D2's `20261017120000` is a no-op either way.
- After this, neither backfill should be redone by hand: D2's rerun is a no-op without the column, and D1's (`20261015120100`) would fail looking for it.
- **Self-hosted installs** that upgrade with Kamal from a version older than D2 migrate in the new container while the old one still serves, so until the cutover (seconds, once the new container passes its health check) the old one fails as in the caution above. That's bounded by the cutover, and D2 and D3 reach `main` separately, so an install that follows `main` passes through D2 first. Stopping the old container before migrating would close the window and cost every upgrade its zero-downtime cutover, so it isn't done.
- **Plaintext outside the table**: backups and binlogs taken before this migration still hold it, until their retention runs out. On SQLite, `remove_column` rebuilds the table, but the old pages stay in the file as free pages until a `VACUUM`.
- Staging has its own database, so it migrates separately, by the same gate: staging on D2 first.

## Verified

On thelio at the `dcb914ceb` head; this PR's diff over #3202 is byte-identical since. Gated on exit status (CI's commands: `bin/rails db:setup` then `bin/rails test`, against a dedicated `mysql:8.4` container):

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| SaaS (MySQL 8.4) | 2285 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors |
| OSS (SQLite) | 2117 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors |
| OSS (MySQL 8.4, `DATABASE_ADAPTER=mysql`) | 2117 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors |

Migration round trip, SQLite and a dedicated MySQL 8.4 container: continuing #3202's (#3192's schema, a pre-D1 plaintext-only token, a D1 token, an OAuth grant): up through `20261017130000`, the column is gone, every index is intact, both personal tokens and a newly created one authenticate, no `updated_at` moved, and the dump matches `db/schema.rb` / `db/schema_sqlite.rb` exactly. Then down newest first: the column comes back nullable and empty, and the dump differs from #3192's only in that the restored column is appended (and, on SQLite, declared as the original `CreateIdentityAccessTokens` declared it, without the dump's `limit: 255`). Then up again and `redo` of `20261017120000` with the column gone (a no-op): checks pass, dump matches.

**#3191 shipped-client pins** need the same two-line `.token` → `.raw_token` change #3202 describes. With it, they passed against this branch before the rebase onto `dcb914ceb` (OSS 19 tests, SaaS 28 with the auditor pins), and against #3202's current head. This branch's own diff over #3202 is unchanged since. The token string and the create JSON shape are unchanged.

## Not done here, on purpose

- **No plaintext is carried anywhere**: there's nothing to keep once every token is digested.
- **No new third party or personal-data flow.**

title: Report OAuth audit events and export OAuth metrics
body:
## What

Fizzy's OAuth server reports its lifecycle as audit events and exports the standard's metrics: **AU-1** and **OB-1** of the 37signals OAuth Standard (bc3 `doc/oauth/rubric.md` §12–13). AU-2, AU-3 and OB-2 aren't in this PR.

### How it's wired

- **Core (OSS and SaaS):** `Oauth::Audit.record` reports each event through `Rails.event` (Rails edge's structured event reporter). Fizzy's own structured logging, `rails_structured_logging`, is SaaS-only, and its `logger.struct` merges fields into a single request line. That can't hold the several events one request reports (a code exchange reports three), or the events the sweeps report from jobs. Metric-only signals (errors, throttling, token request timing, sweep failures) are Active Support notifications named `*.oauth`. Core never references Yabeda.
- **SaaS:** `Fizzy::Saas::OauthAuditLog` writes each `oauth.*` event as its own ECS-shaped JSON line to `config.structured_logging.logger` (STDOUT → Loki). Its `transaction.id` is the request id, as on the request line, so the two join. `Yabeda::Oauth` (`saas/lib/yabeda/oauth.rb`, installed like the other `saas/lib/yabeda` modules) subscribes to both sources.
- Grants and PATs report their creation and their ending from `after_commit` callbacks on `Identity::AccessToken`. So an event always describes a change that committed, and **every way a grant ends reports**: callers that know why use `#revoke(reason:, actor:)`, and a cascade from a deleted identity or client is named through `destroyed_by_association` (`identity_deleted`, `client_deleted`, otherwise `deleted`).

### Events (AU-1)

| Event | Where | actor | reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `oauth.client.registered` | client created | `client` (DCR) / `admin` | |
| `oauth.client.swept` | `Oauth::Client.cleanup` | `system` | `unused` |
| `oauth.consent.{shown,approved,denied}` | authorization endpoint | `user` | |
| `oauth.code.issued` | consent approved | `user` | |
| `oauth.code.redeemed` / `oauth.grant.created` / `oauth.token.issued` | code exchange (after commit) | `client` | |
| `oauth.code.replayed` | second redemption of a code | `client` | |
| `oauth.token.refreshed` | rotation | `client` | |
| `oauth.grant.narrowed` | a refresh that narrows scope | `client` | |
| `oauth.token.grace_replay` | retired refresh token within grace, including one whose scope is refused | `client` | `answered` / `superseded` / `scope_mismatch` / `successor_gone` |
| `oauth.token.reuse_detected` | retired refresh token past grace | `client` | |
| `oauth.grant.revoked` | every grant ending | `client` / `user` / `system` | `revocation_endpoint` (+ `presented: access\|refresh`), `disconnected`, `lapsed`, `reuse_detected`, `code_replayed`, `identity_deleted`, `client_deleted`, `deleted` |
| `oauth.pat.created` / `oauth.pat.revoked` | personal access tokens | `user` / `client` (at RFC 7009) / `system` | `revoked`, `revocation_endpoint`, `identity_deleted` |

Every event carries `app` (`fizzy`), `event`, `client_id`, `client_class` (`dcr`, `first_party` for `trusted`, `partner` for other operator-provisioned clients, `pat`), `client_type`, `grant_id`, `family_id` (the grant row is the family), `identity_id`, `tenant_id`, `actor`, `reason` and `request_id`. A field that doesn't apply is nil, not absent. Details are limited to `grant_type`, `permission` and `presented`. Fizzy revokes whole grants, so there's no separate `oauth.token.revoked`: it's `oauth.grant.revoked` with `presented`.

### Metrics (OB-1)

Under bc3's names and labels: `oauth_token_grants_total{grant_type,client_type}`, `oauth_token_errors_total{error_code,client_type}` (token and revocation endpoints), `oauth_token_request_duration_seconds{grant_type}`, `oauth_authorization_grants_total{client_type,account_scope="identity"}`, `oauth_authorization_denials_total{client_type}`, `oauth_revocations_total{token_type,initiator}` (initiator `user`/`client`), `oauth_family_revocations_total{reason}` (grants the server ends; never PATs), `oauth_dcr_registrations_total`, `oauth_dcr_rejections_total{reason}`, `oauth_rate_limit_hits_total{endpoint}`, `oauth_cleanup_step_failures_total{step}`, and the proposed `oauth_replays_total{kind=grace|reuse}`.

- Every label value comes from a fixed set in the code. `client_type` is `public`/`confidential`/`unknown`. No client id is a label.
- A throttled request counts as a rate-limit hit, not as a token error or DCR rejection.
- There's no `app` label: the scrape already adds `app="fizzy"` (`rails_requests_total` in Thanos has it).

## Personal data

This adds no new personal data and no new third party, so it needs no Trust & Compliance card. The events carry internal ids the request log already records: the identity id, and the account's queenbee id as `tenant_id` (nil in practice, since OAuth endpoints run outside any account). `client_id`, `request_id` and enums make up the rest. One placement is new: the token endpoint and the sweeps have no signed-in identity, so their request and job lines carry none, while their events carry the grant's `identity_id`. That's the same internal id, in the same Loki, that every API call made with that grant already logs. The IP address and user agent aren't repeated; `request_id` joins an event to the request line that already holds them. No event carries a token, refresh token, client secret, authorization code or digest. The tests check this on every event they capture, and `Rails.event`'s `filter_parameters` masking is a second net that the tests also assert never fires on a real field.

## Tests

- `test/integration/oauth_audit_test.rb` and `test/models/oauth/audit_test.rb` cover every path above, cascades and a rolled-back revocation included. Every captured event is checked for exactly the standard fields, nothing credential-shaped (`fizzy_(pat|at|rt|cs)_`, 64-hex digests), and none of the raw tokens, codes or secrets the test handled, nor their digests.
- `test/integration/oauth_instrumentation_test.rb` covers the notifications and their bounded labels.
- `saas/test/lib/yabeda/oauth_test.rb` checks every counter and histogram increment, and that no series is labeled with a client id.
- `saas/test/lib/oauth_audit_log_test.rb` checks the line shape, the `transaction.id` join, that the engine subscribes, and that a line carries no IP address or user agent.
- Mutation checks: dropping the revocation callback fails 11 tests, and reverting reuse detection to a bare `destroy` fails its test.

Local runs on thelio at `42e29ea2d` (on `oauth-token-digests` 1b3ab1f17), as CI runs them:

| Suite | Runs | Failures | Errors | Skips | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SaaS, MySQL 8.4 | 2353 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| OSS, SQLite | 2167 | 0 | 0 | 5 | 0 |
| OSS, MySQL 8.4 | 2167 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 |

The OSS runs boot and pass without Yabeda in the bundle.

## Not in this PR

- AU-2 needs an admin disable action, which Fizzy doesn't have.
- AU-3 (account activity) and OB-2 (dashboard and alerts as code) are follow-ups.
- OSS installs get no audit log subscriber. Events reach `Rails.event`, where a self-hosted install can subscribe.

title: Issue personal access tokens from a first-party client, and backfill existing ones onto it
body:
> [!WARNING]
> **This PR contains migrations. Don't merge it directly.** It has to go through the beta integration branch ([`oauth-integration-2026-10-15`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/oauth-integration-2026-10-15/docs/oauth/integration-migrations.md)) and be **migrated by hand on beta before it lands**. beta1 runs against `fizzy_production` (`saas/config/database.yml` ends `beta: *production`), so migrating on beta1 *is* migrating production. The rows to add to that branch's migration inventory are [below](#migration-inventory-rows-for-the-integration-branch); this PR doesn't push to the integration branch.

Stacked on #3192 (train: #2296 → #3080 → #3081 → #3082 → #3160 → #3161 → #3159 → #3163 → #3169 → #3192 → this).

Implements #3164 steps 1 to 3: a personal access token becomes a one-off access token of a first-party client, `fizzy-personal-access`, the way bc3's are of `bc-personal-access`. Rubric checks **LG-1** and **LG-2** (bc3 `doc/oauth/rubric.md`, branch `oauth-standard`):

- **LG-1**: "A PAT is a degenerate grant: an internal `*-personal-access` client, and a one-off access token in the same digest-stored table. It is shown once, can be revoked, and is listed with connected apps. Identity-wide reach is rechecked live against membership."
- **LG-2**: "Migrating existing PATs keeps their reach, their non-expiry and their token string. Re-digest them in place; never re-issue."

LG-1 is met; its "listed with connected apps" is settled as personal access tokens staying on their own page ([below](#decisions)). LG-2 is met. No token is re-issued or re-digested: the backfill sets only `oauth_client_id`, and #3192 already digested every token in place.

## The issuer ([`Oauth::Client`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/59d6546a522e7fa785e2f6ac640e85c494f6ad7c/app/models/oauth/client.rb#L16-L26))

- `PERSONAL_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID = "fizzy-personal-access"`, named "Personal Access Tokens". It is `trusted`, public (`none`), has scopes `read write`, and has no redirect URIs. It's the only client exempt from the redirect requirement.
- **It isn't dynamically registered,** so the #3159 sweep (`Oauth::Client.stale`, which takes only `dynamically_registered` clients) never picks it up. A test ages it a year and sweeps.
- **It's listed for no grant type, so it fails closed.** `GRANT_TYPES = %w[ authorization_code refresh_token ]` is now an allowlist that both endpoints check (`#grant_types`, `#allows_grant_type?`), and the issuer's list is empty, as bc3's `grant_types: []` is.
  - The authorization endpoint refuses it with `unauthorized_client` ([`set_client`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/59d6546a522e7fa785e2f6ac640e85c494f6ad7c/app/controllers/oauth/authorizations_controller.rb#L75)).
  - The token endpoint refuses it with `unauthorized_client`, for any grant type, before looking up a code or refresh token ([`validate_client_grant_type`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/59d6546a522e7fa785e2f6ac640e85c494f6ad7c/app/controllers/oauth/tokens_controller.rb#L83)).
  - Before this, nothing in those paths could have minted for it anyway: it has no redirect URIs, and `find_by_refresh_token` is OAuth-scoped. The allowlist makes the refusal explicit instead of incidental.
- **Its client_id can't be claimed by anyone else.** It contains a hyphen, and generated client_ids (`has_secure_token`, base58) never do.
- **It can't be destroyed.** A `before_destroy`, prepended so it runs ahead of #3159's `lock_client` and of the cascade, aborts on the *stored* `client_id`, so an unsaved change in memory doesn't get past it. Destroying it would cascade (`dependent: :destroy`) to every client-backed personal access token on the install.
- **Provisioning.**
  - By migration, so SaaS and self-hosted installs that migrate both get it.
  - On first use, through `Oauth::Client.personal_access_issuer` (`create_or_find_by!` on the unique `client_id` index). A fresh install loads the schema rather than running migrations, so this covers it.

Minting ([`My::AccessTokensController#create`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/59d6546a522e7fa785e2f6ac640e85c494f6ad7c/app/controllers/my/access_tokens_controller.rb#L18)) now passes `oauth_client: Oauth::Client.personal_access_issuer`. The JSON response shape fizzy-cli reads is unchanged: `id token description permission created_at`, and a test pins the key set.

## Every "no client means personal" check, for both forms

A personal access token is now "no client, **or** the personal access client". The client-less form stays fully supported: production `main` doesn't know the issuer, keeps writing client-less tokens until this train ships, and shares the database with beta.

| Check | Where | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `personal` / `oauth` scopes | [`access_token.rb#L33`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/59d6546a522e7fa785e2f6ac640e85c494f6ad7c/app/models/identity/access_token.rb#L33) | `personal` = nil **or** the issuer (subquery). `oauth` excludes both forms |
| `honored?`: personal tokens stay honored while OAuth is dark | [`#L157`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/59d6546a522e7fa785e2f6ac640e85c494f6ad7c/app/models/identity/access_token.rb#L157) | `oauth_client_id.nil? \|\| acceptance_enabled? \|\| personal? \|\| pilot`. The client is only loaded while OAuth is dark, as before |
| `lapsed` scope and `lapsed?`: personal tokens never lapse | [`#L37`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/59d6546a522e7fa785e2f6ac640e85c494f6ad7c/app/models/identity/access_token.rb#L37), [`#L187`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/59d6546a522e7fa785e2f6ac640e85c494f6ad7c/app/models/identity/access_token.rb#L187) | Both go through `oauth` |
| Expiry and refresh-token callback: personal tokens get neither | [`#L67`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/59d6546a522e7fa785e2f6ac640e85c494f6ad7c/app/models/identity/access_token.rb#L67) | `if: :oauth?` |
| Token prefix (`fizzy_pat_`) and the D1 plaintext kept for production `main` | [`set_token`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/59d6546a522e7fa785e2f6ac640e85c494f6ad7c/app/models/identity/access_token.rb#L235) | `personal?` |
| D1 plaintext fallback and heal | `find_and_digest_undigested` | Already used `personal`, so it now covers both forms |
| Revocation by possession | [`revocable_token`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/59d6546a522e7fa785e2f6ac640e85c494f6ad7c/app/controllers/oauth/revocations_controller.rb#L46) | Already used `personal`.
