title: Save a draft with its empty description so concurrent autosaves update it
body:
Fixes [FIZZY-Z2](https://basecamp.sentry.io/issues/7808339228/) (`ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` on `action_text_rich_texts.index_action_text_rich_texts_uniqueness` in `CardsController#update`). The same race has been filed under a new Sentry group about weekly since July, because the duplicate key is part of the title: FIZZY-T3, TP, V3, VQ, WX (22 events), Y6 (5) and Z2.

## What happened

A draft card autosaves as you type (`auto_save_controller.js` → `CardsController#update.json`), and a new draft has no `description` rich text row. On 2026-10-23 at 08:11:21Z two autosaves of one new draft landed 23 ms apart on two hosts, and both inserted the card's first description. The unique index refused the second, which returned 500. Auto-save ignores the response and no longer counts the form dirty. So when the refused save carried the later keystrokes and nothing was typed after, those keystrokes were lost.

## The change

A draft gets an empty `description` row when it's saved (`Card::Statuses`, `before_validation`, drafts only). The row exists before the first autosave, so concurrent saves update it (last write wins) instead of racing to insert it.

The row is built at validation rather than save so it is validated with the card. That's where the rich text takes its `account` default; a row built in `before_save` skipped validation and failed `NOT NULL account_id`.

## Existing drafts

Drafts made before this have no row until they're next saved. Reopening a board's draft through "new card" (`User#draft_new_card_in`) saves it, so it gets its row then. The one remaining case is a draft left open across the deploy that autosaves twice at once before it's reopened. That can hit the race once.

Published cards aren't affected: only the draft form autosaves. A card created published gets no row it wasn't given.

## Tests (`test/models/card/statuses_test.rb`)

- A draft is saved with an empty description.
- Two first saves of a draft's description in flight together both succeed. Each loads the card before the other's save lands, which reproduces the production interleaving.
- Reopening a draft saved without a row (the `unfinished_thoughts` fixture) gives it one.
- A card created published gets no description row. This is the scope guard.

The first three fail without the change; the concurrent-save test fails with the production `RecordNotUnique`. Run on SQLite locally; full `bin/ci` (MySQL, SaaS and OSS) on this head below.

title: Bump crass to 1.0.8 for GHSA-pq4g-8rxf-4g29
body:
`bin/ci`'s gem audit fails since [GHSA-pq4g-8rxf-4g29](https://github.com/rgrove/crass/security/advisories/GHSA-pq4g-8rxf-4g29) reached ruby-advisory-db today: crass 1.0.7 is affected, 1.0.8 is patched. `bundle update --conservative crass` in both `Gemfile.lock` and `Gemfile.saas.lock`. Nothing else moves in either, the 1.0.8 checksum matches rubygems.org, `bin/bundle-drift check` is in sync, and `bin/bundler-audit check` passes for both Gemfiles. (`bin/bundle-drift correct` would have copied the SaaS lockfile over `Gemfile.lock`, putting crass back to 1.0.7 and moving surfguard, so the SaaS lockfile was bumped directly.) ## Fizzy was exposed The bug is in crass's tokenizer: a bad `url(` token didn't stop at a `)` that follows an escaped backslash, so crass swallowed more input than a browser does. Loofah's CSS scrubber, which rails-html-sanitizer uses for `style` attributes, is built on crass. Lexxy 1.0.1 adds `style` to `ActionText::ContentHelper.allowed_attributes`, and `config/initializers/sanitization.rb` keeps that list. So rich text a member writes, such as a comment body, gets its `style` through Loofah. On 1.0.7 this comes out of `sanitize_action_text_content` with the declarations intact: ```html
…
``` A browser ends the bad url at `\\)`, so it applies `position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0`, which is enough for a page-covering overlay. On 1.0.8 only the `width` survives. `test/helpers/rich_text_style_sanitization_test.rb` runs that payload through Action Text's sanitizer. It fails on 1.0.7 and passes on 1.0.8. ## Re-keying everything cached under 1.0.7 At Jeremy's call ("re-key all at rollout"): - **Server fragments and page ETags.** `ApplicationController::RENDERING_VERSION` (v2) goes into every fragment cache key and replaces the old `etag { "v1" }`. Comments and cards are cached by record, so the bump alone would have left their 1.0.7 renderings in place. Every fragment expires at once, so expect a cold-cache load at rollout. `test/controllers/rendering_version_test.rb` pins it. - **The service worker's offline pages.** The worker keeps pages for up to three days and replays them when the network fails, without the ETag check. It now carries `RENDERING_VERSION`. When the version changes, it clears every offline cache before taking over, and checks again whenever it starts, so a clear that failed or was interrupted is retried. It records the version only after a successful clear. Push and notifications are untouched. `test/controllers/pwa_controller_test.rb` pins the version in the rendered worker. [Changelog](https://github.com/rgrove/crass/blob/v1.0.8/HISTORY.md#108-2026-10-21) and [diff](https://github.com/rgrove/crass/compare/v1.0.7...v1.0.8): one tokenizer fix, no API or option changes. Same bump in basecamp/bc3#14073, basecamp/haystack#9081, basecamp/launchpad#961, basecamp/queenbee#1627 and basecamp/dash#1236.

title: HELD: Let the directory reviewer sign in with a fixed code (SaaS only, off unless configured)
body:
**Held. Draft for Jeremy.** Nothing lights until both env vars below are set on a destination.

## Why

The Claude and ChatGPT directories review a connector by signing in to it themselves, from fresh browsers, without access to an inbox. Fizzy signs in by magic link, emailed code or passkey. It has no password, so a reviewer stalls at "Check your email". The [Fizzy directory packet](https://app.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/48672814/documents/10430117938) lists this as a submission blocker. Option (a) there is shaped like [launchpad#930](https://github.com/basecamp/launchpad/pull/930), which exempted Basecamp's shared reviewer from suspicious-login email verification.

**What exists today:** App Store review signs in as a shared `@hey.com` identity. The 1Password item **Mobile → "App Store Review Fizzy"** holds its username, an empty password field (Fizzy has none), and "Instructions for App Review". Those tell the reviewer to enter the address in Fizzy, then sign in to that HEY mailbox with a password and read the emailed code. In other words, the reviewer is handed an inbox. Neither [fizzy-ios](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy-ios) nor [fizzy-android](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy-android) checks in review notes or fastlane `review_information`. Fizzy has no server-side bypass, no demo account path and no fixed code. Directories reject inbox handoff: they require a sign-in without an email code or magic link, and a reviewer can't be expected to operate a second product.

**Decision:** keep the fixed code, and point it at the **same** App Store review identity. Directory and store reviewers share one demo account, as Basecamp's `basecamp4appreview@hey.com` does under launchpad#930, and the mailbox is on hey.com, a domain we own, readable by whoever holds that item. Creating the identity needs no production write, because it already exists. Store reviewers can keep the inbox route, or use the code: the emailed code works either way.

## What

- **`Identity::ReviewerSignIn`** (SaaS only, `saas/app/models/identity/reviewer_sign_in.rb`). It names exactly one identity, by `FIZZY_REVIEWER_SIGN_IN_EMAIL`. That identity may enter a fixed code in place of the emailed one. Only the code's SHA-256 digest is configured, as `FIZZY_REVIEWER_SIGN_IN_CODE_DIGEST`; the code itself is never in the repo, the config or the tests. Both comparisons are constant-time. The code goes through `MagicLink::Code.sanitize` first, so it's typed like an emailed code: case-insensitive, `O`/`I`/`L` substituted.
- **The hook**, `Sessions::ReviewerSignIn`, is prepended onto `Sessions::MagicLinksController` by the SaaS engine and overrides only `invalid_code`. So it runs only after the emailed code didn't match. It runs behind the same `rate_limit to: 10, within: 15.minutes`, and only with a verified pending-authentication cookie for that same email address, set by entering it on the sign-in page. It then signs in through the controller's own `sign_in`, so the session, redirect and JSON response are the normal ones.
- **Every use** is recorded on the request's structured log line as `authentication.reviewer_sign_in.identity.id` (Loki; not subject to `RAILS_LOG_LEVEL=fatal`), and reported to Sentry as an info message with no identifier.
- **`bin/rails saas:reviewer_sign_in:sign_out`** ends every session of the configured identity, closes its live sockets, and removes its access tokens and passkeys. It needs only `FIZZY_REVIEWER_SIGN_IN_EMAIL`, so it still works after the digest is cleared to turn the code off. Run it on rotation so sessions started with the old code end too.
- **`bin/rails saas:reviewer_sign_in:generate`** prints a random 16-character code (80 bits, the emailed code's alphabet) and the `FIZZY_REVIEWER_SIGN_IN_CODE_DIGEST=` line.
- **The code field's `maxlength`** goes from 6 to 16 in `app/views/sessions/magic_links/show.html.erb`. That's the only change outside `saas/`. A 6-character code would be 30 bits, the only gate on that identity. Nothing auto-submits at 6 characters (`magic_link_controller.js` submits on Enter or paste), so normal sign-in is unchanged.

OSS installs never get it: the model, hook and task live in the SaaS engine.

## Threat model

For the configured identity, **the code is the only gate**, so its security is exactly the code's. That's deliberate, as in launchpad#930.
- **The identity:** a dedicated reviewer, for example `fizzyreview@` on a domain we own. It belongs to one comped, internal account ("Acme Design Co." in the packet's seed), with nothing else in reach.
- **Anyone holding the code** gets exactly what reviewers get. Rotate it after each review: generate a new one, replace the digest, deploy, then run `saas:reviewer_sign_in:sign_out`. The emailed code keeps working throughout.
- **Another identity:** no gain. The match requires the pending email (signed by the app's message verifier, set only by `SessionsController#create`) to equal the configured address, and the code to match its digest.
- **Brute force:** 80 bits behind 10 attempts per 15 minutes per IP.
- **Failing closed:** with either variable unset or blank, nothing changes. A blank code never matches, even against a blank code's digest. If the configured address has no identity, nothing happens.
- **Adding an identity** means changing an env var on a deploy, which takes deploy access.

## To light it

Done in this PR, with nothing deployed:
- Generated a 16-character code with `MagicLink::Code`, the same algorithm as `saas:reviewer_sign_in:generate`, and stored it in **Mobile → "App Store Review Fizzy"**, field **"Directory reviewer sign-in code"**. No value was printed.
- Stored **Deploy → Fizzy → Production → `FIZZY_REVIEWER_SIGN_IN_CODE_DIGEST`** (its SHA-256) and **`FIZZY_REVIEWER_SIGN_IN_EMAIL`** (copied from that item's username). A check confirmed the stored digest is the code's, and the email is the App Store username.
- `saas/.kamal/secrets.production` fetches both, and `deploy.production.yml` lists both under `env.secret`. The email is a secret, not `env.clear`, only because this repo is public. `kamal secrets fetch` resolves both fields.

**Merging and deploying this turns it on in production.** For Jeremy:
1. Confirm the App Store review identity belongs to exactly one comped, internal account, and seed that account for the directory test plan in the [packet](https://app.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/48672814/documents/10430117938). Check with `bin/kamal app exec -d production --reuse "bin/rails runner 'i = Identity.find_by!(email_address: ENV.fetch(%(FIZZY_REVIEWER_SIGN_IN_EMAIL))); p i.users.map { [_1.account.name, _1.role] }'"`.
2. `bin/rails saas:enable`, then `bin/kamal deploy -d production`.
3. Sign in from a private window at app.fizzy.do: enter the App Store review address, then type the "Directory reviewer sign-in code" from the 1Password item in the code field. Check Loki for the request line carrying `authentication.reviewer_sign_in`, and Sentry for the event.
4. Put the code in the directory review notes (Claude and ChatGPT test instructions), never in the repo.
5. After each review, rotate:
   1. Generate a new code.
   2. Replace both 1Password values.
   3. Deploy.
   4. Run `bin/kamal app exec -d production --reuse "bin/rails saas:reviewer_sign_in:sign_out"`.

   Then update the store review notes if they use the code.

## Tests

`saas/test/models/identity/reviewer_sign_in_test.rb` and `saas/test/controllers/sessions/reviewer_sign_in_test.rb` cover:
- the code signs the reviewer in;
- the emailed code still works;
- another identity is refused with the reviewer's code;
- a wrong code is refused;
- with no configuration, the code does nothing;
- the code is refused without a pending sign-in;
- blank input is refused;
- normalization and case-insensitive email matching;
- the generated code's length and alphabet;
- sign-out ends only the reviewer's sessions, and does nothing when unconfigured, and closes the identity's Action Cable connections.

Suites on `67b7fe3ce`, on thelio: SaaS MySQL 1994 tests with 1 error, `Search::ShardingTest` hitting a `StatementTimeout` at load average 19; it passed on rerun. OSS SQLite and OSS MySQL green, rubocop clean. GitHub CI: every test job green. `Security` fails on `bundler-audit` alone: crass 1.0.7, [GHSA-pq4g-8rxf-4g29](https://github.com/rgrove/crass/security/advisories/GHSA-pq4g-8rxf-4g29), published today, which fails main too and is unrelated to this PR.

title: Identify OAuth clients by their metadata document URL, from allowlisted hosts
body:
**Draft, held for Jeremy.** Stacked on #3192 (`oauth-token-digests`). Part of the hosted Fizzy MCP plan ([hosted-plan.md](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy-mcp-server/blob/edb1992/docs/hosted-plan.md), "Then CIMD"), alongside the audience and token-exchange lanes.

Claude and ChatGPT connectors identify themselves by a **Client ID Metadata Document**: the `client_id` is the https URL of a JSON document they host ([draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document/)). This lets them connect without dynamic registration. It's ported from bc3's `Oauth::ClientMetadata`, and covers the **recognized tier only**.

## Behaviour

- **Off unless configured.** `OAUTH_CIMD_ENABLED=true` turns it on, and only while issuance is on (`Oauth::Availability.metadata_documents_enabled?`). The metadata adds `client_id_metadata_document_supported: true` only while it's on, as bc3's does ([metadata_controller.rb#L107-L108](https://github.com/basecamp/bc3/blob/c2cebda3b57/app/controllers/oauth/metadata_controller.rb#L107-L108)). Without that member, clients fall back to DCR.
- **Allowlisted hosts only.** `OAUTH_CIMD_ALLOWED_HOSTS` is a space-separated list of exact hosts, for production `mcp.claude.ai claude.ai claude.com chatgpt.com`, the same four as bc3. These are environment values, not credentials (bc3#13306).
  - A URL client_id on any other host is an unknown client and is never fetched.
  - bc3's open tier (any https host, with heightened warnings and a per-domain row quota) isn't ported.
  - Development and test enable it with the same four hosts.
  - **Deploy (second commit):** `saas/config/deploy.yml` `env.clear` sets `OAUTH_CIMD_ALLOWED_HOSTS: "mcp.claude.ai claude.ai claude.com chatgpt.com"` for every SaaS destination (Kamal merges destination `env.clear` over the base). That alone fetches nothing: **it stays dark** until `OAUTH_CIMD_ENABLED=true`, which no destination sets. Turning it on is Jeremy's call.
- **Identifiers are exact strings.** `Oauth::ClientMetadata::Url` accepts:
  - https only, exact case;
  - a host and a path;
  - no query, fragment, userinfo or dot-segments;
  - at most 255 characters, the existing `client_id` width. Widening it would be a type change.

  `oauth_clients.client_id`'s MySQL collation folds case. So `Oauth::Client.find_presented` compares the stored id exactly after the lookup, and a case variant of a provisioned URL names no client.
- **Two modes**, since GETs read from a replica:
  - **Consent GET:** renders from a freshly fetched, unsaved client.
  - **Authorization POST:** provisions the row before any code is minted, as a public, untrusted, `client_id_metadata_document` client.
  - **Deny:** never registers a client. It uses the stored row when that row allows the redirect, and otherwise reads the document again without saving.
  - **Token and revocation endpoints:** only look rows up. A client site outage can't sign anyone out.
- **Document validation** (`Oauth::ClientMetadata::Document`):
  - the `client_id` member must exactly equal the URL;
  - no `client_secret*` members;
  - the client is provisioned public (`none`), including when it prefers another method but lists `none` in `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported` (ChatGPT does; the bc3#13578 lesson);
  - `grant_types`, if present, must include `authorization_code`; others are ignored;
  - `redirect_uris` is required, at most 10;
  - scopes narrow to `read`/`write`, and silence offers both;
  - the name is `client_name`, or the host.
- **Redirects:** a metadata document client is held to the self-registered rules, https or loopback, and gets an error redirect before consent only to loopback (`vetted_redirect?`).
- **Consent:** shows "Name set by the app at **host**".
- **Cleanup:** metadata document rows left without a grant for 30 days are swept with DCR clients. The next authorization provisions them again.
- **Caching:** the document's `Cache-Control`/`Expires`, clamped to between 5 minutes and 24 hours (default 1 hour). A stale row revalidates with `If-None-Match`, and a 304 extends it. Concurrent writers use a compare-and-swap on `metadata_fetched_at`, and a creation race adopts the winner through the unique index.
- **Fetch budgets, per person:** 6 per URL per minute and 60 per host per hour, counted in `Rails.cache` under the signed-in identity, failing open. **Deviation from bc3**, whose budgets are global: a consent GET fetches without provisioning, so anyone signed in could spend a shared budget and refuse a client's first authorization to everyone. The fetcher's bulkhead and deadline bound Fizzy's fetches overall, and answer a retryable 503 rather than refusing the client. A client already provisioned that is over budget keeps its stored document.
- **Only a string names a client:** a `client_id[]` array never reaches `find_by` as an `IN` list. A metadata document client is reachable only through its URL, so the switch, the exact comparison and the refresh always apply to it.

## The new outbound fetch: SSRF defences

This is new egress from Fizzy to URLs a client names, limited to the allowlisted hosts. `Oauth::ClientMetadata::Fetcher`, ported from bc3:

- **Address:** Surfguard resolves the host once under its strict `:iana_special_use` policy. That refuses private, loopback and link-local addresses, plus every IANA special-purpose range, including NAT64, AMT and AS112, which the default policy admits. An answer set that mixes public and blocked addresses is refused whole (`Surfguard.resolve_public_ip`). The connection is pinned to the address it admitted (`ipaddr`), so DNS rebinding can't move it.
- **No proxy:** the proxy argument is an explicit `nil`, so `HTTP(S)_PROXY` can't reroute the fetch.
- **No redirects.** TLS verifies the peer against the URL host.
- **Bounded:**
  - one 3s deadline, DNS to last byte, backstopped by `Timeout`;
  - 5KB body, checked by both `Content-Length` and streaming;
  - 16KB wire budget over the status line, headers and framing, enforced in `BudgetedIO#rbuf_fill`;
  - identity encoding only, so no decompression bombs;
  - JSON content types only;
  - `max_retries = 0`;
  - at most 2 concurrent fetches per process.
- **Results:** typed failures, never raises; a failure aborts the authorization (`invalid_client_metadata`, or 503 with `Retry-After` under pressure), and none is stored.
- **Kill switches:** for a fetch incident, set `OAUTH_CIMD_ENABLED` to anything else, or block egress. Clients already authorized keep refreshing.

## Migration (row 14 for the runbook)

`20261019150000` adds to `oauth_clients`, which is empty in production, in one bulk ALTER:

| Column | Type |
|---|---|
| `client_id_metadata_document` | boolean, default false, nullable |
| `metadata_fetched_at` | datetime |
| `metadata_expires_at` | datetime |
| `metadata_etag` | string(191) |

No foreign keys, no index, and no change to any existing column. The ALTER ran with an explicit `ALGORITHM=INSTANT` on MySQL 8.4 against the pre-migration table definition with a row in it.

## Not ported from bc3, on purpose

- **Open tier and `DomainQuota`:** not needed with an allowlist.
- **`FetchLease`, the cross-process site fetch slots:** the bulkhead, the budgets and the deadline bound it. Revisit if the allowlist widens.
- **Quarantine (`disable!`):** Fizzy has none. The allowlist and the switch are the containment.
- **Yabeda metrics:** #3204 is a sibling branch; outcomes are logged for now.
- **The SQLite busy retry:** single-writer SQLite installs get a 500 on a concurrent first provisioning instead of a retry.
- **The local-TLS integration test:** `BudgetedIO` is tested against a scripted io; the `on_connect` seam is asserted to exist.
- **`private_key_jwt` and PAR:** a document that offers only `private_key_jwt` is refused.

## Expected conflicts with the sibling lanes

- **Audience lane (B):**
  - `app/controllers/oauth/authorizations_controller.rb`: `set_client` and its new helpers, beside B's `resource` handling.
  - `app/views/oauth/authorizations/new.html.erb`: one `elsif` in the Application block, beside B's account picker.
  - `app/models/oauth/client.rb`: two scopes and three small methods.
- **Token-exchange lane (C):** `app/controllers/oauth/metadata_controller.rb`, one member in the `show` hash; C changes `grant_types_supported`.
- **Both lanes:**
  - `db/schema.rb` and `db/schema_sqlite.rb`: the version line and the `oauth_clients` block.
  - `config/environments/production.rb`: the OAuth block.
  - `app/models/oauth/availability.rb`: one method.

All of these are additive, so restacking should resolve by keeping both sides.

**The coming DCR allowlist lane** (`DCR_ALLOWED_HTTPS_HOSTS`, loopback, cursor/claude schemes) will share:

- `app/models/oauth/client.rb#validate_redirect_uri`: this PR makes metadata document clients follow the self-registered redirect rule (`self_registered?`). If DCR's rule narrows to an allowlist, decide whether metadata document clients follow it too. Their redirects are already bound to an allowlisted document host, so they probably shouldn't.
- `config/environments/production.rb` and `saas/config/deploy.yml` `env.clear`: neighbouring env lines.
- `app/models/oauth/availability.rb`, if DCR gets its own switch.

## Tests

On thelio at `67538b5a5` (before the review fixes; CI covers the head):

| Suite | Runs | Failures | Errors | Skips |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SaaS MySQL 8.4 | 2359 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| OSS SQLite | 2191 | 0 | 0 | 5 |
| OSS MySQL 8.4 | 2191 | 0 | 0 | 1 |

Rubocop is clean. The new tests run with outbound network disabled (`WebMock.disable_net_connect!`):

- `test/models/oauth/client_metadata/`: url, document, fetcher, budgeted_io, resolver
- `test/integration/oauth_client_metadata_documents_test.rb`
- additions to `test/models/oauth/client_test.rb`

The case-variant test branches on adapter: MySQL's case-folding collation refuses the variant's row, while SQLite gives it a separate row. Either way the variant never resolves to the original client.


## Third-party data flow

Resolving a metadata document makes Fizzy's server fetch a public JSON document from the app's own host when someone authorizes that app. Only allowlisted hosts are fetched (`OAUTH_CIMD_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, e.g. Claude's and ChatGPT's). The request is an anonymous GET of the URL the app published as its client_id. It carries no cookie, token, account or person identifier, and no part of the authorization request.

What the host can learn is timing: a fetch shows that someone, somewhere, began authorizing its app at about that moment (CIMD §9.1). Fetches are cached for the document's freshness lifetime, at least five minutes, so even that is coarse. The host is the vendor of the app the person chose to connect, and it learns that the connection completed anyway, from the code exchange. So no new party learns anything and no new subprocessor is involved. The flow is covered by the Trust & Compliance card [Fizzy OAuth: people can connect third-party apps to their Fizzy data](https://app.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/48697456/card_tables/cards/10415396286).

title: Accept self-registered redirects only on loopback, cursor:// and claude://, and allowlisted https hosts
body:
**Held for Jeremy. Draft; don't merge.** Stacked on #3192 (`oauth-token-digests`).

Dynamic client registration is open and unauthenticated. After #3080 it accepted an https callback on **any** host, so anyone could register a client that sends authorization codes to a host they chose; the consent screen was the only check. This tightens it to bc3's strict allowlist, the policy bc3 ran before bc3#13778 opened https (Jeremy's ruling for Fizzy).

## The rule

A self-registered client may name only:

| Redirect | Why it's safe for open registration | Source in bc3 |
|---|---|---|
| `http://127.0.0.1`, `http://[::1]`, `http://localhost`, any port (RFC 8252 §7.3) | served on the user's device | `LOOPBACK_ADDRESSES` |
| `cursor://…`, `claude://…` (RFC 8252 §7.1) | the OS hands it to an app on the user's device | `DCR_ALLOWED_CUSTOM_SCHEMES` |
| `https://` on a host in `OAUTH_DCR_ALLOWED_HTTPS_HOSTS` | a vetted vendor's callback; the consent screen stays the backstop | `DCR_ALLOWED_HTTPS_HOSTS` |

- **App schemes:** only `cursor` and `claude`. They must be hierarchical (`cursor://host/path`, never the opaque `cursor:path`, which can't carry `?code=`), with no userinfo or fragment, and must name a host or path. Dotted reverse-DNS schemes get no pass on shape, because some route to a remote handler (`z39.50r`, `iris.beep`), as bc3#13431 found. This is new for Fizzy: #3080 rejected every custom scheme for DCR.
- **The error is RFC 7591's `invalid_redirect_uri`.** One unallowed URI refuses the whole registration, and the description lists what's accepted, hosts included.
- **Existing clients are unaffected.** The host check runs only on hosts a write *adds* (`Oauth::Client#added_https_hosts_are_vetted`, run on create or when `redirect_uris` changes), never on hosts a client already holds. A client keeps saving and authorizing after its host leaves the list. Tests pin both.
- **Unchanged:** operator-provisioned clients (`dynamically_registered: false`) aren't held to the list, and neither are CIMD clients on `oauth-cimd`, which register with `dynamically_registered: false`. The pre-consent rule is also unchanged: errors for a self-registered client still render on Fizzy unless its redirect is loopback.

## Default host list (SaaS, `saas/config/deploy.yml`)

`OAUTH_DCR_ALLOWED_HTTPS_HOSTS: "claude.ai claude.com chatgpt.com www.cursor.com grok.com"`

| Host | Client | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `claude.ai` | Claude web connectors (`https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback`) | [bc3 `doc/oauth/production_light_up.md#L671`](https://github.com/basecamp/bc3/blob/7c0ea14124ca47789f8ab07c578aa28132c950d6/doc/oauth/production_light_up.md#L671) |
| `claude.com` | Claude (`https://claude.com/api/mcp/auth_callback`) | same line |
| `chatgpt.com` | ChatGPT connectors (`https://chatgpt.com/aip/g/oauth/callback`) | same line |
| `www.cursor.com` | Cursor desktop and cloud, and the Grok Bot through Cursor's client (`https://www.cursor.com/agents/mcp/oauth/callback`) | [bc3 `redirect_uris.rb` before #13778](https://github.com/basecamp/bc3/blob/1ce3d8d279434cbf88fb565f4c41be32270d1ba3/app/models/oauth/client/redirect_uris.rb#L61), `DCR_ALLOWED_HTTPS_HOSTS` |
| `grok.com` | Grok's native connector (`https://grok.com/connectors-oauth-exchange-code/`) | same constant |

bc3's list also held `muse.ai` and `agent.meta.ai`, for Meta's Muse. They're left out because the ruling named Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Grok. Adding them is one line in `deploy.yml`.

In bc3, Claude and ChatGPT reach the server through CIMD, not DCR. They're listed here because Fizzy's CIMD (`oauth-cimd`) isn't merged, and DCR is their fallback until it is (the directory packet: "OAuth with CIMD; DCR as the fallback").

## OSS and self-hosted: strict by default

Unset, `OAUTH_DCR_ALLOWED_HTTPS_HOSTS` allows **no** https host: only loopback and the two app schemes. A self-hoster who wants a hosted connector names its host. This mirrors bc3's positive model: an open-registration server shouldn't accept arbitrary remote sinks by default, and an install that never mentions DCR gets the safe posture. `config.x.oauth.dcr_allowed_https_hosts` is read in `production.rb` and `development.rb`, separated by spaces or commas. `test.rb` names `connector.example.com` so existing tests keep their https client.

## Expected conflicts

- **CIMD (`oauth-cimd`):** both PRs touch `app/models/oauth/client.rb` (validations, private helpers) and `app/controllers/oauth/clients_controller.rb`. CIMD clients aren't `dynamically_registered`, so the rules don't interact. Only the text conflicts.
- **B (#3213) and C (#3214):** both touch `Oauth::Client`. Expect small textual conflicts near the validations.
- **#3212 (consent design):** `connection_kind` groups by how a client registered. A `cursor://` or `claude://` app redirect should probably group with "on your devices", like loopback. Worth a line when the two meet.

## Tests

- New `test/integration/oauth_dcr_redirect_allowlist_test.rb` covers:
  - allowed and unallowed hosts, with the error;
  - one bad URI refusing the whole set;
  - no hosts configured;
  - the two app schemes accepted, others refused;
  - an app-scheme client's consent screen (its CSP names `cursor:`) and its code arriving at `cursor://…`;
  - a client whose host left the list still authorizing.
- `test/models/oauth/client_test.rb` covers:
  - adding a host only from the list;
  - keeping a removed host but not adding another;
  - operator clients exempt;
  - accepted and refused app schemes, including `z39.50r`, `iris.beep`, `javascript`, opaque `cursor:callback`, userinfo and a fragment.
- **Mutation check:** with both the controller's and the model's host checks disabled, 6 tests fail.
- **Locally (OSS SQLite):** 185 tests in the OAuth model and flow files pass, 0 failures. Rubocop is clean.
- **thelio:** the full suites are running. Results follow in a comment.



## Third-party data flow

A person who authorizes the Cursor or Claude desktop app via `cursor://` or `claude://` sends an authorization code for their own Fizzy data to that app, on their device. This is the flow the Trust & Compliance card [Fizzy OAuth: people can connect third-party apps to their Fizzy data](https://app.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/48697456/card_tables/cards/10415396286) covers. No new subprocessor: Fizzy sends nothing to Cursor or Anthropic itself. This PR narrows the flow overall, from any https callback (#3080) to on-device callbacks, these two schemes, and operator-listed https hosts.

title: Update crass to 1.0.8 (GHSA-pq4g-8rxf-4g29)
body:
**Held for Jeremy's merge word.**

This updates `crass` from 1.0.7 to 1.0.8 for [GHSA-pq4g-8rxf-4g29](https://github.com/rgrove/crass/security/advisories/GHSA-pq4g-8rxf-4g29): "Incorrect tokenization of bad URLs enables CSS sanitizer bypass". The fixed version is 1.0.8 or later. `crass` reaches Fizzy through `loofah`, which is behind `rails-html-sanitizer`.

The advisory entered ruby-advisory-db on 2026-10-23, at commit `03da937a9e`. Since then, `bin/bundler-audit check --update` fails the Security check on every Fizzy branch, for example on #3228.

The bump is `bundle update crass --conservative`, run for both `Gemfile.lock` and `Gemfile.saas.lock`. Only `crass` moves, in two lines per lockfile. Both lockfiles have to change together, because the Gemfile drift check (`bin/bundle-drift check`) fails when they differ.

Checked locally:
- `bin/bundle-drift check`: the two lockfiles are in sync.
- `bin/bundler-audit check --update`: no vulnerabilities found.

title: Bump sqlite3 from 2.9.6 to 2.10.0
body:
Bumps [sqlite3](https://github.com/sparklemotion/sqlite3-ruby) from 2.9.6 to 2.10.0.
Release notes

Sourced from sqlite3's releases.

2.10.0 / 2026-10-13

Dependencies

  • Vendored sqlite is updated to v3.54.0 (from v3.53.2). #750 @​flavorjones

    Notable changes in this version include:

    • ALTER TABLE now raises an error when adding, renaming, or dropping a column named ROWID, _ROWID_, or OID.
    • The authorizer callback is now invoked for SQL functions in the DEFAULT clauses of CREATE TABLE statements.
    • SQLite no longer supports Windows XP or earlier. On Windows, the precompiled gem and any installation that compiles the vendored sqlite now require Windows Vista or later.

Added

  • ResultSet#each and #each_hash return an Enumerator when called without a block. Previously they raised LocalJumpError. #656 @​kch
  • Introduce Database#serialize, which returns a database as a binary string, and Database#deserialize, which replaces a database with the contents of such a string. These wrap sqlite3_serialize() and sqlite3_deserialize(). Both methods are defined only when SQLite was compiled without SQLITE_OMIT_DESERIALIZE, and Database#deserialize also requires that the loaded SQLite is v3.54.0 or later. An image of a database in WAL mode cannot be queried after deserializing; see the Database#deserialize documentation. #685 @​Maaarcocr

Fixed

  • Fix Database#statement_timeout= interrupting statements almost immediately instead of after the timeout elapsed, including re-executed prepared statements and calls to Database#execute_batch2. #737 @​palkan @​flavorjones

Improved

  • On CRuby, Statement#types allocates fewer strings. Each declared type is downcased and interned in C, instead of allocating two strings per column. #743 @​jhawthorn

Changed

  • ResultSet#each and #each_hash return the result set when called with a block. As a consequence, Database#execute and #execute2 called with a block return the closed ResultSet instead of nil. #656 @​kch
  • Statement#columns and Statement#types return frozen arrays, and the strings in Statement#types are frozen. Code that mutates them now raises FrozenError. #743 @​jhawthorn
  • Statement#column_decltype and Statement#types return UTF-8 strings. Previously they returned ASCII-8BIT strings. #743 @​jhawthorn

    • The authorizer callback is now invoked for SQL functions in the DEFAULT clauses of CREATE TABLE statements.
    • SQLite no longer supports Windows XP or earlier. On Windows, the precompiled gem and any installation that compiles the vendored sqlite now require Windows Vista or later.

Added

  • ResultSet#each and #each_hash return an Enumerator when called without a block. Previously they raised LocalJumpError. #656 @​kch
  • Introduce Database#serialize, which returns a database as a binary string, and Database#deserialize, which replaces a database with the contents of such a string. These wrap sqlite3_serialize() and sqlite3_deserialize(). Both methods are defined only when SQLite was compiled without SQLITE_OMIT_DESERIALIZE, and Database#deserialize also requires that the loaded SQLite is v3.54.0 or later. An image of a database in WAL mode cannot be queried after deserializing; see the Database#deserialize documentation. #685 @​Maaarcocr

Fixed

  • Fix Database#statement_timeout= interrupting statements almost immediately instead of after the timeout elapsed, including re-executed prepared statements and calls to Database#execute_batch2. #737 @​palkan @​flavorjones

Improved

  • On CRuby, Statement#types allocates fewer strings. Each declared type is downcased and interned in C, instead of allocating two strings per column. #743 @​jhawthorn

Changed

  • ResultSet#each and #each_hash return the result set when called with a block. As a consequence, Database#execute and #execute2 called with a block return the closed ResultSet instead of nil. #656 @​kch
  • Statement#columns and Statement#types return frozen arrays, and the strings in Statement#types are frozen. Code that mutates them now raises FrozenError. #743 @​jhawthorn

Release notes

Sourced from webmock's releases.

3.34.0

  • Allow with(query: :any) to match any query string (#1099)

    stub_request(:get, "www.example.com").with(query: :any) matches requests with any query string, or none. RSpec's anything works the same way. Previously, this raised NoMethodError, and you had to write with(query: hash_including({})).

    Use a URL without query parameters when passing query: :any. Otherwise, WebMock raises ArgumentError.

    Thanks to nightpool

  • Raise a clear ArgumentError for an unsupported query option

    Previously, a value such as with(query: :all) raised NoMethodError (undefined method split). The new error lists the supported values.

  • Show anything for keys given without a value to hash_including or hash_excluding outside RSpec

    Previously, with Minitest or Test::Unit, messages showed #<WebMock::Matchers::AnyArgMatcher:0x...>, for example for with(query: hash_including(:a)). RSpec's own matchers already showed anything.

  • Provide HTTP_HOST to to_rack apps when the client has not supplied a Host header (#1084)

    Previously, requests from some HTTP clients reached the Rack app without HTTP_HOST. This caused host checks such as Sinatra's HostAuthorization to see an empty host.

    WebMock now fills in the host from the request URL, including the port when it is not the default. An explicit Host header is preserved.

    Thanks to Benoit Tigeot

  • Fix Rack compatibility for to_rack apps

    The request environment now passes Rack::Lint.

    SERVER_PORT and CONTENT_LENGTH are now strings. If your app or tests read them directly, use string comparisons, such as env['SERVER_PORT'] == "80". The environment also includes SERVER_PROTOCOL.

    CONTENT_TYPE is omitted when the request has no content type. The Content-Length header is passed only as CONTENT_LENGTH, without an extra HTTP_CONTENT_LENGTH entry. Transfer-Encoding is removed because the body has already been decoded.

    Repeated header values are joined into one string. Header values and the body read from rack.input now use binary (ASCII-8BIT) strings.

3.33.0

  • Return effective_url as a String for stubbed Typhoeus responses (#869)

    Previously, this was an Addressable::URI. If your code calls methods such as effective_url.host, parse the returned string into a URI first.

    The URL keeps the request's port, query order and encoding. It follows curl's formatting: for example, http://example.com:80 becomes http://example.com:80/. Stubbed timeouts now provide an effective_url too.

    Thanks to Tom Brammar

  • Fix incorrect removal of default ports from displayed URLs

    WebMock could accidentally remove :80 or :443 from a URL's path or query. For example, an error message could show /foo/bar instead of /foo:80/bar.

    Only the host's default port is now removed. This also works when the port is immediately followed by a query string, as in http://example.com:80?a=b.

title: Re-key cached rich text past crass 1.0.7
body:
Follow-up to #3226, which merged the crass 1.0.8 bump for [GHSA-pq4g-8rxf-4g29](https://github.com/rgrove/crass/security/advisories/GHSA-pq4g-8rxf-4g29) before this re-key landed on its branch.

Comments and cards are fragment-cached by record, so the bump alone leaves anything rendered under 1.0.7, smuggled `style` declarations included, in the cache until it expires. At Jeremy's call ("re-key all at rollout"):

- **Server fragments and page ETags.** `ApplicationController::RENDERING_VERSION` (v2) goes into every fragment cache key and replaces `etag { "v1" }`. Every fragment expires at once, so expect a cold-cache load at rollout. `test/controllers/rendering_version_test.rb` pins it, and it fails without the change.
- **The service worker's offline pages.** The worker replays cached pages when the network fails or is slow, with no ETag check, and turbo-offline doesn't check `maxAge` on those fallback reads. The worker now carries `RENDERING_VERSION`. When the version changes, activation clears every offline cache and then records the new version. An active worker checks again whenever it starts, so a clear that failed or was cut short is retried. An installing worker doesn't, because the previous worker is still serving then and a page it writes after the clear would be recorded as current. Firefox has no `self.serviceWorker`, so it skips the startup retry and relies on activation. Push and notifications are untouched. `test/controllers/pwa_controller_test.rb` pins the version in the rendered worker. The lifecycle was checked against simulated cache APIs: first install, same-version restart, version change, a rejected clear then restart, and an old worker's late write during install.

**Not doing:** blocking offline reads until a clear is confirmed. That would mean wrapping turbo-offline's fetch handling. The remaining window needs a clear that keeps failing on every start, plus a network failure, for a reader who opened a page planted before the deploy.

title: Ruby 4.0.9
body:
## Motivation

[Ruby 4.0.9](https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/news/2026/10/23/regexp-fixes-for-gitlab-cves/) carries the Onigmo fix for CVE-2026-110264 ([ruby/ruby#16801](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/16801)), which 4.0.8 lacks. Fizzy's own code compiles no regexp from unescaped user input: the signup name, the one user string interpolated into a pattern, goes through `Regexp.escape`. This bump is defense in depth.

## Details

- Set Ruby 4.0.9 in `.ruby-version`, both lockfiles, `Dockerfile`, `saas/Dockerfile` and `saas/hotcell/Dockerfile`, all on the stock `ruby:4.0.9-slim` image.
- Re-pin the hotcell accessory in `saas/config/deploy.yml` to `fizzy-hotcell:bb21fd4fefd5`, which `saas/hotcell/bin/build` built from the new Dockerfile.
- Update `ruby/setup-ruby` from v1.333.0 to [v1.334.0](https://github.com/ruby/setup-ruby/releases/tag/v1.334.0). v1.333.0 lists no Ruby 4.0.9 build.

## Additional information

The new hotcell image is built but not pushed to the registry. `saas/hotcell/bin/check` pushes it at deploy time when the registry lacks it.

Same shape as [#2173 Ruby 4.0.8](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/pull/2173). Tracked on the [App Security card](https://app.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/1666/card_tables/cards/10433170477).

title: HELD: Refuse docker-dev's shared default port in a git worktree
body:
**Held for Jeremy. Don't merge without his word.**

On 2026-10-23 at 19:40Z, an agent's test run in a git worktree on thelio, with `FIZZY_DB_PORT` unset, ran `db:test:prepare` against docker-dev's shared MySQL (`app-dev-mysql84-1`, 127.0.0.1:33384). It dropped `fizzy_test` and `fizzy_saas_test` and reloaded them from its branch's schema. An earlier run the same day reached the same server and failed at connect, before any purge.

## The guard

`saas/config/database.yml` defaults the port of every development and test database to 33384, docker-dev's MySQL. Every checkout of this repo uses the same database names there: `fizzy_development`, `fizzy_test`, `fizzy_saas_test` and the rest. Now a **git worktree** (where `.git` is a file) with `FIZZY_DB_PORT` unset refuses to load the config in development or test:

> FIZZY_DB_PORT is not set in this git worktree (…). The default, 33384, is docker-dev's MySQL, whose fizzy_development and fizzy_test the main checkout and every other worktree share; db:test:prepare here would reset them. Set FIZZY_DB_PORT to this worktree's own MySQL, or to 33384 to share docker-dev's on purpose.

**Why a worktree is the discriminator.** It's what the incident looked like, and it's a real collision even on a developer's own Mac. A worktree on the default port migrates, purges and reloads the main checkout's databases, and those of every other worktree. It isn't specific to agents or to thelio. The main checkout, the common case, keeps the default and needs no env. A developer who wants a worktree on docker-dev's databases anyway sets `FIZZY_DB_PORT=33384`.

**Why not test env or db tasks only.** `bin/rails db:test:prepare` without `RAILS_ENV` runs with `Rails.env` = development. That's exactly the incident's command. A guard keyed on `Rails.env.test?` or on the task would miss it. A worktree on the default port also migrates the shared `fizzy_development` from its branch, which is the same harm. So the check covers `Rails.env.local?`, meaning development and test.

**Deployed environments are untouched.** The check is under `Rails.env.local?`, and images exclude `/.git/` anyway (`.dockerignore`). Production, staging and beta keep `default`'s 3306 behaviour and never read `.git`. CI sets `FIZZY_DB_PORT: 3306` (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) and checks out a full clone, not a worktree.

## Not covered

- A second **full clone**, or the **main checkout itself**, run by an agent or a script on a shared machine: `.git` is a directory there, so the default stands. This guard bounds the worktree case. A shared machine running many checkouts still needs each run to name its port, as the lanes now do.
- **OSS MySQL** (`config/database.mysql.yml`, `MYSQL_PORT`, default 3306): no shared server on that port was involved, so it's left alone.
- A wrong **explicit** port: the guard checks only that a port was named.

## Proof

- `saas/test/lib/database_config_test.rb` renders the file under a stubbed `Rails.root`, `Rails.env` and `FIZZY_DB_PORT`, with 5 tests:
  1. a worktree with the port unset refuses in development and test;
  2. a worktree with the port set uses it;
  3. a worktree naming 33384 shares on purpose;
  4. the main checkout keeps 33384 with no env;
  5. production, staging and beta never raise.
  
  Against `main`'s `database.yml`, the refusal test fails.
- On thelio, in a worktree, on this lane's own MySQL (`portguard-mysql`, 33541):
  - `env -u FIZZY_DB_PORT bin/rails db:test:prepare` exits 1 with the message above, before connecting anywhere;
  - `FIZZY_DB_PORT=33541 bin/rails db:test:prepare` succeeds;
  - the new test passes: 5 tests, 0 failures.

title: Refuse an OAuth parameter that arrives as a list where one value is meant
body:
**Held for Jeremy. Draft, stacked on #3192 (`oauth-token-digests`).** It moves no converged train head.

## The bug

Codex found this on #3228 (CIMD), and the CIMD lane fixed its own path there. The same class sits on the train itself. A `name[]=` form field, or a JSON array or object, reaches `params` as an Array or a nested `Parameters`. Handed to `Oauth::Client.find_by(client_id: params[:client_id])` ([authorizations_controller.rb#L74 at 617edb87b](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/617edb87b003055875ee3fc20d584e9be246f8e9/app/controllers/oauth/authorizations_controller.rb#L74)), an Array becomes an SQL `IN` list. So `client_id[]=<id>` found the client it named, getting past the exact-string comparison that every later check assumes.

## The fix

`Oauth::BaseController` names the parameters that carry one value (RFC 6749 §3.1). Each endpoint refuses any of them that arrives as anything but a string or a JSON null:
- **When:** after the endpoint's availability gate, so a dark server still answers 404, and before any lookup.
- **Error:** `invalid_request`, or `invalid_client_metadata` at registration.
- **A JSON null passes through:** each endpoint already treats it as absent. For a refresh, a null `scope` still means "no scope" and `invalid_grant` follows.

`wrap_parameters false` for OAuth controllers. Rails copied every JSON body under the controller's name, and for the token endpoint that's `token`, which is itself an OAuth parameter.

| Endpoint | Refused when not a string | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| Authorize, GET and the consent POST | `client_id`, `redirect_uri` | Before the client lookup, on Fizzy's own error page; never redirected, since the target is the thing that can't be validated |
| | `response_type`, `code_challenge`, `code_challenge_method`, `scope`, `state` (and `resource`, `account_id` once #3213 is below) | Once the redirect target is validated: an error redirect to a vetted client, the local page otherwise, like every other authorize error |
| Token | `grant_type`, `code`, `code_verifier`, `redirect_uri`, `refresh_token`, `client_id`, `scope` (and the exchange's `subject_token`, `subject_token_type`, `requested_token_type`, `audience`, `resource` once #3214 is below) | `invalid_request` |
| Revocation | `token`, `token_type_hint`, `client_id` | `invalid_request` |
| Registration | any of the names above; `scope` stays a permitted list (`validated_scopes`) | `invalid_client_metadata` |

**Not changed:**
- `client_secret` stays with `Oauth::ClientAuthentication`. A non-string secret already fails there as `invalid_client`, which `oauth_flow_test.rb` pins.
- The rest of registration's metadata (`redirect_uris` and `grant_types` lists, `token_endpoint_auth_method`, `client_name`) is validated by `ClientsController`'s own checks, as before.

## What it doesn't cover

- **Parameters read outside `app/controllers/oauth`:** `My::AccessTokensController` (PATs), Connected Apps' revoke (a route id), API bearer authentication (the Authorization header), sessions.
- **The Basic header:** parsed separately in `ClientAuthentication`, and only ever a string.
- **The denial's `error`:** only compared to `"access_denied"`.
- **A repeated bare `resource=a&resource=b`:** Rack keeps the last value as a String, so this check can't see it. #3213's `single_resource?` raw count stays the guard for that.

## Tests

`test/integration/oauth_single_valued_parameters_test.rb` has 11 tests. 7 fail at 617edb87b; the other 4 pin behaviour that was already right (an array `redirect_uri`, dark-server 404, the token endpoint's string `client_id`, a refresh's null `scope`).
- **The `IN`-list case:** `client_id[]` at authorize GET, at the consent POST, at the token endpoint and at revocation, each asserted with `assert_no_queries_match(/oauth_clients/)`. Nothing touches the clients table before the refusal.
- **Arrays and objects** in every other authorize parameter: an error redirect for a vetted client, the local page for a self-registered one.
- **Token, revocation and registration** arrays, including registration still taking `scope` as a list.

The existing OAuth suites pass unchanged: 326 tests, 0 failures, OSS SQLite on the Mac. Full suites on thelio are below.

## Expected conflicts

- **#3213 (B):** both add private methods to `Oauth::BaseController`. Adjacent, no overlap. `resource` and `account_id` are covered here once B is underneath; B's raw `resource` count stays.
- **#3214 (C):** `TokensController`'s `before_action` list. Its exchange parameters are covered with no change once stacked.
- **#3228 (CIMD):** `AuthorizationsController#set_client`. CIMD's own "only a single string names a client" check can go once this lands; this runs first.
- **#3229 (DCR allowlist):** `ClientsController`'s `before_action` list. Adjacent.

title: Scope webhook dispatch by account as well as board
body:
`Event::WebhookDispatchJob` finds the webhooks for an event through `Webhook.triggered_by`, which matched on `board_id` alone. A webhook row in one account whose `board_id` names another account's board would receive that board's card and comment payloads at its own URL.

Nothing writes such a row today. The account importer is the only path that sets `board_id` from outside, and `Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet#check_associations_dont_exist` refuses any foreign key that names an existing record. That is an import-validity check, though, in code that changes often, and no test pinned it for a plain `belongs_to`. One edit there would turn it into cross-account delivery. So this is a guard against a regression, not a fix for a live hole.

## Change

- `Webhook.triggered_by` matches on the event's account as well as its board (`app/models/webhook/triggerable.rb`). The existing `board_id` index still leads the lookup.
- `test/jobs/event/webhook_dispatch_job_test.rb`: a webhook in another account that points at the event's board gets no delivery (fails without the fix); a same-account webhook still gets one.
- `record_set_test.rb`: the importer refuses a webhook pointing at an existing board in another account. It passes today; it is there to pin that refusal (it fails if the existing-record check is removed).

## Other webhook paths checked

- Webhooks, activations and deliveries controllers go through `@board.webhooks`, where `@board` comes from `Current.user.boards`. A planted foreign row would show up in the victim board's admin list, which reveals the planter's own URL to the victim and nothing of the victim's to anyone; with dispatch scoped, the row is inert. Left as is.
- `Webhook::Delivery` and its payloads render the delivery's own event. Deliveries are created only by `Webhook#trigger` (now account-scoped) or by import, which refuses an existing `event_id` or `webhook_id`.
- Events keep `account == board.account`: card moves between boards stay within an account, and nothing moves a board between accounts.

## Verification

- Targeted tests (webhook models, dispatch job, record set): 51 runs, 0 failures; the dispatch test fails with the scope reverted, and the importer test fails with the existing-record check disabled.
- A separate adversarial review of the diff (event/board account agreement, controller and delivery paths, import paths, index use) found nothing.
- `bin/ci` signs off on the head.

title: Use Ruby's GC defaults and log job memory
body:
## Motivation

`saas/Dockerfile` sets `RUBY_GC_HEAP_{0..4}_INIT_SLOTS`, `RUBY_GC_MALLOC_LIMIT` and `RUBY_GC_MALLOC_LIMIT_MAX` from Autotuner recommendations made on Ruby 3.4.7. Fizzy now runs Ruby 4.0.9 ([#3234 Ruby 4.0.9](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/pull/3234)), and nobody has tuned these values for it. Dash jobs ran out of memory after the same upgrade. Removing Dash's old GC overrides cut job RSS by 23% in a beta probe ([basecamp/dash#1243](https://github.com/basecamp/dash/pull/1243)).

## Details

- Remove the GC env vars from the SaaS image and keep `LD_PRELOAD` for jemalloc. The OSS `Dockerfile` sets no GC vars.
- Port Dash's `Memory::Stats` to the SaaS engine. With `LOG_JOB_MEMORY=true`, every job's structured log line gets `performance.memory` (RSS) and `performance.gc` (heap slots, allocations, minor and major GC counts, old-malloc growth, GC time, last major trigger), as totals and as deltas across the job. The deltas are process-wide, so they include other jobs that ran on the same process at the same time.
- Set `LOG_JOB_MEMORY=true` on beta jobs, as Dash does. Production stays off until someone adds it to the production jobs role in `saas/config/deploy.production.yml`.
- Document it under "Job memory diagnostics" in `saas/README.md`.

## Additional information

Watch web and jobs RSS, GC time and p95 latency after deploy. The Autotuner gem stays, so it can recommend values for Ruby 4.

title: Lock the reviewer's email address so revocation can't be bypassed
body:
This fixes a revocation bypass in the reviewer sign-in from #3227, which is merged but not lit. Land it before the light-up.

## The bypass

The finding was raised by Codex on #3192: [thread](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/pull/3192#discussion_r4368449999). With a normal session from the reviewer code, a code holder can request an email change to an address they control and confirm it. An email change doesn't rename an identity. [`User#change_email_address`](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/bd7ee27b8/app/models/user/email_address_changeable.rb#L33-L38) moves the **user** to another identity, found or created for the new address. The demo account's membership then belongs to the code holder's own identity, which signs in by emailed code like anyone else. `saas:reviewer_sign_in:sign_out` cleans the configured identity, which no longer holds anything, so the code holder keeps the account after rotation.

## The fix: lock the address, don't chase it

- **`User::ReviewerEmailAddressLock`**, prepended onto `User` in the SaaS engine. For the reviewer's users, `send_email_address_change_confirmation` sends nothing and `change_email_address` returns `false`. That second guard also refuses a confirmation link minted earlier, and `Users::EmailAddresses::ConfirmationsController` already answers `false` with its invalid-token response.
- **`Users::ReviewerEmailAddressLock`**, included into `Users::EmailAddressesController`. It refuses `new` and `create` up front: a redirect with "This email address can't be changed", or `403` as JSON. The API path is refused too.
- **Why this obviates pinning to an id.** The reviewer is a comped internal identity, so nobody needs to change its email. Once its users can't move, the configured email always finds the identity, and the identity always holds the membership. No code path writes `Identity#email_address`; the only one is this move. So recording the identity's id at generate time would add a config value and a production lookup, and protect against nothing that's still possible.

## The same class, closed in the same pass

I asked what else could leave a code holder a way back in after rotation, beyond the email instance:
- **Pending session transfers.** `Identity::Transfer` tokens live for 4 hours and mint a session. Sign-out now deletes them.
- **The account join code.** Any member can read it (`Account::JoinCodesController#show` has no admin check), and redeeming it adds a user under an identity of the code holder's own. Sign-out now resets the join codes of the reviewer's accounts, so a code read during a review stops working at rotation.

**Decided by Jeremy (2026-10-24): (a).** A code holder who redeemed the join code during a review has their own user in the demo account, and rotation doesn't remove it. So the members are checked after each review: `saas:reviewer_sign_in:sign_out` now also prints every active member of the reviewer's accounts (`Identity::ReviewerSignIn.members_of_reviewer_accounts`, 65bb7f0a4). Deactivate anyone there who isn't the reviewer or the account's own staff.
- **(b) rejected:** the reviewer keeps its role, because reviewers need Fizzy's full functionality.
- **(c) rejected:** it would build machinery for a seeded demo account.

**Rotation after each review:** the operational steps live in the internal reviewer runbook, not here. Sign-out's member list is the step that catches anyone who joined during the review.

## Tests

`saas/test/models/user/reviewer_email_address_lock_test.rb` holds the test the finding asked for:
- The reviewer tries to move its user to an attacker address with a confirmation token.
- That's refused, the user stays on the reviewer identity, and no identity is created for the attacker address.
- Sign-out still ends the reviewer's sessions.
- The code doesn't authenticate under the attacker address.

Other coverage:
- No confirmation email is sent.
- Other users can still change their address.
- Nothing is locked when the feature is unconfigured.

`saas/test/controllers/users/reviewer_email_address_lock_test.rb`:
- Requesting a change is refused, as HTML and as JSON, with no mail.
- A minted confirmation link answers `422`, and the user doesn't move.

`saas/test/models/identity/reviewer_sign_in_test.rb`:
- Sign-out deletes transfers.
- Sign-out resets the reviewer's accounts' join codes and no others.

**Mutation checks:**
- With the two engine lines removed, the lock tests fail (4 failures, 1 error).
- With the transfer and join-code lines removed, the sign-out tests fail (2 failures).

The existing email-change tests pass unchanged.



## Review round on 65bb7f0a4, and where this control stops

Codex raised three findings on 65bb7f0a4:
- **Fixed in 357bd4632:** the app refuses to deactivate the reviewer's users, so the account can't drop out of sign-out's reach.
- **Fixed in 357bd4632:** the member audit prints escaped values.
- **Declined:** a join-code redemption racing the reset. The window is milliseconds inside one server-side request, at a moment the client can't see. A general `Account::JoinCode#redeem_if` fix would belong on main.

These are the fourth and fifth ways back in that we've found, after the email change and the join code. Each new one fixes another path by which a code holder keeps a membership in the demo account. **The protected thing is a seeded demo account with no customer data.** The code reaches nothing else, because the identity belongs only to that account. The controls here are bounded to the paths that move or add a membership:
- email change;
- self- or peer-deactivation;
- transfer tokens;
- join codes, reset at rotation;
- the after-review member list.

**Accepted residual:** a determined code holder may keep access to the demo account until someone notices them in the member list. A further finding of the same kind should be weighed against that residual, not patched by reflex.

title: Switch the MySQL adapter from Trilogy to mysql2
body:
## Motivation

Migrating back to mysql2. https://app.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/1666/card_tables/cards/10439628795

## Details

- `Gemfile`: `mysql2 (~> 0.5)` replaces `trilogy`. `config/database.mysql.yml` and `saas/config/database.yml`: `adapter: mysql2`. mysql2 0.5.7 connects in `utf8mb4` by default, as Trilogy does.
- Code that named the Trilogy adapter now names Mysql2:
  - the UUID type registration, its lookups in `MysqlUuidAdapter` and `Board::Accessible`, and the load hook in `config/initializers/uuid_primary_keys.rb`
  - the sharded-search check in `Search::Record`
  - `ActiveRecordSqlRedaction`, which reads a server error's number from `Mysql2::Error#error_number`. A new test checks that a MySQL server error keeps only its code.
- `saas/config/database.yml` names `username: root` for development and test. With no username, mysql2 connects as the OS user.
- Remove `lib/rails_ext/active_record_trilogy_quote_string.rb`, which matched Trilogy's quoting to mysql2's.
- `test/lib/database_adapter_test.rb` checks, in MySQL mode, the adapter, a utf8mb4 round trip, and that `binary(16)` columns are UUIDs.
- Both Dockerfiles install `libmariadb-dev` to build and `libmariadb3` to run. The test workflow installs `libmysqlclient-dev`, and the Brewfile adds `mysql-client`.

## Additional information

What changes for a self-hosted install on MySQL:

- An install without Docker needs the MySQL client library (`libmysqlclient`, or MariaDB Connector/C) to build mysql2.
- In the Docker image, mysql2 links MariaDB Connector/C. `MYSQL_SSL_MODE=disabled`, `required` and `verify_identity` work as before. `verify_ca` gives a warning and no certificate check.
- With no `connect_timeout` set, mysql2 waits up to 120 seconds to connect. The OSS config sets none, as before.

The macOS build of mysql2 against Homebrew's `mysql-client` is not checked.

title: Import an export that lacks a column this database has only just gained
body:
The account importer requires every column of a record's table. When a migration adds a nullable column, every export made before it fails its check as soon as the migration runs, even before any code reads the column.

The OAuth train adds `webhooks.creator_id` and `webhooks.created_via_id` (20261006130100, #3169). beta1 shares production's database, so running that migration from beta1 would make production reject every account import that carries a webhook. Main's suite against the migrated schema reproduces it: `RecordSetTest#test_check_rejects_a_webhook_that_points_at_an_existing_board_in_another_account` fails with `missing required fields: created_via_id, creator_id`.

**Change**
- `RecordSet` takes `optional_attributes:`. An export may lack them, and they import as null.
- Only the ones that are columns in this database count. Naming a column before its migration runs changes nothing: it isn't required, and it isn't inserted.
- `Manifest` names the two webhook columns as optional. Imports therefore pass on either side of 20261006130100.
- #3169's own importer change (4fab82da8) can then build on this; it leaves `created_via_id` behind.

**Tests:** optional attributes only count where they're columns; a missing non-optional attribute is still rejected; a record lacking an optional attribute checks and imports it as null; the manifest's webhook record set imports a webhook that predates both columns. On this branch the webhook columns don't exist yet. The integration branch runs the same tests with them migrated.

title: Fix public pages to the HTML format
body:
Public board and card routes only produce HTML, but extensionless requests still let request headers select the implicit render format. Give the public namespace an HTML route default so every extensionless public URL returns the complete public document regardless of `Accept` or `X-Requested-With`.

This keeps the 30-second public cache on one representation per URL. Cloudflare now supports `Vary` when explicitly enabled in a Cache Rule, but Fizzy's current rule has no `Vary` setting, so an origin header alone is insufficient. An explicit extension such as `.json` still overrides the default and remains explicit.

Validation:

- New regression on the untouched base: fails because an XHR-shaped request returns the template without `body.public`
- All public-controller tests: 13 tests, 42 assertions, green
- Full non-system suite: 1,801 tests, 6,865 assertions, green (5 skips)
- RuboCop: 2 files, clean
- Route recognition: extensionless URL has `format: :html`; `.json` has `format: "json"`
- Generated public URLs remain extensionless

title: Filter presigned storage signatures from logs
body:
Presigned storage URLs were logged with their `X-Amz-Signature`, which makes the logged URL a working link to the file until it expires. Three log lines carried it:

- Action Controller's `Redirected to …` line, for a redirect to storage
- the structured request line's redirect location (SaaS), which filters with the same `filter_parameters`
- Active Storage's `Generated URL for file at key: … (…)` debug line, for every URL it generates, direct uploads included

**Change**

- `signature` joins the credentials in `filter_parameters`. Both redirect lines filter the location's query through that list.
- Active Storage's structured event skips payload filtering, so `lib/rails_ext/active_storage_log_subscriber_filtered_urls.rb` filters the URL's query pair by pair with the same filter before `ActiveStorage::LogSubscriber#service_url` logs it, as Action Dispatch does for a redirect. Only the logged copy changes.

**Tests** (all four fail without the change)

- `test/lib/rails_ext/active_storage_log_subscriber_filtered_urls_test.rb`: a real `S3Service` presigns a download URL and a direct-upload URL; the returned URLs keep their signatures, and the logged lines keep the key and expiry but not the signature. A URL fragment stays apart from the filtered query.
- `test/integration/storage_redirect_logging_test.rb`: a blob redirect to a presigned location logs `Redirected to …X-Amz-Signature=[FILTERED]`.

The same change is in Basecamp (bc3#14116) and HEY.

title: Refuse a join code that was reset while it was being redeemed
body:
`Account::JoinCode#redeem_if` took the row lock only after `JoinCodesController` had found the code. A reset by an admin landing between the lookup and the lock let the old code redeem anyway, counted against the reset code's fresh usage count.

`with_lock` reloads the row, so `redeem_if` now compares the code it was found by against the locked row's code and refuses a mismatch. The block isn't called, so nobody joins. The controller's `User.active.find_by!` then answers not found, as for any code that didn't take.

Test: `redeem_if refuses a code reset after it was found` resets the row through a second instance, then redeems the stale one. It fails without the change (usage count 0 → 1, and the block runs).

title: Pin fizzy-mcp-server v0.2.0
body: Held for Jeremy. Moves the `fizzy_mcp` accessory's image from v0.1.0 to v0.2.0, signed, `sha256:f16aa6bf…e848`. v0.2.0 serves the curated hosted surface, scoped by grant, with capped results and OpenAI domain verification. Follows #3209, which merged with v0.1.0 pinned.

title: Limit OAuth to 37signals staff while it's piloted
body:
Stacked on #3214.

`OAUTH_STAFF_ONLY=true` limits OAuth to staff (`Identity#staff?`), whichever client asks. `Oauth::Availability`'s acceptance, issuance and pilot switches choose *clients*; this one chooses *people*, and composes with them: a request has to pass both.

This works like Basecamp's, where only staff can authorize an agent for now, and anyone else is told so, not shown a 404.

### What's gated

| Where | Staff | Anyone else |
|---|---|---|
| Consent screen (GET and approve) | as today | 403 page: "Only 37signals staff can connect apps to Fizzy for now." No code. |
| Declining at consent | as today | still declines, so the app hears no |
| Code redemption | as today | `invalid_grant`, even for a code issued while they were staff |
| Refresh | as today | `invalid_grant`. The grant stays, for its owner to revoke. |
| An OAuth token at the API, delegated tokens included | as today | `invalid_token`, via `Identity::AccessToken#honored?` |
| Delegation exchange | as today | subject refused, via the same `honored?` |
| Personal access tokens | untouched | untouched |
| Connected Apps, revocation | open | open |

Gating `honored?` means someone who stops being staff loses what they connected on their next request. That's the only part that runs per request, and it reads the identity, which is already loaded to authenticate.

### Turning it on

`OAUTH_STAFF_ONLY: "true"` is set in the clear env of the production, staging and beta deploy configs, so OAuth lands staff-gated everywhere it might be lit. Opening it up means removing those lines. Anything but exactly `"true"` is off, and OSS installs never set it.

### Tests

`test/integration/oauth_staff_only_test.rb` covers:
- staff connect;
- anyone else is refused at consent, both showing and approving, but can still decline;
- a de-staffed code doesn't redeem;
- a de-staffed grant stops authenticating and refreshing;
- personal access tokens work for anyone.

The exchange test covers a de-staffed subject and its delegated token. `Oauth::AvailabilityTest` covers `admits?` and exact-`true` parsing.

I removed each of the four gates in turn, and each removal fails at least one of these tests.

### Stacking note

The personal-access-token exemption reads `oauth_client_id.nil?` here, as C does. #3205 moves PATs onto a first-party client and adds `personal?`. When the two meet, this check becomes `personal?`, or every PAT would be gated.

title: HELD: Light OAuth for staff on production, with the hosted MCP exchange
body:
**Held: don't merge until the prerequisites below are done, on Jeremy's word.**

Turns Fizzy's OAuth authorization server on in production for 37signals staff only, and lights the hosted MCP server's delegation exchange.

## Change
- **Production app env:**
  - `OAUTH_ACCEPTANCE_ENABLED`: discovery, consent and token endpoints answer.
  - `OAUTH_CIMD_ENABLED`: Client ID Metadata Documents from the hosts already allowlisted in `deploy.yml`.
  - `FIZZY_OAUTH_MCP_RESOURCES`: grants can be audienced to `https://mcp.fizzy.do/mcp`.
- **`fizzy_mcp` accessory:**
  - The exchange's token URL and client id.
  - Its client secret, read from the deploy secrets.
  - `FIZZY_MCP_UPSTREAM=http://host.docker.internal` with `--add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway`, which resolves the TODO that stood in its place. The exchange and the API calls after it go to the app on the accessory's own iad web host, through that host's kamal-proxy, over the plain http the balancers already use. They stay in iad without depending on any one balancer. The issuer, token endpoint and API base keep their https URLs; only the connection moves (fizzy-mcp-server#19).
  - `app.fizzy.do:host-gateway` as well, so an image without `FIZZY_MCP_UPSTREAM` fails its startup metadata check rather than reaching Fizzy outside iad.

OAuth stays limited to staff by `OAUTH_STAFF_ONLY` (#3246); this PR doesn't change that.

## Prerequisites, in order
1. The OAuth train, including the staff gate (#3246), is on main and deployed to production.
2. `mcp.fizzy.do` resolves and serves HTTPS.
3. The production `fizzy-mcp-server` client is provisioned with `bin/rails oauth:provision_first_party_clients`, run once with `FIZZY_OAUTH_MCP_RESOURCES=https://mcp.fizzy.do/mcp` passed explicitly, because production only gets that variable when this PR lands. Its secret is then minted with `bin/rails "oauth:mint_client_secret[fizzy-mcp-server]"` into the deploy secrets. Until that secret exists, any production deploy from this branch fails at secret fetch, which is why this PR is held.
4. Done: fizzy-mcp-server#19 is released as v0.2.1, and `fizzy_mcp`'s image in `deploy.yml` is pinned to that release's digest on main (#3254).
5. Done: #3255 is merged to main. It prunes dynamically registered clients that were never authorized after 24 hours, and runs `cleanup_oauth_clients` hourly.

## After merge
1. Deploy production.
2. Reboot `fizzy_mcp` one host at a time (`saas/bin/mcp-rolling-reboot`).

title: dep: update sqlite3, net-ssh and faraday
body:
## Motivation

Bring the lockfiles clear of every advisory `bundler-audit` reports.

- `sqlite3` 2.9.6 truncated SQL strings and bound values longer than `INT_MAX` bytes ([GHSA-4fqr-96q8-xrfx](https://github.com/sparklemotion/sqlite3-ruby/security/advisories/GHSA-4fqr-96q8-xrfx)), and could crash or deadlock a connection when a callback raised, including an interrupt that lands in Rails' busy handler.
- `net-ssh` 7.3.3, which `kamal` uses to deploy, carried several advisories, including shell injection through ProxyCommand/ProxyJump ([GHSA-3x7f-q7wf-fp73](https://github.com/net-ssh/net-ssh/security/advisories/GHSA-3x7f-q7wf-fp73)) and ssh-agent exposure when port forwarding is on ([GHSA-qpg5-fx6p-8cq3](https://github.com/net-ssh/net-ssh/security/advisories/GHSA-qpg5-fx6p-8cq3)).
- `faraday` 2.14.0 in the SaaS bundle let a protocol-relative URL override a connection's host ([GHSA-33mh-2634-fwr2](https://github.com/lostisland/faraday/security/advisories/GHSA-33mh-2634-fwr2)). CI audits only `Gemfile.lock`, so it did not report this one.

## Details

- Update `sqlite3` to [v2.10.2](https://github.com/sparklemotion/sqlite3-ruby/releases/tag/v2.10.2). The jump also takes in 2.10.0 and 2.10.1, which update the vendored SQLite to 3.54.1. This app uses none of the behavior those releases change.
- Update `net-ssh` to 7.3.8 in both lockfiles. The commit message says why 7.3.8 rather than 7.3.5.
- Update `faraday` to 2.14.4 in `Gemfile.saas.lock`.

Supersedes #3231, which stops at `sqlite3` 2.10.0.
