title: Calm the consent page: name the app once, say each thing once
body:
The consent page said who was asking four times and how the app works twice. This brings it to the shape HEY's consent page just took (basecamp/haystack#9267): one heading, "Connect <app> to Fizzy?", one line on who's asking, the choices with short labels, one line of fine print, and Authorize / Deny.

No change to what a grant reaches or how consent is checked.

## The page, shorter

Visible words, header included: 127 → 85 for a self-registered web app on a port with two accounts, 125 → 83 with one account, 125 → 85 for a self-registered app on this device, and 92 → 69 for a 37signals app.

A self-registered web app on a port, with two accounts:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| **Authorize the app at connector.example.com:8443** | **Connect the app at connector.example.com:8443 to Fizzy?** |
| **connector.example.com:844** / **3** (a second heading, broken mid-port on phones) | |
| Says it's "Claude Desktop" | Says it's "Claude Desktop" |
| **We haven't checked this app.** Anyone can run an app at any address, so only authorize it if you trust **connector.example.com:8443**. | **We haven't checked this app.** Only authorize it if you trust that address. |
| Signed in as david@… Not you? | Signed in as david@… Not you? |
| **Account**: 37signals / Initech LLC | **Account**: 37signals / Initech LLC |
| The app reaches this account only. Connect it again to add another. | |
| **Read only**: See your boards, cards, comments and the people in your account. It can't change anything. | **Read only**: See boards, cards, comments and people. It can't change anything. |
| **Read and write**: See everything you can, and act as you: create, edit, move, close and delete cards, comments and boards. | **Read and write**: Also create, edit, move, close and delete cards, comments and boards. |
| It works as you, so it can only reach what you can, in the account above. | It acts as you, so it reaches only what you can, in that account. |
| Either way, you'll go back to **connector.example.com:8443**. You can disconnect it at any time in Connected apps. | You can disconnect it anytime in Connected apps. |
| Authorize / Deny | Authorize / Deny |

An app on this device is headed "Connect an app on your device to Fizzy?", and its caution is "**We haven't checked this app.** Only authorize it if you started it." A 37signals app is headed by its name, with "Made by 37signals." under it. An app with a client metadata document keeps "Name set by the app at **host**."

### What's cut, and why

- **The second heading** (the host again, in the panel): the page heading already names it. On a phone it broke inside the port (`…:844` / `3`). The heading now wraps between words and breaks inside a word only when a host is too long for the line.
- **The host in the caution and in "Either way, you'll go back to…"**: the heading of a self-registered app *is* where it goes back to, so the caution points at "that address", and the return line goes. A 37signals app or one with a metadata document can only return to callbacks Fizzy or its document host registered, as on HEY.
- **"Anyone can run an app at any address" / "It runs on your device and will get this access"**: the heading says what and where; the caution keeps the one instruction that matters.
- **"See everything you can, and act as you"** in the write choice and **"It works as you, so it can only reach what you can"** under it said the same thing. It's said once now, under the choices, with where it reaches: that account, or every account you belong to.
- **"The app reaches this account only. Connect it again to add another."**: how-to, not a decision. The Account legend and the reach line say what it reaches.

## Contracts unchanged

Account choice (radio per account, preselection, one account carried hidden, required), the read / read-write scope radios, the hidden OAuth parameters and resource, CSRF, Not you?, and Authorize / Deny (`error=access_denied`) post exactly as before. `oauth_access_levels` loses its `one_account:` option: the descriptions no longer say "account" or "accounts", since the reach line does.

## Screenshots

Before and after, at 1280 and 390 px (fold and full page), for: a self-registered web app on port 8443 with one and with two accounts, a self-registered app on this device, and a 37signals app. Checked by eye: no heading breaks mid-host at 390, and nothing new falls below the fold.

## Tests

- `oauth_consent_screen_test.rb`: heading and title copy, the shorter caution, the reach line and the fine print; the host appears once in the page body.
- `oauth_flow_test.rb`: the port test asserts the heading, and that `connector.example.com:8443` appears once.
- `oauth_dcr_redirect_allowlist_test.rb`: a private-use scheme callback is headed as an app on your device.
- `oauth_helper_test.rb`: every access level has a label and a short line.
- OAuth, helper and connected-apps tests: 483 pass. Local `bin/ci` on `5001ac8`: style, security, setup phases, and the OSS suite and system tests pass. The SaaS (MySQL) suites ran in this PR's checks rather than locally.

Updates `webmock` from 3.26.4 to 3.34.0
Release notes

Sourced from webmock's releases.

3.34.0

  • Allow with(query: :any) to match any query string (#1099)

    stub_request(:get, "www.example.com").with(query: :any) matches requests with any query string, or none. RSpec's anything works the same way. Previously, this raised NoMethodError, and you had to write with(query: hash_including({})).

    Use a URL without query parameters when passing query: :any. Otherwise, WebMock raises ArgumentError.

    Thanks to nightpool

  • Raise a clear ArgumentError for an unsupported query option

    Previously, a value such as with(query: :all) raised NoMethodError (undefined method split). The new error lists the supported values.

  • Show anything for keys given without a value to hash_including or hash_excluding outside RSpec

    Previously, with Minitest or Test::Unit, messages showed #<WebMock::Matchers::AnyArgMatcher:0x...>, for example for with(query: hash_including(:a)). RSpec's own matchers already showed anything.

  • Provide HTTP_HOST to to_rack apps when the client has not supplied a Host header (#1084)

    Previously, requests from some HTTP clients reached the Rack app without HTTP_HOST. This caused host checks such as Sinatra's HostAuthorization to see an empty host.

    WebMock now fills in the host from the request URL, including the port when it is not the default. An explicit Host header is preserved.

    Thanks to Benoit Tigeot

  • Fix Rack compatibility for to_rack apps

    The request environment now passes Rack::Lint.

    SERVER_PORT and CONTENT_LENGTH are now strings. If your app or tests read them directly, use string comparisons, such as env['SERVER_PORT'] == "80". The environment also includes SERVER_PROTOCOL.

    CONTENT_TYPE is omitted when the request has no content type. The Content-Length header is passed only as CONTENT_LENGTH, without an extra HTTP_CONTENT_LENGTH entry. Transfer-Encoding is removed because the body has already been decoded.

    Repeated header values are joined into one string. Header values and the body read from rack.input now use binary (ASCII-8BIT) strings.

3.33.0

  • Return effective_url as a String for stubbed Typhoeus responses (#869)

    Previously, this was an Addressable::URI. If your code calls methods such as effective_url.host, parse the returned string into a URI first.

    The URL keeps the request's port, query order and encoding. It follows curl's formatting: for example, http://example.com:80 becomes http://example.com:80/. Stubbed timeouts now provide an effective_url too.

    Thanks to Tom Brammar

  • Fix incorrect removal of default ports from displayed URLs

    WebMock could accidentally remove :80 or :443 from a URL's path or query. For example, an error message could show /foo/bar instead of /foo:80/bar.

    Only the host's default port is now removed. This also works when the port is immediately followed by a query string, as in http://example.com:80?a=b.

title: Deliver FIZZY_REVIEWER_SIGN_IN_CODES to production
body:
Held: don't merge or deploy without Jeremy's word, and not before the secret below exists.

## Why

#3257 moved directory reviewers to one identity and code per partner, read from `FIZZY_REVIEWER_SIGN_IN_CODES`, and deliberately left step 3 of its rollout (wiring the secret into the production deploy) for later. Production still fetches and sets only the single `FIZZY_REVIEWER_SIGN_IN_EMAIL` / `FIZZY_REVIEWER_SIGN_IN_CODE_DIGEST` pair, so `config.x.reviewer_sign_in.code_digests` is always nil in production and no per-partner code signs in, or passes the `CONNECTED_APPS_PREVIEW` gate (#3271).

## What changed

- `saas/.kamal/secrets.production`: fetch `FIZZY_REVIEWER_SIGN_IN_CODES` with the other production secrets, and extract it.
- `saas/config/deploy.production.yml`: add it to `env.secret`, beside the pair.
- The single pair stays wired: `Identity::ReviewerSignIn` still reads it beside the list (the list wins where both name an address). Dropping it is #3257's optional step 4, once the list carries the original reviewer.
- Production only, as the pair is: no beta or staging destination wires reviewer sign-in today.

## Before this deploys

`kamal secrets fetch` fails when a requested field doesn't exist, so the next production deploy after this merges fails unless `FIZZY_REVIEWER_SIGN_IN_CODES` already exists in production's secret store, beside `FIZZY_REVIEWER_SIGN_IN_CODE_DIGEST`. Its value is the `FIZZY_REVIEWER_SIGN_IN_CODES=` line `bin/rails saas:reviewer_sign_in:generate EMAIL=…` prints (cumulative, so the last run's line lists every reviewer). Create it first, then merge, then deploy. Every production secret here is fetched in the one call, so there's no existing pattern for an optional secret to follow.

## Tests

`saas/test/lib/production_secrets_test.rb`, against the Kamal configuration production renders:
- the reviewer sign-in variables (the pair and the list) are among the web role's secrets;
- every secret a production role or accessory reads is assigned in `secrets.production`, and every one assigned by `kamal secrets extract` is in the fetch.

Each fails with its part of the fix reverted: without the `env.secret` entry, the first; without the fetch name or the extract line, the second.

title: Let a browser approve OAuth consent, and answer OAuth clients whatever their user agent
body:
Two bugs kept anyone from connecting an app to Fizzy.

### Consent posts were refused with a 422

Every authorization server response sent `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, the consent page included. A browser that posts a form from a no-referrer page sends `Origin: null`, and Rails' origin check (`valid_request_origin?`, on under `load_defaults`) raises `InvalidCrossOriginRequest` for a null origin before it looks at `Sec-Fetch-Site`. So Authorize, Deny and "Not you?" all answered 422 in a real browser.

Tests didn't catch it because the test environment turns forgery protection off. The system test that clicks Authorize now runs with forgery protection on, and it fails on `main` (the browser stays on `/oauth/authorization`).

The fix: the pages a GET renders (consent, the preview notice, error pages, and the sign-in and error redirects) send `same-origin`. Our own form posts keep their Origin, and nothing goes to any other site, so the authorization request's parameters still stay with us. A POST's answer keeps `no-referrer`, including the redirect that carries the code to the client, because a redirect's policy is the one its next hop is sent under.

Basecamp's consent works with the same `no-referrer` header because its layout's `<meta name="referrer">` overrides it. HEY's consent never sets `no-referrer`.

### OAuth endpoints answered 406 to old browser user agents

`allow_browser versions: :modern` gated every controller. A token request whose platform sends an old browser's user agent got the 406 unsupported-browser page, which no OAuth client can act on. Token, delegation exchange, revocation, registration and both discovery documents now answer any user agent (`allow_any_user_agent`). Consent, which people see, keeps the gate. A test holds every `Oauth::` controller to that choice, so a new controller fails the test until someone decides which side it belongs on.

### Not in this PR: a funnel alarm

Both bugs were silent: no exceptions and no errors in the OAuth error metrics. The only signal was a funnel that never got past consent. An alarm worth adding is "consent pages render, but consent.approved stays at zero for N days" (or approvals with no matching token.issued). Either one would have caught these within a day.

### Tests

- `test/system/oauth_consent_test.rb`: a real browser clicks Authorize with forgery protection on.
- `test/integration/oauth_response_headers_test.rb`: `same-origin` on GET pages and redirects, `no-referrer` on the code-bearing redirect and on "Not you?".
- `test/integration/oauth_user_agents_test.rb`: the machine endpoints answer an old Safari user agent, and consent still answers it 406.

Every new or changed test fails without the app changes (8 failures and 1 error out of 14). The OSS suite passes locally (2666 tests). The SaaS suite runs in CI.

title: Refine the OAuth screens from design review
body:
Held: don't merge without Jeremy's word.

The design and copy edits from @jzimdars's review of the OAuth screens, on top of #3259. The answers to #3259's questions are in a comment there. Run `script/dev/oauth_states` to see every state.

## Consent

- Every authorization page (consent, the error page, "Not available yet", "Connecting apps is paused") uses the sign-in layout, so the Fizzy logo heads it with no account menu. The logo gets a little more room under it, to sit as far from the page heading as the account menu does. The panels get the same top margin as Account Settings.
- "Signed in as … Use a different account?" moves under the page heading, outside the panel. "Not you?" becomes "Use a different account?".
- The page heading is "Connect this app to Fizzy?" for every app, and so is the title. The panel opens with the app's name, and under it in grey who set that name, as Connected apps shows it: "Name set by the app at tools.example.com" (a self-registered app, by this request's callback host), "Name set by an app on your device", "Name set by the app at claude.ai" (a metadata document's host) or "Made by 37signals". "Says it's …" is gone. Self-registered apps keep "We haven't checked this app." beneath. `oauth_client_display_identity`, which only the old heading used, is gone.
- The account and access choices are each one bordered group, as in bc3's consent: the rows share a frame, and the chosen row is tinted and outlined. The radio is drawn in CSS, so it follows Fizzy's theme rather than the OS's.
- Each group's note moves under its heading, small and subtle. The account note reads "The app connects only to the account you choose. Connect it again to add another." With one account it reads "The app connects only to **37signals**."
- The closing line reads "If you change your mind, you can revoke its access at any time in Connected apps."

## Connected apps

- The intro reads "Apps you've connected directly to your Fizzy account. Each one works as you, with the access listed below. Don't recognize one? Revoke it, and it's cut off right away."
- Disconnect becomes "Revoke access", as in HEY and Basecamp: the row's button, the dialog ("Revoke access for Board Sync?"), its button, and the notice ("Access revoked for Board Sync").
- The dialog's text is centred. Its second sentence reads "To use it again, reconnect it." The webhooks the app set up sit in the warning box, with "Also remove these webhooks" inside it, and a full space comes before the buttons.
- A self-registered app with both a web callback and an on-device one names both: "Name set by the app at tools.example.com, or an app on your device" (before, only the web host), as bc3 and HEY do. Consent names the one callback in use, so it needs no change.
- Each row reads in three blocks: the name with its grey byline tight under it, the access lines, and the grey "Connected … · access last renewed …" line, with a paragraph's space between the blocks. The empty state loses its dashed frame.

## Error pages

- The "For the app's developer" line is gone: a person reads the plain sentence only. The code stays on the page as `data-oauth-error`, which the tests read.
- A dark server shows "Not available yet", as bc3 and HEY do, in place of the app's 404 page. It still answers 404.

## Elsewhere

- The personal access token form and reveal say "Read only", as consent and Connected apps do.

## Tests

The consent, switch, error page, audience, flow, metadata document, Connected apps and token form tests follow the new copy. The error page tests check `data-oauth-error` in place of the developer line, and that the developer's description never reaches the page.

`bin/ci` passes on 2fe9c5c9a (OSS: 2688 tests and 47 system tests), signed off.

No new third party or personal data.

title: Bump Lexxy to 1.0.4
body:
Updates Lexxy from 1.0.1 to [v1.0.4](https://github.com/basecamp/lexxy/releases/tag/v1.0.4), with the latest `main` merged in. ## 🤖 Review: what changes in Fizzy Fizzy loads Lexxy's JavaScript straight from the gem through the importmap (`pin "lexxy"`), and its CSS from the gem's stylesheets, so the gem bump is the whole bump. Fizzy has no patched or vendored copy of Lexxy. It customises Lexxy in these places, and each one still works on 1.0.4: - `app/assets/stylesheets/lexxy.css` and the `--lexxy-*` variables in `cards.css`, `comments.css`, `card-perma.css`, `attachments.css` and `golden-effect.css`. Every element, class and variable they target still exists in 1.0.4. - `initializers/lexxy_markdown_paste.js`: `lexxy:insert-markdown` and `addBlockSpacing()` are unchanged. - `initializers/lexxy_mermaid.js`: Mermaid is still added to the code language picker. - `syntax_highlight_controller.js`: Lexxy still exports `highlightCode`. - The `@` and `#` prompts: `insert-editable-text`, `remote-filtering` and `supports-space-in-searches` are unchanged. - Sanitizer lists: Lexxy now adds its tags once the app has booted ([#1356](https://github.com/basecamp/lexxy/pull/1356)), and Fizzy's `config/initializers/sanitization.rb` still merges with them. On 1.0.4 the allowed list keeps `s`, `u`, `details`, `summary`, `table`, `figure`, `action-text-attachment`, `style` and `data-language`. ### Visible changes in Fizzy 1. **Underlined text now shows as underlined in saved cards and comments.** Lexxy 1.0.4 allows `` ([#1248](https://github.com/basecamp/lexxy/pull/1248)), and Fizzy's own list allowed `` but not ``. On 1.0.1 underlines showed in the editor but not on the saved card or comment. The underline was stored all along, so underlines people already saved will start to show. 2. **Italic words inside a quote now show upright**, so they still stand out from the quote's italic text ([#1215](https://github.com/basecamp/lexxy/pull/1215)). 3. **A mention inside a text selection now shows as selected.** Its avatar takes the selection tint while it's selected ([#1205](https://github.com/basecamp/lexxy/pull/1205)). Local drafts stop saving an empty paragraph, and comment validation is unaffected. - Paste handling: email layout tables are unwrapped (Gmail), Outlook spacing and bullets are kept, blank lines from Trix are kept, Markdown copied from VS Code is converted, plain text takes the formatting at the caret, HTML snippets pasted as text stay text, and pasted link addresses are trimmed. - An image can carry a link: select it and use the toolbar's link button ([#1272](https://github.com/basecamp/lexxy/pull/1272)). - The `@` and `#` menus wrap keyboard navigation and flip above the caret when they would be clipped ([#448](https://github.com/basecamp/lexxy/pull/448), [#1317](https://github.com/basecamp/lexxy/pull/1317)). title: Report a fresh access token's whole lifetime in expires_in
body:
`Identity::AccessToken#expires_in` was `(expires_at - Time.current).to_i`. It counted down from the clock at response time and truncated, so any time between the mint and the response (there's always some) turned a 1-hour token's 3600 into 3599, and a delegated token's 300 into 299. Some MCP clients require an access token that lasts at least an hour, and they refuse a provider whose token response says less. Basecamp had the same bug and gets the same fix.

## Change

- A token keeps an in-memory `issued_at` (never stored) from the clock reading its expiry was taken from: set on create, and on rotation in `#refresh`, where `updated_at` now shares that reading too.
- `expires_in` (RFC 6749 §5.1, the token's lifetime) is measured from `issued_at` when this instance minted the token. A token loaded later, such as a refresh retried within the grace window, reports what it has left. Both round up, so a fraction of a second never costs a whole one.

This covers the authorization_code, refresh_token and token-exchange responses, which all read `expires_in`. No TTL changes and no migration.

## Tests

- Model: a fresh token reports 3600 with the clock frozen, and 0.4s and 2s after the mint. A refreshed token reports 3600 0.4s after rotation. A token reloaded 10m0.4s later reports 3000.
- Integration: the authorization_code and refresh_token grants answer `expires_in == 3600`, and the exchange answers `TTL_CAP` (300), all on the real clock.

Checked against the old `expires_in`: 6 of the 7 new or tightened assertions fail there with 3599/2999/299. The frozen-clock case passes on both, because no time passes in it.

title: Take turns on the shared advisory database in bin/bundler-audit
body:
## What

`bin/bundler-audit` holds an exclusive `flock` on a lock file beside the advisory database (`~/.local/share/ruby-advisory-db.lock`, or beside `$BUNDLER_AUDIT_DB`) for the whole check. The lock is named from the database's own name, so it sits beside it whatever the path ends in: a trailing slash on `BUNDLER_AUDIT_DB` once put it inside, where it made a fresh database look downloaded and the audit passed on no advisories.

## Why

Every checkout on a machine shares one ruby-advisory-db clone, and `bin/bundler-audit check --update` git-pulls into it. When two `bin/ci` runs on one host (thelio runs many lanes at once) reach "Security: Gem audit" together, git refuses the second pull (`cannot lock ref`, `Cannot rebase onto multiple branches`, untracked files in the way) and that run fails, sometimes both do and the database stays stale.

The lock lives in the binstub because that's what `config/ci.rb` and people both run, and these apps share no CI helper to hold it once. It's Ruby's `File#flock`, so it works on macOS, which has no `flock(1)`. Holding it for the whole check, not only the pull, also keeps a check from reading the database mid-pull; a check takes about a second. A run that finds vulnerabilities still exits 1: the lock is released when the block unwinds.

The same change is going into basecamp/bc3#14357, basecamp/dash#1309, basecamp/fizzy#3289, basecamp/haystack#9277, basecamp/launchpad#990 and basecamp/queenbee#1658, the apps whose CI runs `--update`; they all lock the same file, so they take turns across apps too.

## Proof

On thelio, two `bin/bundler-audit check --update` at once against a scratch advisory database reset 40 commits behind upstream, fresh for each trial (`BUNDLER_AUDIT_DB=/tmp/audit-race-db`):

- **Before**, bc3's current binstub: 8 of 8 trials (two rounds) failed at least one run, and 4 of 8 failed both and left the database stale (`fatal: Cannot rebase onto multiple branches.`, `error: cannot lock ref 'refs/remotes/origin/master'`, `untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge`).
- **After**: both runs passed and the database ended at upstream's head in every trial: 5 then 3 for bc3 and 3 then 3 for each of dash, fizzy, haystack, launchpad and queenbee, on the first head and the final one.
- Across apps: bc3 and haystack at once on one stale database both passed and it ended current.
- First download: two runs at once with the database and its parent directory missing both passed.
- The real default path: fizzy and launchpad at once both passed, and the lock file appeared at `~/.local/share/ruby-advisory-db.lock`.
- A vulnerable lockfile (rack 1.0.0) still exits 1 through the lock.
- `BUNDLER_AUDIT_DB=/tmp/x/db/` (trailing slash, nothing there yet) with that lockfile: the first head exited 0 against an empty `db/` holding only `.lock`; every app's final binstub downloads the database, locks `/tmp/x/db.lock` and exits 1.

A binstub without the lock doesn't take turns, so until every app has it an old one can still collide with a new one.

title: Keep a filtered board in columns when asked
body:
Discussion: https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/discussions/3290

Filtering a board swaps its columns for a flat list of matching cards. This adds a toggle to the filter bar, shown only while a filter is set, that keeps the columns instead. Each column (Maybe?, the board's own columns, Not Now and Done) then shows and counts only the cards the filter matches. The list stays the default, so nothing changes for anyone who doesn't use the toggle.

- `Filter#apply_to(cards)` narrows any card relation by the filter's criteria, without the list's open / not-now defaults. That way closed and postponed matches still land in Done and Not Now. `Filter#cards` now shares those criteria through a private `narrow`, so its query is unchanged.
- The column frame `src`s and drop URLs carry the filter params. Lazy-loaded columns, their pagination and the drag-and-drop stream responses (`ColumnFiltering` concern) stay filtered. With no filter set, the URLs are exactly as before.
- The choice travels as `view=columns` in a hidden field inside the (permanent) filter form, so it survives later filter changes.
- Streams that re-render a column without knowing the filter (card hotkeys, column edits and moves) are followed by a morph refresh of the filtered board (`filtered-columns` controller). Filtered columns skip the fragment cache. Column frames now follow the server when a refresh hands them a different `src` (a column moved by a stream comes back unfiltered); unfiltered boards never hit that path.
- Columns keep their own sort, so `sorted_by` has no effect in columns mode.

Testing:
- 15 new tests: model, board show, each column controller, column and stream drops, search rate limiting, and system tests for a card action and a column move that re-render columns. Each fails without its fix, except one that pins down the existing list behaviour.
- Full suite passes locally on SQLite (2682 tests, 0 failures) and MySQL (2686 tests, 0 failures), and the new system tests pass on both. RuboCop, Brakeman, bundler-audit, importmap audit, bundle drift and the agent docs check all pass. The system suite has flaky failures that change from run to run; unmodified `main` shows the same on this machine.
- Checked by hand in the browser on a dev board with a tag filter: the list shows the matching cards; columns mode shows the same cards in their columns with filtered counts; dragging a card between columns keeps both columns filtered; moving a column left or right keeps it filtered; toggling back works; an unfiltered board is unchanged.
- Not checked: the `[`/`]` card hotkeys by hand (covered by a system test that issues the same request) and the native apps.

No new third parties or personal data.

title: Page the activities feed through ids, and stop counting every poll
body:
The activities feed is slow for readers with a long history because of how it sorts. A reader's activities span all their boards, so the database sorts every matching event to keep one page of 15. The page query selected whole rows, so MySQL fetched each matching row before it sorted.

On Call card: [[Fizzy] Activities API is slow and costly to poll](https://app.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/27/card_tables/cards/10483559130). After #3274, activities requests hit the cache on 99.7% of reads, but about 260 ms of the 306 ms median was still database time.

## What production showed

`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on the replica, for one sampled reader with 4 boards and 8,804 matching events:

```
-> Index lookup on events using index_events_on_board_id_and_action_and_created_at (board_id=accesses.board_id), with index condition: action IN (12 actions)  (actual time=0.312..57.3 rows=2201 loops=4)
-> Covering index lookup on events using index_events_on_board_id_and_action_and_created_at (actual time=0.0116..0.743 rows=2201 loops=4)
```

The first line is the page query: 57 ms per board to fetch full rows, 229 of its 242 ms. The second is the count, which reads only the index: 9.5 ms in total. A small reader's page query took 1.4 ms. This is one sampled reader.

## What changes

1. **The feed pages through ids, then loads only that page's rows.** Ids sort straight from the board, action and created_at index, because InnoDB stores the primary key in every secondary index. On a local MySQL 8.4 copy of that reader's shape (9,057 matches on 4 boards, warm buffer pool), the page query dropped from 27–32 ms to 4.2 ms. The 15 rows then load by id through the same access scope, so an event that moved off the reader's boards in between stays out.
2. **No more count.** geared_pagination's `X-Total-Count`, and its last-page check, counted every event the reader can see on every request. The feed now sends only the `Link` header, which is all the [API docs](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/a3fe5ba7b24bc63a9436f0e1d6c55a9d812a5df3/docs/api/README.md#pagination) promise. That saves about 10 ms of the 250 for a big reader, so it's the smaller part of this change.
3. **The next-page link keeps repeated filters.** Several `creator_ids[]` or `board_ids[]` used to collapse to the last one in the link.

Trade-offs:

- `X-Total-Count` goes away for this endpoint. It isn't documented, but a client could read it.
- When the last page is exactly full, the client follows one more link and gets an empty page.
- With `creator_ids` set, the id query still reads rows, because creator isn't in the index.

No new third party or personal data.

title: Create missing webhook trackers on import
body:
The import writes webhooks with `insert_all!`, so the `after_create` that gives every webhook its `Webhook::DelinquencyTracker` never runs. The tracker only comes from the archive's `data/webhook_delinquency_trackers/`. An archive that leaves it out imports webhooks whose every delivery fails on a nil tracker:

```
NoMethodError: undefined method 'record_delivery_of' for nil
app/models/webhook/delivery.rb:41:in 'Webhook::Delivery#deliver'
```

In production this came from hand-built archives uploaded to the import endpoint.

A tracker only holds a failure streak, and a new one is the state a new webhook starts in. So rather than reject such an archive, `Account::Import#process` now creates a tracker for every imported webhook that lacks one, after the record sets run, next to `create_missing_user_settings`. This also covers a real export where a webhook changes mid-export, since export takes no shared snapshot across record sets.

Creating the tracker lazily on delivery was the other option, but `webhook_id` has no unique index, so concurrent deliveries could create two.

Tests:

- An exported account with its tracker files removed imports, and every webhook gets a tracker. The test fails without the change.
- `bin/ci` passes locally apart from setup (needs sudo) and gitleaks (not installed here).

title: Accept any https callback in dynamic client registration
body:
Self-registered (RFC 7591) clients could only use an https callback on a host listed in `OAUTH_DCR_ALLOWED_HTTPS_HOSTS`. A client sends its `redirect_uris` as one set and the whole set is refused if any one fails, so any hosted client we hadn't listed couldn't connect. VS Code is one: it registers two vscode.dev callbacks beside its loopback ones. A self-hosted install with the variable unset accepted no hosted client at all. Basecamp dropped its list for the same reason, and this brings Fizzy to the same rules.

## What a registration may name now

| Callback | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `http://` loopback (127.0.0.1, [::1], localhost), any port | accepted | accepted |
| `cursor://`, `claude://` | accepted | accepted |
| `https://` on a listed host | accepted | accepted |
| `https://` on any other plain host | **refused** | accepted |
| `https://` on this install's own host, or on fizzy.do, basecamp.com, 37signals.com or hey.com and their subdomains | refused (never listed) | refused |
| `http://` off loopback, fragments, userinfo, percent-encoded or non-canonical hosts, other schemes, more than 10 | refused | refused |

The own-host check only applies when a host is added, so a client that already has one still saves. `Oauth.dcr_redirect_shape?` is unchanged.

## Safeguards, all already in place

- A self-registered client is never trusted and always gets the consent screen. The screen heads it with "the app at host" and adds "We haven't checked this app".
- An error found before consent is never bounced to a self-registered https callback (`Oauth::Client#vetted_redirect?`, RFC 9700 §4.11.2). That matters more now that any host can register, so this PR adds a test for it.
- Registration is rate limited, capped at 10 callbacks, and swept when nobody authorizes it.

## Config

`OAUTH_DCR_ALLOWED_HTTPS_HOSTS` is removed from `config/environments/*.rb`, `saas/config/deploy.yml` and `docs/docker-deployment.md`. Nothing reads it any more, so an install that still sets it just ignores it.

title: End the connected apps preview in production
body:
## What changes

`saas/config/deploy.production.yml` sets `CONNECTED_APPS_PREVIEW: "false"`. Anyone can then connect an app to Fizzy in production, not only 37signals staff and the reviewers `CONNECTED_APPS_PREVIEW_REVIEWERS` lists (`Oauth::Availability`).

Its old name, `OAUTH_STAFF_ONLY`, also goes to `"false"`. An image from before #3271 reads only the old name, so rolling back to one leaves the destination open as well, rather than quietly closing it again.

Staging and the betas are unchanged and keep the preview.

| Destination (rendered by Kamal, every role) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| production | `"true"` / `"true"` | **`"false"` / `"false"`** |
| staging | `"true"` / `"true"` | unchanged |
| beta1 | `"true"` / `"true"` | unchanged |

(Each cell is `CONNECTED_APPS_PREVIEW` / `OAUTH_STAFF_ONLY`.)

## Rollback

Set both values back to `"true"` and deploy. Grants made in the meantime stay. A non-previewer's tokens stop working on their next use, since the preview is checked when a token is used, not only at consent.

## Pre-lift checklist

- **Rate limits on the hosted MCP path:** no shared address bucket stands in the way here. Fizzy has no Rack-level general limiter. The hosted MCP server limits per source (`internal/hosted/limit.go` in fizzy-mcp-server). The token exchange has one budget shared by every user, by design, guarded per source (`Oauth::TokenExchangesController::CLIENT_BUDGET`). Nothing limits API volume per token; that would be a new limit, not a fix to a shared one.
- **Betas:** the beta runs a build that holds OAuth to staff, which is stricter than the preview, and this change doesn't touch it.
- **Docs:** the `connector_preview` line on fizzy.do/ai comes out at lift time, in basecamp/fizzy-site#22 (draft, stacked on #16). Publish it once this deploy finishes.

## Verification

- `bin/rails test test/models/oauth/availability_test.rb`: 15 tests, 0 failures. It pins `"false"` → off, and covers the old name being ignored once the new one is set.
- The production, staging and beta1 config was rendered through Kamal's own loader, every role, with the results in the table above.
- No test in this repo pins the per-destination value. Full CI runs on the PR.

title: Keep rich text attachments Action Text can't read
body:
An `<action-text-attachment>` tag with no attribute that Action Text recognizes, such as one with only the `gid` attribute our exports write, makes `Content#attachment_for_node` return `nil`. `Content#attachments` then holds `nil`, and several paths raise:

- Scanning for mentions (`Mention::CreateJob`, `NotifyRecipientsJob`): `undefined method 'attachable' for nil`
- Rendering the rich text: `undefined method 'node' for nil`
- Exporting a card that holds it

This patches `ActionText::Content#attachment_for_node` to keep the attachment as parsed when it can't be rebuilt from full attributes. The tag then renders as a missing attachable (☒), and the mention scan skips it. Valid attachments are unchanged.

The patch lives in `lib/rails_ext`, with a guard test that fails once Rails handles this upstream.

title: Don't publicly cache public pages rendered for a signed-in person
body:
Public board pages are sent with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=30`. They still resume the visitor's session, so when a signed-in person opens one, the page carries their user id, timezone and other session details. A shared cache can then serve that page to the next visitors for up to 30 seconds.

This marks the page as publicly cacheable only when nobody is signed in. A page rendered for a signed-in person falls back to Rails' default private headers.

title: The "C" add card hotkey does nothing on "Assigned to me", "Added by me" and other filtered card views
body:
Approved in discussion #2841, where a maintainer said a pull request would be welcome.

The `C` hotkey ("Add a card") works on Home and on a board, but does nothing on the filtered cards view (`/cards`). That view is where the Jump menu's **Assigned to me** (`2`) and **Added by me** (`3`) links go, along with any filter that leaves a board's columns. There's no "Add a card" button there either, so you have to go back to Home or a board to create a card.

**Proposal:** render the Home page's "Add a card" button (with its `C` hotkey) in the filtered cards view header too. Like on Home, it adds the card to the first board in the filter, or to the most recently accessed board when the filter has no boards.

title: Add a card with C from the filtered cards view
body:
Closes #3300, following discussion #2841.

The `C` hotkey and the "Add a card" button were only on Home and on boards. The filtered cards view, where **Assigned to me** (`2`) and **Added by me** (`3`) take you, had neither. This change renders Home's add card button (`events/index/_add_card_button`) in that view's header as well.

It picks the board the same way Home does (`User::Filtering#single_board_or_first`): the first board in the filter, or the most recently accessed board when the filter has no boards. Changing the board filter reloads the whole page (`submitToGenericCardsView`), so the button's board always matches the current selection.

The header looks the same as Home's: the button sits on the left, and on narrow screens it collapses to the round `+` icon.

### Testing

- New controller tests cover the hotkey button on an unscoped filter (most recently accessed board) and on a board filter (the filtered board). Both fail without the view change.
- `bin/rails test test/controllers test/helpers` and `bin/rubocop` pass.
- I checked it in a browser: pressing `C` on "Assigned to me" opens a new draft card, and the header renders correctly at desktop and mobile widths.

title: Fix 406 when watching or unwatching a board
body:
When you watched or stopped watching a board, the change saved but the page didn't update. Your avatar never appeared under "Watching for new cards" and the button kept its old label until you reloaded. The request came back 406.

Card: https://app.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/43795599/card_tables/cards/10499407588

**Why:** Turbo asks for a Turbo Stream first when it submits a form. #2675 added JSON responses for the SDK, and along the way it added a bare `format.turbo_stream` to `Boards::InvolvementsController#update`. There's no `update.turbo_stream.erb`, so Rails answered 406 instead of falling back to `update.html.erb`, which is the response that replaces the involvement frame.

**Fix:** drop that one line. Turbo gets the HTML frame again, and JSON still gets its 204, which is what #2675 was after. A new controller test sends Turbo's Accept and Turbo-Frame headers and checks for the 200, your avatar in the watchers list, and the "Stop watching" button. It fails with a 406 without the fix.

**Who it affects:** the Android and iOS apps (QA found it in Fizzy Android 1.2.0, and it's in 1.1.3 too, since both load this page from the server) and the web. Any Turbo form submit sends the same Accept header.

**Tested:** the full SQLite suite (2697 tests) and rubocop pass locally on Ruby 4.0.9.

## Codex review

- Round 1: approved, no findings. No more rounds needed.

title: "Clear all" in the notifications tray points the tray at bulk_reading, so a later reload 404s
body:
Reported in discussion #3162. Reproducible on `main`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the notifications tray (`N`) while you have unread notifications.
2. Click **Clear all**.
3. Wait 10 minutes, then switch to another window and come back. Or call `document.getElementById("notifications").reload()` in the console to skip the wait.

### What happens

"Clear all" submits `POST /notifications/bulk_reading?from_tray=true` into the `notifications` frame, and `Notifications::BulkReadingsController#create` answers `head :ok`. Turbo takes the frame's new `src` from the response URL, so the tray frame ends up pointing at `/notifications/bulk_reading?from_tray=true`.

The tray's `frame-reloader` controller reloads the frame from its `src` when the window regains focus. That sends `GET /notifications/bulk_reading?from_tray=true`, which has no route and returns 404. The 404 page has no `notifications` frame, so Turbo navigates the whole page to it. The person ends up on a 404 page at the bulk reading URL, away from what they were doing. (The discussion also reports a "Content missing" frame.)

### Expected

After "Clear all", the tray stays pointed at `/notifications/tray` and later reloads keep working.

### Proposed fix

When the request comes from the tray, redirect to `tray_notifications_path` instead of returning an empty 200. The frame then renders the now-empty tray, and its `src` stays on the tray.

title: Redirect to the tray after clearing all notifications from it
body:
Closes #3303, reported in discussion #3162.

"Clear all" in the notifications tray posts to `bulk_reading` into the `notifications` frame, and the response was an empty 200. Turbo takes the frame's `src` from the response URL, so afterwards the tray frame pointed at `/notifications/bulk_reading?from_tray=true`. When the window regains focus, the tray's `frame-reloader` reloads that `src` with a GET, which has no route. The 404 response has no `notifications` frame, so Turbo navigates the whole page to it.

When the request comes from the tray, this redirects to `tray_notifications_path` instead. The frame renders the now-empty tray and keeps `/notifications/tray` as its `src`. The non-tray HTML and JSON responses are unchanged.

### Testing

- New `test/system/notifications_tray_test.rb`: it clears the tray, checks that the frame still points at the tray, then reloads it the way `frame-reloader` does. Without the fix it fails, and in the browser the reload takes the page to the 404 at `/notifications/bulk_reading?from_tray=true`.
- Updated the bulk readings controller test for the redirect.
- `bin/rails test test/controllers/notifications` and `bin/rubocop` pass.

title: Page the activities feed through event ids
body:
`GET /activities` read and sorted every full event row that the reader can see, to return one page. For the Notify/1.0 poller on the [on-call card](https://app.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/27/card_tables/cards/10483559130), that is 40,010 rows on every request, about 215ms of the 270ms DB time.

This pages through `events.id` first, which MySQL reads from the covering `index_events_on_board_id_and_action_and_created_at`, then loads only that page's events, with their preloads, through the same feed scope.

Measured in production for the poller's user (median of 5, read-only via `bin/kamal query`):

| Page (rows) | Now | ids + load | Same rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (15) | 213.5ms | 52.6 + 0.9ms | yes |
| 4 (100) | 215.9ms | 53.7 + 3.2ms | yes |
| 9 (100) | 210.5ms | 53.5 + 3.2ms | yes |

Expected DB time per poller request: about 270ms → 110ms. Staging showed the same 3.2–3.5× gain for wide, narrow and very large readers. Narrow readers don't get slower.

Pagination, `Link` and `X-Total-Count` are unchanged. The reload goes through the authorized, filtered relation, so an event that moves to a board the reader can't see between the two queries stays hidden. That can leave a page one row short, which is the same race offset pagination already has between pages and between the page query and the count.

The sort stays: the id query still sorts every visible entry, about 1.3µs each. If the alert continues, the next step is the account index from the card, with a guard for narrow readers, plus a change to the count.

No new third parties or personal data.

title: Harden webhook delivery against non-HTTP hosts
body:
An account created webhooks pointing at SMTP and SSH ports on public hosts. Surfguard already refused private addresses, so nothing internal was reached, but two gaps showed up:

- **No port check.** A webhook could target any port, so an account could scan ports and send its payload to non-HTTP services from our IPs. Webhook URLs now allow only ports 80 and 443. The check runs when a URL is set, so webhooks already saved with other ports can still be deactivated, and again at delivery, where those webhooks record a `forbidden_port` failure without connecting.
- **Non-HTTP replies failed the job.** A banner reply raised `EOFError` or `Net::HTTPBadResponse`, which `perform_request` didn't rescue, so the job failed and the delinquency tracker never counted the attempt. These, `Net::HTTPHeaderSyntaxError`, and the `ArgumentError` Net::HTTP raises for a header value with a bare CR now record `invalid_response`. The `ArgumentError` rescue covers only the request, so an error building the payload still fails the job. `Errno::EPIPE` during the TLS handshake now records `destination_unreachable`. Deliveries send `Accept-Encoding: identity`, so a bogus gzip body can't raise `Zlib::DataError`.

The new tests fail without the app changes and pass with them. Webhook model tests, the full OSS suite, Rubocop and Brakeman pass locally. Codex reviewed it until it had no more findings.

title: Bump solid_queue from 1.7.0 to 1.7.2
body:
Bumps [solid_queue](https://github.com/rails/solid_queue) from 1.7.0 to 1.7.2.
Release notes

Sourced from solid_queue's releases.

v1.7.2

Summary

Concurrency-limited jobs now give their slot back only to the semaphore they got it from. That fixes a job that ran past its duration letting an extra job run alongside the next holder (#827). It also fixes jobs whose class goes missing during a deploy giving back a slot they never took, or keeping one they did take. Nothing needs migrating; see "Upgrading to version 1.7.2" for what to do before 2.0.

What's Changed

  • Give concurrency slots back only to the semaphore they came from by @​rosa in rails/solid_queue#831

Full Changelog: https://github.com/rails/solid_queue/compare/v1.7.1...v1.7.2

v1.7.1

Summary of changes

Process resilience

  • Processes stop and get replaced when their heartbeats keep failing past the alive threshold (#778).
  • The async supervisor replaces dead threads even if releasing their jobs fails during a database outage (#791, fixes #823).
  • Workers stop when finishing a job fails (#768).
  • Forked processes exit immediately, which avoids the exit hang on SQLite (#801).
  • The Puma plugin keeps shutting down when its output pipe is gone (#800, #737).
  • In async mode, in-flight jobs go back to the queue when shutdown times out (#815).

Jobs and concurrency

  • Jobs whose class no longer loads are failed with ClassMissingError instead of being dropped (#783).
  • Discarding ready jobs in bulk unblocks the jobs waiting behind them (#818).
  • Retrying failed jobs in bulk resets their retry counters (#817).
  • Concurrency locks are taken in key order when dispatching several jobs, which avoids deadlocks (#812).
  • One less query per enqueue (#819).
  • On MySQL, failed jobs with very large error messages no longer crash workers (#822).
  • Bulk-discarding claimed executions raises UndiscardableError instead of NameError (#828).
  • Batch completion errors no longer block the next job (#816).

Queues and recurring tasks

  • Queue prefixes escape _ and %, and each queue is selected only once (#811).
  • Dynamic tasks recreated with the same key are rescheduled (#793).

Other

  • The CLI is no longer eager loaded (#826).
  • CI pins json below 3 for Rails 7.1 and 8.0 (#813). That's test-only, but it explains the Gemfile change.
  • README additions: READ COMMITTED for MySQL, sql_notifications, the Puma plugin's behavior, retry_on and process death, async mode with TERM and QUIT, and removing leftover recurring tasks.

What's Changed

  • Replace terminated threads even if releasing their claimed jobs fails by @​rosa in rails/solid_queue#791
  • Stop processes whose heartbeats keep failing past the alive threshold by @​wintan1418 in rails/solid_queue#778
  • Stop workers when job finalization fails by @​rafael-pissardo in rails/solid_queue#768
  • Add README notes on READ COMMITTED, sql_notifications, and the Puma plugin's failure behaviour by @​rosa in rails/solid_queue#795
  • Assert the successful job's output regardless of execution order by @​rosa in rails/solid_queue#796
  • Document that retry_on can't intercept process-death errors by @​wintan1418 in rails/solid_queue#789
  • Harden the lifecycle and pool-size worker tests against slow databases by @​rosa in rails/solid_queue#798
  • Exit forked processes immediately to avoid a SQLite mutex deadlock at exit by @​rosa in rails/solid_queue#801

title: Experiment: run some system tests without a browser (rails-jsdom)
body:
This is an experiment, and I am not sure that you want it. Please close it if it does not fit the project. I wrote [rails-jsdom](https://github.com/jakehow/rails-jsdom), and I used Fizzy to find out where it works and where it does not. Fizzy found many gaps, and fixing them made the gem much better, so thank you for publishing the app. rails-jsdom runs tests that use the system test methods (`visit`, `click_on`, `fill_in`, `assert_selector`) without Chrome or a test server. Rails renders the pages, and the real Stimulus controllers, Turbo and Action Cable run in jsdom, in the test process. ## Highlights - 18 of the 47 system tests run as interaction tests: the back link, card refresh and markdown paste tests, the 2 Mermaid editor tests and 5 smoke tests. - Those 18 tests took 21.5s as system tests and 9.6s as interaction tests, in one process on one machine (2.2x faster). Your system tests are already fast, so the gain is small. I measured only on my machine. - 29 tests stay system tests, because they need things jsdom does not do: Mermaid diagrams (canvas), scroll positions, pagination that loads on scroll, computed colours, the OAuth consent redirect (Content Security Policy) and drag and drop. I did not try `board_keyboard_focus_test.rb`. - The 2 back link tests that start on the activity page set the clock to the card's latest fixture event. Without this, they fail between midnight and 1 a.m., because jsdom does not load the previous day when the "Load more…" link scrolls into view. ## Open points - To fulfill the automated review's requests, I added these after opening the PR: - The test workflow sets up Node from a new `.node-version` (26) and runs `npm ci`. rails-jsdom needs Node 22.22.2+, 24.15+ or 26. - `bin/setup` runs `npm ci`, mise installs Node from `.node-version`, and `docs/development.md` says so. - `Gemfile.saas.lock` now locks rails-jsdom, so the drift check passes. The workflow steps are yours to change or drop if you would rather set up Node another way. - The PR adds a gem, two npm packages (jsdom and esbuild) and a new kind of test to maintain. With a 2.2x gain on 18 tests, that may not be worth it to you, and I understand. The full report, with how I measured and why each remaining system test stays, is [here](https://github.com/jakehow/rails-jsdom/blob/v0.2.0/docs/reference_apps.md).

Confidence Score: 4/5

Update the SaaS lockfile before merging so the existing pull request checks can pass.

Findings

1.  **SaaS lockfile is out of sync** ▶ 2.  **Local setup omits Node dependencies** ▶
Fix with agent prompt `````markdown ### Issue 1 Gemfile:72 `rails-jsdom` was added to `Gemfile.lock` but is missing from `Gemfile.saas.lock`, even though `Gemfile.saas` loads `Gemfile`. The `Gemfile drift` job runs `bin/bundle-drift check`, which reports the missing gem and exits with an error. Update and commit `Gemfile.saas.lock` too. ### Issue 2 package.json:3-5 The new interaction tests need Node and these packages, but the local setup path has no install instructions for them. `docs/development.md` still directs contributors to run `bin/setup` followed by `bin/rails test`, while `bin/setup` never runs `npm ci`. Add the supported Node versions and package installation steps to the development guide or local setup script so contributors can run the migrated tests. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time! --- For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly. `````

Summary

 Moves 18 browser tests to `RailsJsdom::TestCase` and adds `rails-jsdom`, `jsdom`, and `esbuild`. - Selected interaction tests now run without Chrome. Acknowledged by jakehow: CI does not install Node or run `npm ci`; workflow changes were deliberately left to maintainers. That known gap is not reported again. title: Drop the runner's MySQL server before installing system packages
body:
The test jobs' "Install system packages" step now fails on every PR: installing `libmysqlclient-dev` upgrades the MySQL server the runner image ships to 8.4.13, and that package's postinst exits 1, so apt exits 100 before the tests run (seen on #3313, a one-line config change).

The tests never use that server; MySQL jobs talk to the `mysql` service container. This purges `mysql-server` and `mysql-server-core` before the install, leaving the client libraries and CLI in place.

title: Drop board routes that have no controller
body:
Two route declarations point at controllers that don't exist, and Rails warns about them on every boot: ``` GET /boards/:board_id/subscriptions(.:format) references a missing controller: uninitialized constant Boards::SubscriptionsController GET /prompts/boards(.:format) references a missing controller: uninitialized constant Prompts::BoardsController ``` - `resource :subscriptions` in the boards scope has no `Boards::SubscriptionsController`, and nothing links to it. This PR removes it. - The prompts namespace draws `resources :boards` only to nest `users` under it, so it also draws the seven board routes, which have no `Prompts::BoardsController`. This PR draws it with `only: []`, as `columns/cards` already does since #3072. `prompts_board_users_path`, which `RichTextHelper` uses, is unchanged. A new route test fails when any route names a controller that doesn't exist. On `main` it fails with `["boards/subscriptions", "prompts/boards"]`, and with this change it passes. Local OSS suite: 2707 tests, 0 failures. I couldn't run SaaS mode because it needs private gems. The SaaS routes are drawn in the engine's own route set, so the new test doesn't see them. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge.

title: Register read and write for a dynamic registration that names no scope
body:
A client metadata document that names no scope is provisioned with `read write` ([document.rb](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/09c479e71e67b668c3c6633988163e3ad0b6788f/app/models/oauth/client_metadata/document.rb#L14-L16)), so the consent screen offers both levels and the person picks. Dynamic registration gave the same client `read` alone, through `Oauth.canonical_scope("")`.

The hosted MCP server's 401 challenge names `scope="read write"`. A client that registered with no scope and then authorized with that scope was refused `invalid_scope` (`validate_scope` → `Client#allows_scope?`), before the person saw the consent screen.

- `Oauth::ClientsController#validated_scopes`: a registration that names no scope, counting `offline_access` as none (as `Oauth.requested_scopes` already does), registers `read write`, the same default as a metadata document.
- A registration that names only scopes Fizzy doesn't issue still registers `read`, as before.
- Tests: an unscoped registration (absent, blank, `offline_access` only, empty list) registers `read write` and its consent screen offers both levels with `read write` preselected; the first fails on `main` with `Expected: "read write" Actual: "read"`. A second pins the unknown-scopes case.

Clients already registered with no scope keep `read`. They can't be told apart from clients that asked for `read`, so they aren't widened. One refused this way never reached consent, so the unauthorized-registration sweep removes it within a day, and the client registers again.

title: Load the OAuth consent screen in full so Authorize can redirect to the app
body:
If you're signed out when an app (Cursor, for example) starts connecting to Fizzy's MCP server, clicking **Authorize** on the consent screen does nothing in Chrome. The console shows a `form-action 'self'` CSP violation for the redirect to the app's callback.

## Cause

The consent controller already adds the validated redirect origin to `form-action`, but only that page's response carries it. When you sign in mid-flow, the code form submits through Turbo. Turbo follows the redirect back to `/oauth/authorization/new` and swaps in the body, so the document keeps the sign-in page's policy (`form-action 'self'`). The Authorize POST is allowed, and the browser then blocks its 302 to the app.

Anyone already signed in loads the consent screen with a full page load, which is why the existing system test passed.

## Fix

The consent screen now emits `turbo_page_requires_reload`, so Turbo always loads it in full and its own CSP applies.

For people who sign in mid-flow, the consent action runs twice (once as Turbo's fetch, once as the full load), so `consent.shown` is recorded twice and an unstored client-metadata document is fetched twice (3 of the resolver's 6 per URL per minute).

## Tests

- New system test: start signed out, sign in with the emailed code, click Authorize, and land on the callback. It fails on `main` (stays on the consent screen) and passes with the fix.
- `test/integration/oauth_*` all pass.

title: Log Cloudflare's visitor location as client.geo
body:
## What

- Each request's structured log line now carries `client.geo`: country, region, city and `location` (lat, lon), read from Cloudflare's `CF-IPCountry`, `CF-Region-Code`, `CF-IPCity`, `CF-IPLatitude` and `CF-IPLongitude` headers.
- These are the same `client.geo` fields Basecamp logs, so log queries work the same across both apps.
- SaaS engine only, since `logger.struct` comes from `rails_structured_logging` in `Gemfile.saas`. Empty values and non-numeric or out-of-range coordinates are left out, and city names keep their accents.

## Why

Ops can't filter or group Fizzy requests by place in the logs today: Fizzy production has no `client_geo_*` fields, while Basecamp has them on every line. Unlike Basecamp, nothing goes into `Current`, because nothing else reads it.

## Personal data

This adds the visitor's region, city and IP-derived coordinates (Cloudflare's city-level estimate, not a device location) to the request logs. The client IP is already logged. No new third party: Cloudflare already fronts Fizzy. Trust & Compliance has been notified.

Region, city and coordinates only arrive once Cloudflare's visitor location headers are turned on for the production app zone (a separate change on our side). Until then, production logs only the country.

## Testing

- `bin/rails test saas/test` (SaaS mode, MySQL 8.4): 285 tests, 0 failures, including the 5 new ones in `saas/test/integration/client_geo_logging_test.rb`.
- `bin/rubocop saas`: no offenses.
- Production logs: Fizzy has 0 lines with `client_geo_*` over the last hour, Basecamp has them on every request.

---

title: Allow full-mark GC during request handling
body:
## Motivation

`config/puma.rb` turns off full-mark GC in each worker and relies on the `out_of_band` hook to run the deferred major GC between requests:

    before_worker_boot do
      GC.config(rgengc_allow_full_mark: false)
    end

https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/da4fb423d831963d94d6873dee61aa85a9e78259/config/puma.rb#L42-L46

Puma runs `out_of_band` only when a worker is idle, so a worker with queued requests runs no full mark until its queue empties. Between hook runs, CRuby skips the full mark it would otherwise do ([`default.c` L8949-L8952](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/caf4f279d15bac633083cba3fd53c8ed62162032/gc/default/default.c#L8949-L8952)) and stops aging objects ([L6338-L6339](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/caf4f279d15bac633083cba3fd53c8ed62162032/gc/default/default.c#L6338-L6339)). `GC.start` turns full marks on for its own run ([L10345-L10346](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/caf4f279d15bac633083cba3fd53c8ed62162032/gc/default/default.c#L10345-L10346)) and restores the setting when it returns ([L10384](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/caf4f279d15bac633083cba3fd53c8ed62162032/gc/default/default.c#L10384)).

In another of our apps, this setting caused steady growth in old objects and memory.

## Details

Remove the `before_worker_boot` block that calls `GC.config(rgengc_allow_full_mark: false)`, so CRuby runs a full mark whenever its heuristics call for one. Keep `Process.warmup` and the `out_of_band` hook, which still runs `GC.start` when `GC.latest_gc_info(:need_major_by)` is set. Reword its comment, which described the deferral.

## Additional information

I added this block in basecamp/fizzy@257aeb8511414c6cb737f873fda5b9ec34228d84.

Updates `webmock` from 3.26.4 to 3.34.0
Release notes

Sourced from webmock's releases.

3.34.0

  • Allow with(query: :any) to match any query string (#1099)

    stub_request(:get, "www.example.com").with(query: :any) matches requests with any query string, or none. RSpec's anything works the same way. Previously, this raised NoMethodError, and you had to write with(query: hash_including({})).

    Use a URL without query parameters when passing query: :any. Otherwise, WebMock raises ArgumentError.

    Thanks to nightpool

  • Raise a clear ArgumentError for an unsupported query option

    Previously, a value such as with(query: :all) raised NoMethodError (undefined method split). The new error lists the supported values.

  • Show anything for keys given without a value to hash_including or hash_excluding outside RSpec

    Previously, with Minitest or Test::Unit, messages showed #<WebMock::Matchers::AnyArgMatcher:0x...>, for example for with(query: hash_including(:a)). RSpec's own matchers already showed anything.

  • Provide HTTP_HOST to to_rack apps when the client has not supplied a Host header (#1084)

    Previously, requests from some HTTP clients reached the Rack app without HTTP_HOST. This caused host checks such as Sinatra's HostAuthorization to see an empty host.

    WebMock now fills in the host from the request URL, including the port when it is not the default. An explicit Host header is preserved.

    Thanks to Benoit Tigeot

  • Fix Rack compatibility for to_rack apps

    The request environment now passes Rack::Lint.

    SERVER_PORT and CONTENT_LENGTH are now strings. If your app or tests read them directly, use string comparisons, such as env['SERVER_PORT'] == "80". The environment also includes SERVER_PROTOCOL.

    CONTENT_TYPE is omitted when the request has no content type. The Content-Length header is passed only as CONTENT_LENGTH, without an extra HTTP_CONTENT_LENGTH entry. Transfer-Encoding is removed because the body has already been decoded.

    Repeated header values are joined into one string. Header values and the body read from rack.input now use binary (ASCII-8BIT) strings.

3.33.0

  • Return effective_url as a String for stubbed Typhoeus responses (#869)

    Previously, this was an Addressable::URI. If your code calls methods such as effective_url.host, parse the returned string into a URI first.

    The URL keeps the request's port, query order and encoding. It follows curl's formatting: for example, http://example.com:80 becomes http://example.com:80/. Stubbed timeouts now provide an effective_url too.

    Thanks to Tom Brammar

  • Fix incorrect removal of default ports from displayed URLs

    WebMock could accidentally remove :80 or :443 from a URL's path or query. For example, an error message could show /foo/bar instead of /foo:80/bar.

    Only the host's default port is now removed. This also works when the port is immediately followed by a query string, as in http://example.com:80?a=b.

... (truncated)

title: Bump httpx, puma and net-ssh for security advisories
body:
## Summary

Upgrade httpx from 1.7.1 to 1.9.1 in `Gemfile.saas.lock`, and puma from 8.0.3 to 8.0.4 and net-ssh from 7.3.8 to 7.3.10 in both lockfiles, to clear their advisories. `bin/bundler-audit` now passes on both lockfiles.

### httpx

The httpx bump clears [GHSA-jgqw-w3x2-9h6q](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jgqw-w3x2-9h6q). With `Oj` loaded and `MultiJson` absent, httpx 1.7.1's `HTTPX::Response#json` decoded with Oj's default `:object` mode, which can build arbitrary Ruby objects. Fizzy was not exposed: the bundle has no `oj`, and `action_push_native` 0.3.1, the only httpx consumer, never calls `Response#json`.

http-2 moves from 1.1.1 to 1.3.0, because httpx 1.9.1 requires `http-2 >= 1.2.0`. Only `Gemfile.saas.lock` changes; `Gemfile.lock` has neither gem.

Of 575 upstream commits (467 httpx, 108 http-2), recon skipped 295. Of the 280 analyzed against Fizzy, 220 have no impact and 60 matched code Fizzy reaches; none of the 60 needs a code change in Fizzy. 0 mitigations applied, 1 transitive dependency analyzed.

### puma

puma 8.0.4 fixes [GHSA-4v6q-hvv7-49h9](https://github.com/puma/puma/security/advisories/GHSA-4v6q-hvv7-49h9), memory exhaustion over SSL connections, and [GHSA-rhww-p99c-hgj9](https://github.com/puma/puma/security/advisories/GHSA-rhww-p99c-hgj9), a JRuby header parsing bug. Fizzy was not exposed to either: its Docker images run puma on CRuby behind Thruster, and puma listens for plain HTTP. The puma plan found nothing in the range that needs a change in Fizzy.

### net-ssh

net-ssh 7.3.10 fixes [GHSA-hjwv-j52r-xcg7](https://github.com/net-ssh/net-ssh/security/advisories/GHSA-hjwv-j52r-xcg7), which accepted host keys that `known_hosts` marks `@revoked`, and [GHSA-qcf4-j55x-72hv](https://github.com/net-ssh/net-ssh/security/advisories/GHSA-qcf4-j55x-72hv), where `Net::SSH::Proxy::HTTPS` skipped TLS certificate verification by default. Fizzy uses net-ssh through Kamal tooling; Rails boot does not load it. The net-ssh plan found nothing in the range that needs a change in Fizzy. Kamal never uses `Net::SSH::Proxy::HTTPS`, and on Kamal's path sshkit parses `known_hosts` itself, so the `@revoked` fix does not change deploys.

## Upgrade Plan

- [httpx 1.7.1..1.9.1 for fizzy](https://github.com/basecamp/37signals-hq/blob/9a7a27bdd11f2dc4b4d86344c46fa2775f2b8c4f/upgrade-analysis/fizzy-20261121-httpx_1.7.1..1.9.1.md)
- [http-2 1.1.1..1.3.0 for fizzy](https://github.com/basecamp/37signals-hq/blob/9a7a27bdd11f2dc4b4d86344c46fa2775f2b8c4f/upgrade-analysis/fizzy-20261121-http-2_1.1.1..1.3.0.md)
- [puma v8.0.3..v8.0.4 for fizzy](https://github.com/basecamp/37signals-hq/blob/af50e4c2055f9c7d0782a63e09a3f72fcb51aa66/upgrade-analysis/fizzy-20261122-puma_v8.0.3..v8.0.4.md)
- [net-ssh v7.3.8..v7.3.10 for fizzy](https://github.com/basecamp/37signals-hq/blob/c42e7094956a4556d9062a5b7a2f2907074d7a8d/upgrade-analysis/fizzy-20261123-net-ssh_v7.3.8..v7.3.10.md)

httpx risks to watch after deploy:

- **Unbounded GOAWAY retries.** If APNs or FCM closes every new HTTP/2 connection with GOAWAY before accepting a request stream, httpx 1.9.1 can resend the pending push indefinitely. The per-attempt `request_timeout` does not cap the loop. The HTTP/2 connection requeues unprocessed requests on a recoverable GOAWAY, and since 1.8.2 [`0a146d05`](https://gitlab.com/os85/httpx/-/commit/0a146d05) lets `:persistent` retry a `GoawayError` without decrementing the retry counter. The fix for [httpx#393](https://gitlab.com/os85/httpx/-/work_items/393), [`bc285052`](https://gitlab.com/os85/httpx/-/commit/bc285052bf0eebcd560e857aba3010b5a9bd9082), treats a GOAWAY with last stream id `0` as unrecoverable, so its retries count against the retry limit. It is on httpx `master` and in no release yet. Watch for push jobs that never finish.
- **Timeouts.** `action_push_native` sets only `request_timeout` (APNs 30 s, FCM 15 s). In httpx 1.9.1 that timeout runs per attempt from TCP and TLS setup, and the default connect, settings, read and write timeouts no longer apply.
- **Ping timeout.** httpx 1.8.0 added a 2 s `ping_timeout` on reused connections. When a liveness probe times out, `:persistent` can reconnect and resend the pending push without decrementing the retry counter. Watch push latency as well as `ActionPushNative::TimeoutError` rates.

## Changes

- `bundle update --conservative httpx` against `Gemfile.saas`.
- `bin/bundle-drift forward` restored the `mini_portile2 (2.8.9)` spec that the httpx update pruned, so `bin/bundle-drift check` passes.
- I edited the version and checksum of puma and of net-ssh by hand in both lockfiles, because `bundle update --conservative --patch` for either gem also pruned the ruby-platform `nokogiri`, `sqlite3` and `mini_portile2` specs from `Gemfile.lock`.

The lockfile diffs hold only httpx, http-2, puma and net-ssh.

CI's gem audit step reads only `Gemfile.lock` ([`config/ci.rb` line 22](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/67305bee55469942a91ffd6c662186ad977dbcb0/config/ci.rb#L22)), so CI never reported the httpx advisory. I ran `bin/bundler-audit check --gemfile-lock Gemfile.saas.lock` locally; it passes. I left CI unchanged.

title: Embed an upload by its attachable_sgid, not its signed_id
body:
The API's rich text guide (`docs/api/sections/rich_text.md`) says to put a direct upload's `signed_id` in an `<action-text-attachment sgid>`. Fizzy accepts that with a 201, but the attachment renders as a broken placeholder and `has_attachments` stays false. Only the upload's `attachable_sgid` works, and the direct upload response includes it alongside `signed_id` (Action Text adds it to every attachable's JSON). The fizzy CLI already embeds `attachable_sgid` (`internal/commands/inline_attachments.go`).

I checked this against a local run of `main` (60c5be7a9), on card descriptions and comment bodies, with an image and with a text file:
- `sgid` set to the `attachable_sgid` renders the figure or file block. A `caption` attribute survives sanitization and is shown in place of the filename.
- `sgid` set to the `signed_id` gives the broken placeholder.
- A card's `image` takes the `signed_id`; the `attachable_sgid` there is a 500.
- A blob already embedded in rich text is refused as a card image with a 422 (`active_storage_no_reuse.rb`).

Docs only. I found this while adding file attachments to Fizzy's MCP server.
